Relational Data Base Management Systems (RDBMS) are database management systems 
that maintain data records and indices in tables. Relationships may be created and 
maintained across and among the data and tables. In a relational database, relationships 
between data items are expressed by means of tables. Interdependencies among these 
tables are expressed by data values rather than by pointers. This allows a high degree of 
data independence. An RDBMS has the capability to recombine the data items from 
different files, providing powerful tools for data usage.
What are the properties of the Relational tables?
Relational tables have six properties:
Column values are of the same kind.
The sequence of columns is insignificant.
The sequence of rows is insignificant.

A network is a set of devices connected by physical media links. A network is 
recursively is a connection of two or more nodes by a physical link or two or more networks 
connected by one or more nodes.

At the lowest level, a network can consist of two or more computers directly connected 
by some physical medium such as coaxial cable or optical fiber. Such a physical medium is called as 
Link.

A network can consist of two or more computers directly connected by some physical medium 
such as coaxial cable or optical fiber. Such a physical medium is called as Links and the computer it 
connects is called as Nodes.
What is a gateway or Router?

A node that is connected to two or more networks is commonly called as router or Gateway. It
generally forwards message from one network to another.

questions.question: Look at this series: 2, 1, (1/2), (1/4), ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation:
This is a simple division series; each number is one-half of the previous number.In other terms to say, the number is divided by 2 successively to get the next result.4/2 = 2
2/2 = 1
1/2 = 1/2
(1/2)/2 = 1/4
(1/4)/2 = 1/8 and so on.

questions.question: Look at this series: 7, 10, 8, 11, 9, 12, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is a simple alternating addition and subtraction series. In the first pattern, 3 is added; in the second, 2 is subtracted.

questions.question: Look at this series: 36, 34, 30, 28, 24, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: This is an alternating number subtraction series. First, 2 is subtracted, then 4, then 2, and so on.

questions.question: Look at this series: 22, 21, 23, 22, 24, 23, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: In this simple alternating subtraction and addition series; 1 is subtracted, then 2 is added, and so on.

questions.question: Look at this series: 53, 53, 40, 40, 27, 27, ... What number should come next?
questions.explanation: In this series, each number is repeated, then 13 is subtracted to arrive at the next number.

questions.question: SCD, TEF, UGH, ____, WKL
questions.explanation: There are two alphabetical series here. The first series is with the first letters only: STUVW. The second series involves the remaining letters: CD, EF, GH, IJ, KL.

questions.question: B2CD, _____, BCD4, B5CD, BC6D
questions.explanation: Because the letters are the same, concentrate on the number series, which is a simple 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 series, and follows each letter in order.

questions.question: FAG, GAF, HAI, IAH, ____
questions.explanation: The middle letters are static, so concentrate on the first and third letters. The series involves an alphabetical order with a reversal of the letters. The first letters are in alphabetical order: F, G, H, I , J. The second and fourth segments are reversals of the first and third segments. The missing segment begins with a new letter.

questions.question: ELFA, GLHA, ILJA, _____, MLNA
questions.explanation: The second and forth letters in the series, L and A, are static. The first and third letters consist of an alphabetical order beginning with the letter E.

questions.question: CMM, EOO, GQQ, _____, KUU
questions.explanation: The first letters are in alphabetical order with a letter skipped in between each segment: C, E, G, I, K. The second and third letters are repeated; they are also in order with a skipped letter: M, O, Q, S, U.

options.A: The ski instructors at Top of the Peak Ski School work from December through March.
options.B: Matthew prefers jobs that allow him to work outdoors.
options.C: Lucinda makes an appointment with the beach resort restaurant manager to interview for the summer waitressing position that was advertised in the newspaper.
options.D: oug's ice cream shop stays open until 11 p.m. during the summer months.

questions.explanation: Although the ski instructors at Top of the Peak Ski School do work seasonally, choice a does not describe anyone  applying for seasonal employment. In choice b, the statement that Matthew likes to work outdoors tells us nothing about seasonal employment or someone applying for it. And although choice d describes a business with seasonal hours, it does not describe a person applying for seasonal work. Choice c, on the other hand, very specifically depicts a person, Lucinda, who is applying for a job as a summer waitress at a beach resort, which is dependent upon a particular season of the year.

questions.question: Violating an Apartment Leaseoccurs when a tenant does something prohibited by the legally binding document that he or she has signed with a landlord. Which situation below is the best example of Violating an Apartment Lease?

options.A: Tim has decided to move to another city, so he calls his landlord to tell him that he is not interested in renewing his lease when it expires next month.
options.B: Valerie recently lost her job and, for the last three months, has neglected to pay her landlord the monthly rent they agreed upon in writing when she moved into her apartment eight months ago.
options.C: Mark writes a letter to his landlord that lists numerous complaints about the apartment he has agreed to rent for two years.
options.D: Leslie thinks that her landlord is neglecting the building in which she rents an apartment. She calls her attorney to ask for advice.

questions.explanation: Valerie signed a legally binding document that requires her to pay a monthly rent for her apartment and she has failed to do this for the last three months. Therefore, she has violated her apartment lease.

questions.question: AnInformal Gatheringoccurs when a group of people get together in a casual, relaxed manner. Which situation below is the best example of an Informal Gathering?

options.A: The book club meets on the first Thursday evening of every month.
options.B: fter finding out about his promotion, Jeremy and a few coworkers decide to go out for a quick drink after work.
options.C: Mary sends out 25 invitations for the bridal shower she is giving for her sister.
options.D: Whenever she eats at the Mexican restaurant, Clara seems to run into Peter.

questions.explanation: After getting some good news, Jeremy and a few friends casually get together for a drink after work, thereby having an informal gathering. Choices a and c describe more formal types of gatherings. Choice d describes a chance or coincidental kind of meeting.

questions.question: Peoplespeculatewhen they consider a situation and assume something to be true based on inconclusive evidence. Which situation below is the best example of Speculation ?

options.A: Francine decides that it would be appropriate to wear jeans to her new office on Friday after reading about "Casual Fridays" in her employee handbook.
options.B: Mary spends thirty minutes sitting in traffic and wishes that she took the train instead of driving.
options.C: fter consulting several guidebooks and her travel agent, Jennifer feels confident that the hotel she has chosen is first-rate.
options.D: When Emily opens the door in tears, Theo guesses that she's had a death in her family.

questions.explanation: This is the only situation in which someone makes an assumption that is not based on conclusive evidence. Choices a and c reflect situations in which assumptions are made based on evidence. In choice b, Mary is not assuming anything to be true. She is simply wishing that she'd made a different decision.

questions.question: Posthumous Publicationoccurs when a book is published after the author's death. Which situation below is the best example of Posthumous Publication ?

options.A: Richard's illness took his life before he was able to enjoy the amazing early reviews of his novel.
options.B: Melissa's publisher cancels her book contract after she fails to deliver the manuscript on time.
options.C: larence never thought he'd live to see the third book in his trilogy published.
options.D: Elizabeth is honored with a prestigious literary award for her writing career and her daughter accepts the award on behalf of her deceased mother.

questions.explanation: Although choice d also mentions a writer who has died, it does not state that one of the writer's books was published after her death, only that she received an award. Choice  a states that Richard wasn't around  to see the early reviews of his novel, therefore implying that Richard died before the book was published. The other two options depict living writers.

questions.question: Eileen is planning a special birthday dinner for her husband's 35th birthday. She wants the evening to be memorable, but her husband is a simple man who would rather be in jeans at a baseball game than in a suit at a fancy restaurant. Which restaurant below should Eileen choose?

options.A: lfredo's offers fine Italian cuisine and an elegant Tuscan decor. Patrons will feel as though they've spent the evening in a luxurious Italian villa.
options.B: Pancho's Mexican Buffet is an all-you-can-eat family style smorgasbord with the best tacos in town.
options.C: The Parisian Bistro is a four-star French restaurant where guests are treated like royalty. Chef Dilbert Olay is famous for his beef bourguignon.
options.D: Marty's serves delicious, hearty meals in a charming setting reminiscent of a baseball clubhouse in honor of the owner,Marty Lester, a former major league baseball all-star.

questions.explanation: Since Eileen's husband does not enjoy fancy restaurants, choices a and c can be ruled out. Choice b, although casual, doesn't sound as though it would be the kind of special and memorable evening that Eileen is looking for. Choice d, which is owned by a former baseball star  and is described as "charming" and "reminiscent of a baseball clubhouse", sounds perfect for Eileen's husband, who is described as a baseball fan and a man with simple tastes.

questions.question: The film director wants an actress for the lead role of Lucy who perfectly fits the description that appears in the original screenplay. He is not willing to consider actresses who do not resemble the character as she is described in the screenplay, no matter how talented they are. The screenplay describes Lucy as an average-sized, forty  something redhead, with deep brown eyes, very fair skin, and a brilliant smile. The casting agent has four actresses in mind.Actress #1is a stunning red-haired beauty who is 5'9" and in her mid-twenties. Her eyes are brown and she has an olive complexion.Actress #2has red hair, big brown eyes, and a fair complexion. She is in her mid-forties and is 5'5".Actress #3is 5'4" and of medium build. She has red hair, brown eyes, and is in her early forties.Actress #4is a blue-eyed redhead in her early thirties. She's of very slight build and stands at 5'.
questions.explanation: Actresses #2 and #3 possess most of the required traits. They both have red hair and brown eyes, are average-sized, and are in their forties. Actress #1 is very tall and is only in her mid-twenties. She also has an olive complexion. Actress #4 is of very slight build and is in her early thirties. She also has blue eyes.

questions.question: The school principal has received complaints from parents about bullying in the school yard during recess. He wants to investigate and end this situation as soon as possible, so he has asked the recess aides to watch closely. Which situation should the recess aides report to the principal?

options.A: girl is sitting glumly on a bench reading a book and not interacting with her peers.
options.B: Four girls are surrounding another girl and seem to have possession of her backpack.
options.C: Two boys are playing a one-on-one game of basketball and are arguing over the last basket scored.
options.D: Three boys are huddled over a handheld video game, which isn't supposed to be on school grounds.

questions.explanation: Seeing four girls surrounding another girl, while in possession of her backpack, is the most suspicious of the incidents described.

questions.question: Mrs. Carson took a taxi to meet her three friends for lunch. They were waiting for her outside the restaurant when she pulled up in the car. She was so excited to see her friends that she left her tote bag in the taxi. As the taxi pulled away, she and her friends took notice of the license plate number so they would be able to identify the car when they called the taxi company.#1: The four women seem to agree that the plate starts out with the letter J.#2: Three of them agree that the plate ends with 12L.#3: Three of them think that the second letter is X, and a different three think that the third letter is K.The four license plate numbers below represent what each of the four women thinks she saw. Which one is most likely the license plate number of the taxi?
questions.explanation: The four women seem to agree that the plate starts out with the letter J. Three of them agree that the plate ends with 12L. Three of them think that the second letter is X, and a different three think that the third letter is K. The plate description that has all of these common elements  is"Option A".

questions.question: Zachary has invited his three buddies over to watch the basketball game on his wide-screen television. They are all hungry, but no one wants to leave to get food. Just as they are arguing about who should make the food run, a commercial comes on for a local pizze-ria that delivers. The phone number flashes on the screen briefly and they all try to remember it. By the time Zachary grabs a pen and paper, each of them recollects a different number.#1: All of the men agree that the first three numbers are 995.#2: Three of them agree that the fourth number is 9.#3: Three agree that the fifth number is 2.#4: Three agree that the sixth number is 6; three others agree that the seventh number is also 6.Which of the numbers is most likely the telephone number of the pizzeria?
questions.explanation: All of the men agree that the first three numbers are  995. Three of them agree that the fourth number is 9. Three agree that the fifth number is 2. Three agree that the sixth number is 6; three others agree that the seventh number is also 6."Option A"is the best choice because it is made up  of the numbers that most of the men agree they saw.

questions.question: Vincent has a paper route. Each morning, he delivers 37 newspapers to customers in his neighborhood. It takes Vincent 50 minutes to deliver all the papers. If Vincent is sick or has other plans, his friend Thomas, who lives on the same street, will sometimes deliver the papers for him.

options.A: Vincent and Thomas live in the same neighborhood.
options.B: It takes Thomas more than 50 minutes to deliver the papers.
options.C: It is dark outside when Vincent begins his deliveries.
options.D: Thomas would like to have his own paper route.

questions.explanation: The fact that Vincent and Thomas live on the same street indicates that they live in the same neighborhood. There is no support for any of the other choices.

questions.question: The Pacific yew is an evergreen tree that grows in the Pacific Northwest. The Pacific yew has a fleshy, poisonous fruit. Recently, taxol, a substance found in the bark of the Pacific yew, was discovered to be a promising new anticancer drug.

options.A: Taxol is poisonous when taken by healthy people.
options.B: Taxol has cured people from various diseases.
options.C: People should not eat the fruit of the Pacific yew.
options.D: The Pacific yew was considered worthless until taxol was discovered.

questions.explanation: Given the information presented, the only statement that could be considered true is that the fruit should not be eaten because it is poisonous. There is no support that taxol is poisonous or that taxol has cured anyone (choices a and b). There is no support for choice d.

questions.question: Erin is twelve years old. For three years, she has been asking her parents for a dog. Her parents have told her that they believe a dog would not be happy in an apartment, but they have given her permission to have a bird. Erin has not yet decided what kind of bird she would like to have.

options.A: Erin's parents like birds better than they like dogs.
options.C: Erin and her parents live in an apartment.
options.D: Erin and her parents would like to move.

questions.explanation: Since Erin's parents think a dog would not be happy in an apartment, we can reasonably conclude that the family lives in an apartment. We do not know if Erin's parents dislike dogs (choice a) or if Erin  dislikes birds (choice b).There is no support for choice d.

questions.question: Tim's commute never bothered him because there were always seats available on the train and he was able to spend his 40 minutes comfortably reading the newspaper or catching up on paperwork. Ever since the train schedule changed, the train has been extremely crowded, and by the time the doors open at his station, there isn't a seat to be found.

options.A: Tim would be better off taking the bus to work.
options.B: Tim's commute is less comfortable since the train schedule changed.
options.C: Many commuters will complain about the new train schedule.
options.D: Tim will likely look for a new job closer to home.

questions.explanation: The passage tells us that Tim's commute didn't bother  him because he was always able to sit down and comfortably read or do paperwork. Therefore, it is reasonable to assume that Tim's commute has become less comfortable since the schedule change, because it is very crowded and he can no longer find a seat. There is no information given that supports choices a, c, and d.

questions.question: When they heard news of the hurricane, Maya and Julian decided to change their vacation plans. Instead of traveling to the island beach resort, they booked a room at a fancy new spa in the mountains. Their plans were a bit more expensive, but they'd heard wonderful things about the spa and they were relieved to find availability on such short notice.

options.A: Maya and Julian take beach vacations every year.
options.C: It is usually necessary to book at least six months in advance at the spa.
options.D: Maya and Julian decided to change their vacation plans because of the hurricane.

questions.explanation: The first sentence makes this statement true. There is no support for choice a. The passage tells us that the spa vacation is more expensive than the island beach resort vacation, but that doesn't necessarily mean that the spa is overpriced; therefore, choice b cannot be supported. And even though the paragraph says that the couple was relieved to find a room on short notice, there is no information to support choice c, which says that it is usually necessary to book at the spa at least six months in advance.

questions.question: Tanya is older than Eric.Cliff is older than Tanya.Eric is older than Cliff.If the first two statements are true, the third statement is
questions.explanation: Because the first two statements are true, Eric is the  youngest of the three, so the third statement must be false.

questions.question: Blueberries cost more than strawberries.Blueberries cost less than raspberries.Raspberries cost more than strawberries and blueberries.If the first two statements are true, the third statement is
questions.explanation: Because the first two statements are true, raspberries are the most expensive of the three.

questions.question: All the trees in the park are flowering trees.Some of the trees in the park are dogwoods.All dogwoods in the park are flowering trees.If the first two statements are true, the third statement is
questions.explanation: All of the trees in the park are flowering trees, So all dogwoodsin the parkare flowering trees.

questions.question: Mara runs faster than Gail.Lily runs faster than Mara.Gail runs faster than Lily.If the first two statements are true, the third statement is
questions.explanation: We know from the first two statements that Lily runs fastest. Therefore, the third statement must be false.

questions.question: Apartments in the Riverdale Manor cost less than apartments in The Gaslight Commons.Apartments in the Livingston Gate cost more than apartments in the The Gaslight Commons.Of the three apartment buildings, the Livingston Gate costs the most.If the first two statements are true, the third statement is
questions.explanation: Since the Gaslight Commons costs more than the Riverdale Manor and the Livingston Gate costs more than the Gaslight Commons, it is true that the Livingston Gate costs the most.

questions.question: Senators from urban areas are very concerned about assuring that there will be funding for a new international airport. Senators from rural areas refuse to fund anything until money for agricultural subsidies is appropriated. If the legislature funds these two programs, on which of the following could they spend the rest of the money?

options.A: the school music program and national radio
options.C: harbor improvements and the school music program

questions.explanation: The total cost of the school music program and national radio is $1 million, the amount left after the international airport and agricultural subsidies are funded.International airport + Agricultural subsidy program$4 million + $2 million = $6 millionschool music program and national radio is $1 million.Hence, Total $7 million.

questions.question: If the legislature decides to fund the agricultural subsidy program, national radio, and the small business loan program, what two other programs could they fund?

options.B: harbor improvements and school music program
options.C: hurricane preparedness and school music program

questions.explanation: The only two programs that total 1.5 million dollars are the harbor improvements and school music program.

questions.question: If the legislature decides to fund the agricultural subsidy program, national radio, and the small business loan program, the only other single program that can be funded is
questions.explanation: The total of the three programs (2 million + 0.5 million + 3 million) is 5.5 million. That leaves 1.5 million (7 million - 5.5 million), and the only single program needing that amount is the senate office building remodeling.

questions.question: One New York publisher has estimated that 50,000 to 60,000 people in the United States want an anthology that includes the complete works of William Shakespeare. And what accounts for this renewed interest in Shakespeare? As  scholars point out, his psychological insights into both male and female characters are amazing even today.This paragraph best supports the statement that

options.A: Shakespeare's characters are more interesting than fictional characters today.
options.B: people even today are interested in Shakespeare's work because of the characters.
options.C: academic scholars are putting together an anthology of Shakespeare's work.
options.D: New Yorkers have a renewed interested in the work of Shakespeare.

questions.explanation: The last sentence in the paragraph clearly gives support for the idea that the interest in Shakespeare is due to the development of his characters. Choice a is incorrect because the writer never makes this type of comparison. Choice c is wrong because even though scholars are mentioned in the paragraph, there is no indication that the scholars are compiling the anthology. Choice d is wrong because there is no support to show that most New Yorkers are interested in this work. There is no support for choice e either.

questions.question: One of the warmest winters on record has put consumers in the mood to spend money. Spending is likely to be the strongest in thirteen years. During the month of February, sales of existing single-family homes hit an annual record rate of 4.75 million.This paragraph best supports the statement that

options.A: consumer spending will be higher thirteen years from now than it is today.
options.B: more people buy houses in the month of February than in any other month.
options.C: during the winter months, the prices of single-family homes are the lowest.
options.D: there were about 4 million homes for sale during the month of February.

questions.explanation: This is clearly the best answer because the paragraph  directly states that warm weather affects consumers inclination  to spend. It furthers states that the sales of single-family homes was at an all-time high. There is no support for choice a or c. Choice b is wrong because even though there were high sales for a particular February, this does not mean that sales are not higher in other months. Choice d presents a misleading figure of 4 million. The paragraph states that the record of 4.75 million was at an annual, not a monthly, rate.

questions.question: Generation Xers are those people born roughly between 1965 and 1981. As employees, Generation Xers tend to be more challenged when they can carry out tasks independently. This makes Generation Xers the most entrepreneurial generation in history.This paragraph best supports the statement that Generation Xers

options.A: work harder than people from other generations.
options.B: have a tendency to be self-directed workers
options.C: have an interest in making history
options.D: tend to work in jobs that require risk-taking behavior.

questions.explanation: The support for choice b is given in the second sentence of the paragraph. Generation Xers like to work independently, which means they are self-directed. No support is given for either choice a or choice c. Choice d is not related to the paragraph. Although the paragraph mentions that Generation Xers like to be challenged, it does not say they like to challenge their bosses attitudes; therefore, choice  e can be ruled out.

questions.question: If you're a fitness walker, there is no need for a commute to a health club. Your neighborhood can be your health club. You don't need a lot of fancy equipment to get a good workout either. All you need is a well-designed pair of athletic shoes.This paragraph best supports the statement that

options.A: fitness walking is a better form of exercise than weight lifting.
options.B: a membership in a health club is a poor investment.
options.C: walking outdoors provides a better workout than walking indoors.
options.D: fitness walking is a convenient and valuable form of exercise.

questions.explanation: By stating that fitness walking does not require a commute to a health club, the author stresses the convenience of this form of exercise. The paragraph also states that fitness walking will result in a good workout. Choice a is incorrect because no comparison to weight lifting is made. Choice b may seem like a logical answer, but the paragraph only refers to people who are fitness walkers, so for others, a health club might be a good investment. Choice c is not in the passage. Although choice e seems logical, the paragraph does not indicate that the wrong shoes will produce major injuries.

questions.question: In the past, consumers would rarely walk into an ice cream store and order low-fat ice cream. But that isn't the case today. An increasing health consciousness combined with a much bigger selection of tasty low-fat foods in all categories has made low-fat ice cream a very profitable item for ice cream store owners.This paragraph best supports the statement that

options.A: low-fat ice cream produces more revenue than other low-fat foods.
options.B: ice cream store owners would be better off carrying only low-fat ice cream.
options.C: ice cream store owners no longer think that low-fat ice cream is an unpopular item.
options.D: low-fat ice cream is more popular than other kinds of ice cream.

questions.explanation: This choice is supported as the best answer because the paragraph indicates that low-fat ice cream was once an unpopular item, but now, because consumers are more health conscious and because there is a wider array of tasty low-fat foods, low-fat ice cream is a profitable item for ice cream store owners. There is no indication that choices a, b, d,or e are true based on the information given.

questions.question: Statement:"You are hereby appointed as a programmer with a probation period of one year and your performance will be reviewed at the end of the period for confirmation." - A line in an appointment letter.Assumptions:The performance of an individual generally is not known at the time of appointment offer.Generally an individual tries to prove his worth in the probation period.

options.C: Either I or II is implicit
options.D: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: The performance of the individual has to be tested over a span of time as the statement mentions. So, I is implicit. The statement mentions that the individual's worth shall be reviewed (during probation period) before confirmation. So, II is also implicit.

questions.question: Statement:It is desirable to put the child in school at the age of 5 or so.Assumptions:At that age the child reaches appropriate level of development and is ready to learn.The schools do not admit children after six years of age.

options.C: Either I or II is implicit
options.D: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: Since the statement talks of putting the child in school at the age of 5, it means that the child is mentally prepared for the same at this age. So, I is implicit. But nothing about admission after 6 years of age is mentioned in the statement. So, II is not implicit.

questions.question: Statement:"In order to bring punctuality in our office, we must provide conveyance allowance to our employees." - In charge of a company tells Personnel Manager.Assumptions:Conveyance allowance will not help in bringing punctuality.Discipline and reward should always go hand in hand.

options.C: Either I or II is implicit
options.D: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: Assumption I goes against the statement. So, it is not implicit. The allowance will serve as a reward to the employees and shall provoke them to come on time. So, II is implicit.

questions.question: Statement:Unemployment allowance should be given to all unemployed Indian youth above 18 years of age.Assumptions:There are unemployed youth in India who needs monetary support.The government has sufficient funds to provide allowance to all unemployed youth.

options.C: Either I or II is implicit
options.D: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: I directly follows from the statement and so is implicit. Also, the statement is a suggestion and does not tell about a government policy or its position of funds. So, II is not implicit.

questions.question: Statement:"If you trouble me, I will slap you." - A mother warns her child.Assumptions:With the warning, the child may stop troubling her.All children are basically naughty.

options.C: Either I or II is implicit
options.D: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.explanation: The mother warns her child with the expectation that he would stop troubling her. So, I is implicit. The general nature of children cannot be derived from the statement. So, II is not implicit.

questions.question: Statement:A large number of people in ward X of the city are diagnosed to be suffering from a fatal malaria type.Courses of Action:The city municipal authority should take immediate steps to carry out extensive fumigation in ward X.The people in the area should be advised to take steps to avoid mosquito bites.
questions.explanation: Clearly, prevention from mosquitoes and elimination of mosquitoes are two ways to prevent malaria. So, both the courses follow.

questions.question: Statement:Severe drought is reported to have set in several parts of the country.Courses of Action:Government should immediately make arrangement for providing financial assistance to those affected.Food, water and fodder should immediately be sent to all these areas to save the people and cattle.
questions.explanation: In the break-out of a natural calamity, the basic duty of the government becomes to provide the basic amenities essential to save the lives of people and cattle. Providing financial assistance to all would put undue burden on the country's resources. So, only II follows.

questions.question: Statement:Since its launching in 1981, Vayudoot has so far accumulated losses amounting to Rs 153 crore.Courses of Action:Vayudoot should be directed to reduce wasteful expenditure and to increase passenger fare.An amount of about Rs 300 crore should be provided to Vayudoot to make the airliner economically viable.
questions.explanation: Clearly, for better economic gain, losses should be reduced and income increased. So, only course I follows.

questions.question: Statement:Exporters in the capital are alleging that commercial banks are violating a Reserve Bank of India directive to operate a post shipment export credit denominated in foreign currency at international rates from January this year.Courses of Action:The officers concerned in the commercial banks are to be suspended.The RBI should be asked to stop giving such directives to commercial banks.
questions.explanation: The statement mentions that the commercial banks violate a directive issued by the RBI. The remedy is only to make the banks implement the Act. So, none of the courses follows.

questions.question: Statement:A large number of people die every year due to drinking polluted water during the summer.Courses of Action:The government should make adequate arrangements to provide safe drinking water to all its citizens.The people should be educated about the dangers of drinking polluted water.
questions.explanation: The situation demands creating awareness among people about the dangers of drinking polluted water so that they themselves refrain from the same, and at the same time taking steps to provide safe drinking water. So, both the courses follow.

questions.question: Statements:In a one day cricket match, the total runs made by a team were 200. Out of these 160 runs were made by spinners.Conclusions:80% of the team consists of spinners.The opening batsmen were spinners.
questions.explanation: According to the statement, 80% of the total runs were made by spinners. So, I does not follow. Nothing about the opening batsmen is mentioned in the statement. So, II also does not follow.

questions.question: Statements:The old order changed yielding place to new.Conclusions:Change is the law of nature.Discard old ideas because they are old.
questions.explanation: Clearly, I directly follows from the given statement. Also, it is mentioned that old ideas are replaced by new ones, as thinking changes with the progressing time. So, II does not follow.

questions.question: Statements:Government has spoiled many top ranking financial institutions by appointing bureaucrats as Directors of these institutions.Conclusions:Government should appoint Directors of the financial institutes taking into consideration the expertise of the person in the area of finance.The Director of the financial institute should have expertise commensurate with the financial work carried out by the institute.
questions.explanation: According to the statement, Government has spoiled financial institutions by appointing bureaucrats as Directors. This means that only those persons should be appointed as Directors who are experts in finance and are acquainted with the financial work of the institute. So, both I and II follow.

questions.question: Statements:Population increase coupled with depleting resources is going to be the scenario of many developing countries in days to come.Conclusions:The population of developing countries will not continue to increase in future.It will be very difficult for the governments of developing countries to provide its people decent quality of life.
questions.explanation: The fact given in I is quite contrary to the given statement. So, I does not follow. II mentions the direct implications of the state discussed in the statement. Thus, II follows.

questions.question: Statements:Prime age school-going children in urban India have now become avid as well as more regular viewers of television, even in households without a TV. As a result there has been an alarming decline in the extent of readership of newspapers.Conclusions:Method of increasing the readership of newspapers should be devised.A team of experts should be sent to other countries to study the impact of TV. on the readership of newspapers.
questions.explanation: The statement concentrates on the increasing viewership of TV. and does not stress either on increasing the readership of newspapers or making studies regarding the same. So, neither I nor II follows.

questions.question: The attainment of individual and organisational goals is mutually interdependent and linked by a common denominator - employee work motivation. Organisational members are motivated to satisfy their personal goals, and they contribute their efforts to the attainment of organisational objectives as means of achieving these personal goals.The passage best supports the statement that motivation -

options.A: encourages an individual to give priority to personal goals over organisational goals.
options.B: is crucial for the survival of an individual and organisation.
options.C: is the product of an individual's physical and mental energy.
options.D: is the external force which induces an individual to contribute his efforts.

questions.explanation: No answer description is available.Let's discuss.

questions.question: Due to enormous profits involved in smuggling, hundreds of persons have been attracted towards this anti-national activity. Some of them became millionaires overnight. India has a vast coastline both on the Eastern and Western Coast. It has been a heaven for smugglers who have been carrying on their activities with great impunity. There is no  doubt, that from time to time certain seizures were made by the enforcement authorities, during raids and ambush but even allowing these losses the smugglers made huge profits.The passage best supports the statement that

options.A: smuggling hampers the economic development of a nation.
options.C: authorities are taking strict measures to curb smuggling.
options.D: smuggling is fast increasing in our country owing to the quick profit it entails.

questions.explanation: No answer description is available.Let's discuss.

questions.question: Though the waste of time or the expenditure on fashions is very large, yet fashions have come to stay. They will not go, come what may. However, what is now required is that strong efforts should be made to displace the excessive craze for fashion from the minds of these youngsters.The passage best supports the statement that:

options.A: fashion is the need of the day.
options.B: the excessive craze for fashion is detrimental to one's personality.
options.C: the hoard for fashion should be done away with so as not to let down the constructive development.
options.D: work and other activities should be valued more than the outward appearance.

questions.explanation: No answer description is available.Let's discuss.

questions.question: One of the important humanitarian by-products of technology is the greater dignity and value that it imparts to human labour. Which country participated alongside India in the bilateral diving exercise IN-SLN DIVEX 2026 held?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka participated with India in the fourth edition of the bilateral diving exercise IN-SLN DIVEX 2026, conducted in Colombo. The exercise involved coordinated operations between the Indian Navy and the Sri Lankan Navy, focusing on advanced underwater diving techniques, rescue missions, and salvage operations. Activities included deep-sea dives beyond 55 metres and exploration of historical shipwrecks. The collaboration also highlighted strong defence ties, with India providing medical assistance under the Aarogya Maitri initiative. Such exercises strengthen regional maritime cooperation and enhance operational capabilities between the two neighbouring countries.

questions.question: Which regulatory body operationalised the PaRRVA framework to verify performance claims of market intermediaries in 2026?
questions.explanation: SEBI operationalised the Past Risk and Return Verification Agency (PaRRVA) framework to ensure transparency and authenticity in the performance claims made by market intermediaries. This initiative allows for the verification of data related to investment advisory, research services, and algorithmic trading. By providing standardized and validated performance metrics, it aims to protect investors from misleading advertisements and improve trust in financial markets. The framework also involves collaboration with entities like Care Ratings and NSE for data handling and verification processes, strengthening the regulatory oversight in India’s financial ecosystem.

questions.question: In which state was the SAMVAAD 2026 national cybersecurity conference organised to strengthen India's cyber audit ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Goa was chosen as the venue for the SAMVAAD 2026 national cybersecurity conference, organised by CERT-In under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The event focused on enhancing India’s cyber audit ecosystem and addressed emerging challenges in areas such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, IoT, and post-quantum cryptography. Hosted at the BITS Pilani K. K. Birla Goa Campus, it brought together over 500 delegates and featured numerous technical presentations. The conference also introduced new tools and certification programs aimed at strengthening cybersecurity practices, particularly for financial institutions and critical infrastructure sectors.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Advisor (BC Welfare & Development) by the Telangana government on April 30, 2026?
questions.explanation: V. Hanumantha Rao was appointed as the Advisor for Backwards Classes Welfare and Development by the Telangana government. This position carries the rank of a State Cabinet Minister, highlighting its significance in policymaking and governance. He is an experienced political figure who has previously served as both a Member of the Legislative Assembly and a Rajya Sabha Member of Parliament. His appointment reflects the government’s focus on strengthening welfare initiatives for backward classes. Alongside his appointment, other advisory roles were also filled, contributing to a broader administrative framework in the state.

questions.question: In which city was India’s first multilingual AI system for the Namma 112 emergency response network launched in 2026?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru is the city where India’s first multilingual AI system for the Namma 112 emergency response network was launched. Developed to enhance emergency services, the system can interpret and relay distress calls in multiple Indian and international languages without requiring manual translation. This innovation significantly improves response efficiency, especially in a linguistically diverse country. Known as the Silicon Valley of India, Bengaluru provides an ideal environment for such technological advancements due to its strong ecosystem of AI and tech development, making it a hub for pioneering digital solutions in public safety.

questions.question: In which city was the 10th National Summit on Good and Replicable Practices and Innovations in Public Health Systems inaugurated in 2026?
questions.explanation: Chandigarh served as the host city for the 10th National Summit on Good and Replicable Practices and Innovations in Public Health Systems held from April 30 to May 1, 2026. The summit focused on sharing best practices and innovations in healthcare across Indian states, featuring numerous presentations and discussions. Organised by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare along with NHSRC, the event also included the release of an important review report assessing healthcare performance in multiple states. It continues to function as a vital platform for strengthening public health initiatives nationwide.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Group Country Manager for India and South Asia by Visa on May 01, 2026?
questions.explanation: Suresh Sethi was appointed as the Group Country Manager for India and South Asia by Visa, a major global digital payments company. In this role, he is responsible for overseeing business strategy and operations across six South Asian countries, including India, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka. Based in Mumbai, he reports to the Regional President for Asia Pacific. Prior to this role, he served as Managing Director and CEO of Protean e-Gov Technologies Ltd, where he played a key role in developing Digital Public Infrastructure. His leadership experience makes him well-suited for this strategic regional position.

questions.question: Which country became the 33rd nation globally to generate electricity using nuclear energy after beginning uranium fuel loading at Unit-1 of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant in 2026?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh achieved a major milestone by entering the group of nations capable of generating electricity through nuclear energy. This development began with uranium fuel loading at Unit 1 of its first nuclear power facility, which has a total planned capacity of 2,400 MW. The project is expected to contribute significantly to meeting national electricity demand, supplying around 10–12% once fully operational. Supported by international collaboration, particularly from Russia, this initiative reflects Bangladesh’s commitment to diversifying its energy sources and strengthening long-term energy security.

questions.question: How many types of disabilities can the Prashast 2.0 app identify in school children during its screening process?
questions.explanation: 21 types of disabilities are identified by the Prashast 2.0 app, which is designed to streamline the process of recognising and supporting children with special needs in schools. The app enables early detection at the school level and connects educators with specialists to ensure appropriate interventions. This aligns with the expanded list of disabilities recognised under the RPWD Act, 2016, which increased the number from 7 to 21. By integrating with the Samagra Shiksha initiative, the app helps provide targeted educational support, ensuring inclusivity and improved learning outcomes for affected students across various regions.

questions.question: Which country announced a comprehensive roadmap to completely phase out fossil fuels by 2050 at an international conference in 2026?
questions.explanation: France announced a comprehensive roadmap to phase out fossil fuels by 2050 during an international conference focused on transitioning away from fossil fuels. The plan outlines specific deadlines for coal, oil, and natural gas phaseouts, along with consistent emission reduction targets to achieve carbon neutrality. It also emphasises the electrification of key sectors and the end of domestic fossil fuel production. Additionally, the country is known for its strong reliance on nuclear power for electricity and has Paris as its capital, further confirming its identity.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Strategic Defence Advisor by Synergy Quantum to strengthen India's cybersecurity infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Madhavan Nair, a retired Lieutenant General with extensive experience in military communications and cybersecurity, was appointed as the Strategic Defence Advisor by Synergy Quantum. He has held several key positions, including Signal Officer-in-Chief at the Indian Army Headquarters and National Cyber Security Coordinator. His expertise lies in areas such as cyber defence, signal intelligence, and post-quantum cryptography. Through this role, he is expected to contribute to strengthening India’s sovereign cybersecurity framework and advancing strategic initiatives related to national security, including proposals for specialised institutions in quantum technology and cybersecurity.

questions.question: In which city did Google lay the foundation for a ₹1.35 lakh crore Artificial Intelligence hub?
questions.explanation: Visakhapatnam has been selected as the site for a massive Artificial Intelligence hub backed by a ₹1.35 lakh crore investment. The project involves collaboration between major technology and infrastructure companies and is spread across multiple locations within the district. Designed as a large-scale data centre ecosystem, it will support advanced AI workloads and digital services. The initiative is expected to create thousands of technical jobs and contribute significantly to the region’s economic growth. It also marks a strategic shift in the city’s identity toward becoming a major technology and data hub in India.

questions.question: Which organisation signed a Licensing Agreement for Transfer of Technology (LAToT) with NSTL for the naval LM2500 Gas Turbine Infrared Suppression System in 2026?
questions.explanation: BHEL entered into a significant agreement with the Naval Science & Technological Laboratory for the transfer of technology related to the LM2500 Gas Turbine Infrared Suppression System. This system is crucial for reducing infrared signatures of naval vessels, thereby enhancing stealth and survivability in maritime operations. The agreement includes fabrication, installation, and commissioning of the system for deployment on Indian Navy ships. Developed indigenously under DRDO, this collaboration aligns with the Make in India initiative, promoting self-reliance in advanced defence technologies and strengthening India’s naval capabilities.

questions.question: Which region is set to be connected with the mainland under India’s first dedicated commercial seaplane service, approved in 2026?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep is the region targeted for connectivity under India’s first commercial seaplane service, launched by SkyHop Aviation after receiving approval from the DGCA. The project aims to connect five islands with the mainland, significantly improving accessibility to this remote archipelago. Using a modified Twin Otter aircraft, this initiative marks a milestone in domestic aviation innovation. It is further supported by government schemes like UDAN and Viability Gap Funding, ensuring affordability and sustainability. This development is expected to boost tourism, enhance local connectivity, and strengthen regional infrastructure in island territories.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Rohit Jain was appointed as the Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, bringing nearly 30 years of experience in banking supervision, financial regulation, and risk management. Prior to this role, he served as an Executive Director at the RBI, handling critical responsibilities in supervision and vulnerability assessment. His appointment reflects the government’s focus on strengthening the central bank’s leadership with experienced professionals. With strong academic qualifications and professional certifications, he is expected to play a key role in addressing emerging financial challenges and maintaining stability in India’s banking and regulatory systems.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) in 2026?
questions.explanation: Bharat Khera, a 1995-batch IAS officer from the Himachal Pradesh cadre, has been appointed as the Secretary of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. He brings over three decades of administrative experience across both central and state governments. His career includes key roles in the Ministry of Defence, Cabinet Secretariat, and Department of Consumer Affairs. With expertise in policy implementation and governance, he is expected to strengthen the MSME sector, which contributes significantly to India’s GDP. His leadership aims to enhance growth, innovation, and efficiency within this crucial segment of the economy.

questions.question: Which country successfully launched the Pakistani satellite PRSC-EO3 into orbit using a Long March-6 rocket in April 2026?
questions.explanation: China carried out the successful launch of the Pakistani satellite PRSC-EO3 using its Long March-6 carrier rocket. The launch took place from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Centre located in Shanxi Province. This mission highlights China’s growing role in international space cooperation and its advanced launch capabilities. By placing the satellite into its designated orbit, the operation supports Pakistan’s space and research objectives. Such collaborations demonstrate the strengthening of technological partnerships between nations and reflect ongoing developments in global space exploration and satellite deployment initiatives.

questions.question: What was the theme of International Labour Day 2026 as designated by the International Labour Organisation (ILO)?

options.A: Ensuring a Healthy Psychosocial Working Environment
options.B: Promoting Fair Wages for All Workers

questions.explanation: Ensuring a Healthy Psychosocial Working Environment was chosen as the theme for International Labour Day 2026 by the International Labour Organisation. This theme emphasises the importance of mental well-being, stress management, and supportive workplace conditions in modern employment settings. With evolving work environments and increasing psychological pressures, the focus extends beyond physical safety to include emotional and social health. The theme highlights the need for policies and practices that foster a balanced, inclusive, and respectful workplace, ensuring overall well-being and productivity of workers across different sectors globally.

questions.question: Which organisations collaborated to launch a biometric authentication system for card transactions in 2026?

options.B: Google Pay, ICICI Bank, and PhonePe

questions.explanation: Flipkart, Axis Bank, and PayU jointly introduced a biometric authentication system aimed at enhancing the security of digital transactions. This system replaces traditional SMS-based OTP verification with advanced methods such as fingerprint and facial recognition. The initiative addresses the rising concerns of digital fraud, which has significantly increased in recent years. By implementing device-binding protocols and secure authentication flows, the system reduces risks like SIM-swap and OTP interception. It also aligns with regulatory guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India, ensuring safer and more reliable digital payment experiences for users.

questions.question: In which city was the National Deliberative Summit on “Harmonising Administrative Data for Governance” held in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Bhubaneswar served as the venue for the National Deliberative Summit organised by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The event focused on enhancing data-driven governance by promoting interoperability and standardisation across states. Various states presented innovative approaches to data integration, while Odisha highlighted its Data Policy 2.0, aligned with national data protection laws. The summit also emphasised the importance of administrative data as an economic asset under the System of National Accounts 2025. Such initiatives are crucial for improving policymaking, ensuring transparency, and strengthening digital governance frameworks across India.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the brand ambassador for the F1 Programme in India by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited?
questions.explanation: Shreyas Iyer has been appointed as the brand ambassador for the F1 Programme in India by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited. This initiative coincides with the launch of the F1 Sim Racing India Open 2026, aimed at promoting esports talent in the country. Iyer’s selection reflects his strong appeal among youth and his reputation for leadership and performance in cricket. His involvement is expected to help bridge traditional sports with the rapidly growing esports industry. The program also seeks to create structured opportunities for aspiring racers, connecting gaming with professional motorsport and expanding India’s presence in global esports.

questions.question: On which date is International Dance Day celebrated annually to promote dance as a universal form of expression and cultural unity?
questions.explanation: International Dance Day is celebrated every year on April 29 to honour the birth anniversary of Jean-Georges Noverre, a pioneer of modern dance. The day highlights the importance of dance as a universal language that transcends cultural and linguistic barriers. It encourages participation from people of all ages and promotes creativity, emotional expression, and cultural exchange. Organised globally with support from institutions like UNESCO, the observance brings together artists, students, and communities through performances, workshops, and events. It also emphasizes the role of dance in improving physical fitness, mental well-being, and fostering global harmony.

questions.question: Which company has proposed a $11.75 billion all-cash acquisition of Organon & Co., marking one of the largest overseas deals by an Indian firm?
questions.explanation: Sun Pharma has announced a major international acquisition plan to purchase Organon & Co. for $11.75 billion in an all-cash deal. This move represents one of the largest overseas acquisitions by an Indian company and highlights its strategy to expand globally. The acquisition will significantly strengthen its footprint across multiple countries and enhance its presence in high-growth segments like women’s health and biosimilars. With Organon’s extensive product portfolio and global reach, Sun Pharma aims to become a leading global pharmaceutical player while reducing dependence on traditional generics.

questions.question: On which date is the World Day for Safety and Health at Work observed annually to promote safe and healthy workplaces?
questions.explanation: World Day for Safety and Health at Work is observed annually on April 28 to raise awareness about workplace safety and promote healthy working conditions globally. Initiated by the International Labour Organisation (ILO), the day focuses on preventing occupational accidents and diseases while improving overall worker well-being. It also commemorates workers who have suffered injuries or lost their lives due to unsafe work environments. The observance highlights the importance of strong safety standards, mental health awareness, and collaboration among governments, employers, and employees to build safer, more inclusive, and productive workplaces worldwide.

questions.question: Who has recently assumed charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) in India?
questions.explanation: Anugraha Narayana Das, a 1991-batch officer of the Indian Defence Accounts Service (IDAS), has taken charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA). With over three decades of experience in defence finance and public administration, he has held several key positions across ministries and defence establishments. His expertise includes auditing, budgeting, procurement policy, and expenditure monitoring. As CGDA, he is responsible for managing defence accounts, ensuring transparency, auditing expenditures, and advising on financial matters. His leadership is expected to strengthen accountability and efficiency in defence spending, which is a crucial component of government expenditure.

questions.question: What was India’s industrial output growth rate in March 2026, marking the lowest level in five months?
questions.explanation: India’s industrial output growth, measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), slowed to 4.1% in March 2026, marking a five-month low. This decline reflects weakening momentum in key sectors, particularly manufacturing and electricity, which play a major role in industrial performance. While the mining sector showed improvement, it was not sufficient to offset the slowdown in other areas. The IIP is an important indicator of economic health, as it captures trends in industrial activity, demand, and capacity utilisation. A slowdown suggests cautious demand conditions, possible supply disruptions, and broader economic challenges affecting production levels.

questions.question: Which company is developing Vikram-1, India’s first privately built orbital rocket aimed at transforming the country’s private space industry?
questions.explanation: Skyroot Aerospace is the private Indian company behind the development of Vikram-1, marking a significant milestone in India’s space sector. The rocket represents a shift from government-led missions to increased private participation, supported by regulatory bodies like IN-SPACe and technical guidance from ISRO. Vikram-1 is designed for cost-effective and on-demand satellite launches, catering to the growing small satellite market. With advanced features such as 3D-printed engines and lightweight composite structures, the initiative highlights India’s push toward innovation and commercialisation in space technology, positioning Skyroot Aerospace as a pioneering player in this evolving ecosystem.

questions.question: In which state was the fourth phase of the PMGSY road projects launched?
questions.explanation: The fourth phase of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY-IV) was launched in the Rayagada district, which is located in the state of Odisha. This initiative is part of a broader rural development strategy aimed at improving infrastructure and connectivity in remote and hilly regions. The project includes the construction of hundreds of new roads covering extensive distances to link previously unconnected areas. In addition to road development, financial allocations were made for housing, employment generation, and watershed management. These efforts are aligned with the state’s long-term development vision to enhance rural livelihoods and infrastructure.

questions.question: When was the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT) established?
questions.explanation: The Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT) was established in 1963 with the objective of professionalising India’s foreign trade management and supporting export-oriented research and policy development. Over the years, it has grown into a premier institution under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, contributing significantly to international business education and research. Its establishment marked an important step in strengthening India’s global trade capabilities during a period when the country was expanding its economic engagement with the world. The institute continues to play a vital role in shaping skilled professionals in international trade and business domains.

questions.question: What was the percentage drop in snow persistence recorded in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region during the winter season of 2025–2026?
questions.explanation: The Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region witnessed a significant environmental change with a 27% decline in snow persistence during the winter season of November 2025 to March 2026. This marks the fourth consecutive year of declining snow levels, highlighting a worrying trend linked to climate change. Reduced snow persistence affects water availability as it lowers early summer river flows, which are crucial for agriculture, hydropower, and drinking water supply. The decline also increases dependence on groundwater and raises drought risks in several basins. This situation underscores the urgent need for climate adaptation and sustainable water management strategies.

questions.question: Which institution developed a new surgical technique to treat severe spinal deformities in India?
questions.explanation: AIIMS Delhi has pioneered a modified surgical technique to treat severe spinal deformities, marking a significant advancement in medical science. Developed by a specialist team, this method improves upon the traditional posterior vertebral column resection (PVCR) procedure by preserving spinal stability during surgery. The innovation is particularly beneficial for high-risk patients experiencing extreme deformities, breathing issues, and chronic pain. By enhancing surgical safety and reducing neurological complications, the technique has improved patient outcomes and mobility. This breakthrough has also received international recognition, highlighting India’s growing contribution to advanced medical research and surgical innovation.

questions.question: What percentage of all diseases in India is accounted for by cardiovascular diseases according to the NSO Survey 2025?
questions.explanation: Cardiovascular diseases have emerged as a major health concern in India, showing a significant increase over recent years. According to the NSO Survey 2025, these diseases now account for 25.6% of all reported illnesses, making them the leading category among various health conditions. This rise reflects changing lifestyles, increased stress levels, and other risk factors such as poor diet and lack of physical activity. Notably, the impact is not limited to older populations, as younger age groups are also increasingly affected. The data highlights the urgent need for improved public health strategies, awareness campaigns, and preventive healthcare measures to address this growing burden.

questions.question: Which country’s intelligence agency designated Khalistani extremists as a national security threat in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Canada took a significant step in May 2026 by officially designating Khalistani extremists as a national security threat through its intelligence agency, the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS). This classification highlights concerns regarding extremist networks operating within the country that allegedly engage in fundraising and support activities for violent agendas. The designation distinguishes between peaceful political advocacy and extremist actions linked to terrorism. This move also comes in the context of strained diplomatic relations with India, emphasising the importance of national security while balancing civil liberties and international relations.

questions.question: What is the name of the indigenous Integrated Alert System powering the Cell Broadcast Alert System for disaster warnings in India?
questions.explanation: The Cell Broadcast Alert System, introduced in India for real-time disaster warnings, is powered by an indigenous technology known as SACHET. This system has been developed by the Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT) and plays a crucial role in enhancing disaster preparedness and response. It enables authorities to send immediate alerts to citizens’ mobile phones without requiring any prior subscription or user action. The alerts include loud alarm tones and flashing messages, ensuring high visibility. SACHET supports multiple regional languages and is designed to cover a wide range of emergencies, including natural disasters like earthquakes and tsunamis, as well as man-made threats.

questions.question: Where was the ‘Run for Sun’ Marathon, organised by MNRE to mark International Sun Day, held?
questions.explanation: The ‘Run for Sun’ Marathon was organised by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) as part of the celebrations for International Sun Day, emphasising India’s commitment to renewable energy. The event was held in New Delhi, the capital city of India, which frequently serves as the venue for major national initiatives and awareness programs. Conducted at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, the marathon included 2 km and 5 km races. Hosting the event in New Delhi ensured maximum participation, visibility, and outreach for promoting solar energy and sustainability awareness.

questions.question: Which state mandated the timely distribution of educational materials through a centralised procurement system for government schools in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Telangana introduced a significant reform in May 2026 by mandating a centralised procurement system for distributing educational materials in government schools. This initiative aims to ensure timely delivery and maintain uniform quality across all departments, including those serving backward classes, minorities, tribal communities, and scheduled castes. The policy replaces the earlier decentralised system, which had issues related to fund mismanagement and inefficiencies. By centralising procurement, the government seeks to enhance transparency, streamline logistics, and provide students with essential items like uniforms, notebooks, and school supplies efficiently.

questions.question: What percentage of land animal habitats are projected to be threatened by extreme climate events by 2085?
questions.explanation: A global study published in May 2026 highlights the severe impact of climate change on biodiversity, projecting that 36% of terrestrial vertebrate habitats will be affected by extreme weather events by 2085. The research covered thousands of species across multiple ecosystems and revealed that rising temperatures, heatwaves, wildfires, droughts, and floods will increasingly overlap, intensifying risks to wildlife. Regions like the Amazon Basin, Africa, and Southeast Asia are particularly vulnerable. Amphibians are expected to face the highest level of exposure. These findings emphasise the urgent need for climate action and biodiversity conservation strategies worldwide.

questions.question: In which country was an ordinance issued to remove 1,594 political appointees in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Nepal undertook a major administrative reform in May 2026 when its President issued an ordinance to remove 1,594 political appointees. This move was aimed at restructuring the government under the new leadership following recent elections. The ordinance mandated the termination of all public appointments made before a specified date, ensuring a fresh administrative setup. Alongside this, the government initiated several strong measures, including suspending parliamentary sessions and amending financial laws to strengthen governance. These actions reflect Nepal’s efforts to enhance administrative efficiency, enforce accountability, and support its evolving political landscape after the electoral transition.

questions.question: Which private India-based company successfully launched the 190 kg Earth observation satellite “Mission Drishti” aboard a Falcon 9 rocket in May 2026?
questions.explanation: GalaxEye Space, a Bengaluru-based private Earth observation space technology company, successfully launched Mission Drishti aboard SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket on May 3, 2026. The satellite weighs 190 kg and is considered the largest satellite ever built by a private Indian company. It carries the innovative OptoSAR payload, which combines optical imaging and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) into a single platform. This technology allows simultaneous collection of optical and radar data under all weather conditions, both day and night. The satellite is expected to support disaster management, agriculture monitoring, border surveillance, and infrastructure planning with enhanced Earth observation capabilities.

questions.question: Who were appointed as full-time members of NITI Aayog by the Union Government, increasing its total full-time membership to seven?

options.A: r R Balasubramaniam and Dr Joram Aniya
options.B: shok Kumar Lahiri and Rajiv Gauba
options.C: K V Raju and Gobardhan Das

questions.explanation: Dr R Balasubramaniam and Dr Joram Aniya were appointed as full-time members of NITI Aayog by the Union Government. Their appointment expanded the total number of full-time members in the government think tank to seven. Dr R Balasubramaniam is known as a physician, public policy expert, and founder of organisations such as the Swami Vivekananda Youth Movement (SVYM) and GRAAM. Dr Joram Aniya is an academician from Arunachal Pradesh and is recognised as the first woman from the Nyishi community to earn a PhD in the state. NITI Aayog, established in 2015, functions as the premier public policy think tank of the Government of India.

questions.question: With which country did India conduct the bilateral military exercise CINBAX-II 2026?
questions.explanation: India conducted the bilateral military exercise CINBAX-II 2026 with Cambodia. The exercise was held from May 4 to May 17, 2026, at the Techo Sen Phnom Thom Mreas Prov Royal Cambodian Air Force Training Centre in Kampong Speu Province. Conducted under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate, the exercise focused on joint company-level operations in a sub-conventional environment. The Indian Army contingent mainly consisted of personnel from the Maratha Light Infantry Regiment, while the Royal Cambodian Army also participated actively. Key operational areas included counter-terrorism drills, drone operations, mortar deployment, sniper tactics, and joint defence coordination in semi-urban warfare scenarios.

questions.question: Which city emerged as the world's fastest-growing major city through 2035 in Savills' Growth Hubs Index?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru secured the top position in Savills' Growth Hubs Index as the world’s fastest-growing major city through 2035 among 245 evaluated urban centres. The ranking was determined using indicators such as projected GDP growth, personal wealth expansion, demographic trends, inward migration, and high-income household growth. Bengaluru’s rise has been driven by its strong, skilled workforce and the rapid growth of Global Capability Centres (GCCs). Commonly known as the Silicon Valley of India, the city is also home to the headquarters of ISRO. The report highlighted India’s strong presence in the global rankings, reflecting significant urban economic growth across multiple Indian cities.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Director (Strategic Project) of Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) on May 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: Retired Commodore Jasvinder Singh assumed charge as the Director (Strategic Project) of Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL) on May 1, 2026. Before joining HSL, he served as the Director (Strategic Project) in the Indian Navy. With more than three decades of operational and technical experience, he has worked on naval ships, submarines, DRDO facilities, and tri-service establishments. His educational background includes degrees in Mechanical Engineering, Marine Engineering, and Defence and Strategic Studies. At HSL, he is responsible for overseeing strategic initiatives and managing critical submarine projects for the Indian armed forces. HSL, headquartered in Visakhapatnam, is notable for building INS Arihant, India’s first nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the new Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for a three-year term beginning May 3, 2026?
questions.explanation: Rohit Jain was appointed as the new Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for a three-year term effective from May 3, 2026. Before this appointment, he served as an Executive Director at the RBI. He succeeded T Rabi Sankar, who retired after completing his extended tenure. Under the RBI Act, 1934, the central bank is required to have exactly four Deputy Governors, ensuring a balanced structure with internal experts and external professionals. The other serving Deputy Governors are Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta, and S C Murmu. The RBI, established in 1935 and nationalised in 1949, is headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

questions.question: Until which year has the Andhra Pradesh government extended the Ragi Java nutrition programme for government school students?
questions.explanation: The Andhra Pradesh government extended the Ragi Java nutrition programme for government school students until April 2029 through an agreement signed with the Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust. The programme provides a daily nutritious drink made from ragi flour and jaggery, both supplied free of cost by the trust. It currently benefits more than 30 lakh students studying in nearly 44,000 government schools across the state. The initiative aims to improve children’s health, energy levels, attentiveness in classrooms, and school attendance. The Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, founded in 1972, has been actively supporting welfare and educational initiatives in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Which district was officially designated as India's first and only pearl farming cluster in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Hazaribag in Jharkhand was officially designated as India’s first and only pearl farming cluster on May 3, 2026. The project focuses on developing pearl cultivation through dedicated pond clusters in the Daurwa-Kundwa area and integrating pearl culture around cage culture operations in the Tilaiya reservoir. The initiative aims to empower women by involving self-help groups (SHGs) and establishing an all-women Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) for cultivation and management activities. Supported under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), the project uses modern aquaculture technologies and direct market linkages to strengthen freshwater pearl farming and rural livelihoods in the region.

questions.question: Which mutual fund company launched the dedicated Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) brand named RedHex SIF in India in May 2026?
questions.explanation: HSBC Mutual Fund launched RedHex SIF, a dedicated Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) brand in India, on May 4, 2026. The SEBI-approved investment structure is designed for experienced investors, institutional participants, and High Net-Worth Individuals (HNIs). The fund requires a minimum investment of ₹10 lakh and combines the transparency and governance standards of mutual funds with the flexibility of advanced asset management strategies. RedHex SIF focuses on theme-based portfolio construction along with strong risk management practices. HSBC Holdings plc, headquartered in London, operates in 56 countries and territories and is one of the world’s leading banking and financial services organisations.

questions.question: Who won the 2026 WTA 1000 Madrid Open women’s singles title by defeating Mirra Andreeva in the final?
questions.explanation: Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine won the 2026 Madrid Open women’s singles title after defeating Russia’s Mirra Andreeva in straight sets, 7-5, 6-3. The victory marked Kostyuk’s third career WTA tournament title and her first-ever WTA 1000-level championship.
