This partnership aims to modernize India’s vocational training ecosystem by integrating Autodesk’s advanced design and manufacturing tools into Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs). The initiative will train both students and instructors in digital prototyping, CAD, and AI-enhanced design systems, making India’s vocational workforce more future-ready. By embedding these skills early, the collaboration supports innovation, employability, and industry-aligned technical education.

questions.question: Which country is set to join the U.S.-brokered Abraham Accords, marking a major diplomatic shift in Central Asia?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan is poised to become the newest member of the Abraham Accords, a U.S.-brokered framework that normalizes relations between Israel and Muslim-majority nations. Announced by U.S. President Donald Trump on November 6, 2025, this development expands the accords’ influence beyond the Arab world into Central Asia. Kazakhstan’s entry signifies its intent to strengthen diplomatic, economic, and security ties with Israel and other signatories. The move aligns with its foreign policy of dialogue and regional stability, while also advancing the U.S. strategy of deepening engagement with Central Asian nations traditionally within Russia and China’s spheres of influence.

questions.question: Which bird species has vanished from 72% of its historical nesting sites in India, according to a Wildlife Institute of India report?
questions.explanation: A nationwide survey conducted by the Wildlife Institute of India revealed that vultures have disappeared from 72% of their historical nesting sites across India, with only 120 out of 425 sites still active. Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan together account for 63% of the remaining nests, most of which are located in protected areas. The report also identified 93 new nesting sites. Notably, the Slender-billed vulture has lost all 47 of its previous nesting sites, with major threats including habitat destruction, poisoning from toxic veterinary drugs, and attacks by feral dogs.

questions.question: What percentage of its stake in SBI Funds Management Ltd (SBIFML) has the State Bank of India (SBI) approved to divest through an IPO?
questions.explanation: State Bank of India (SBI) has approved the divestment of a 6.3% stake, equivalent to 3.2 crore shares, in its subsidiary SBI Funds Management Ltd (SBIFML) via an Initial Public Offering (IPO). Additionally, its co-promoter, Amundi India Holding, will sell 3.7%, making the total IPO size 10% of equity. This move aims to unlock value and prepare SBIFML for its public listing in 2026, marking it as SBI’s third listed subsidiary after SBI Cards and SBI Life Insurance.

questions.question: Which city was ranked the cleanest in India in October 2025, according to CREA’s Air Quality Snapshot?
questions.explanation: As per the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) Air Quality Snapshot for October 2025, Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, recorded the cleanest air in India with an average PM2.5 concentration of just 10 μg/m³. In contrast, Dharuhera in Haryana topped the list of polluted cities with a PM2.5 level of 123 μg/m³, while other highly polluted cities included Ghaziabad, Delhi, and Noida. The report emphasized the need for consistent and year-round air quality management rather than short-term, seasonal interventions such as the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

questions.question: Which country celebrated 100 years of hockey excellence?
questions.explanation: India celebrated a century of hockey excellence at the Major Dhyan Chand Stadium in New Delhi, marking 100 years of remarkable achievements in the sport. The event was jointly organized by the Sports Authority of India and Hockey India, with participation from Union ministers, the FIH President, and legendary hockey players. Highlights included the launch of a commemorative book and a special exhibition showcasing India’s rich hockey legacy. The celebration also featured a friendly match where the Sports Ministry XI triumphed over the Hockey India XI 3–1, symbolizing India’s enduring passion and success in hockey.

questions.question: Which institution patented an AI-based system to decode rainfall data using radar signals?
questions.explanation: The Cochin University of Science & Technology (CUSAT) has patented an advanced machine learning system designed to accurately decode rainfall information from radar signals. Developed at the Advanced Centre for Atmospheric Radar Research (ACARR), the innovation employs a Hybrid Adaptive Bi-Gaussian Algorithm integrated with a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to distinguish between raindrop and turbulence echoes in real time. This AI-driven approach enhances the precision of monsoon monitoring and flood forecasting, significantly improving Kerala’s climate resilience and contributing to the advancement of atmospheric and environmental research in India.

questions.question: In which city did RITES Ltd sign an MoU with DGNP for naval infrastructure projects?
questions.explanation: RITES Ltd, a Government of India enterprise under the Ministry of Railways, entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Directorate General of Naval Projects (DGNP) in Mumbai to provide consultancy services for naval infrastructure development in the Mumbai region. The services will cover soil studies, feasibility analysis, detailed project reports, structural design, project management, and third-party inspection. This partnership aims to improve planning, design, and execution efficiency for Indian Navy infrastructure projects, strengthening defence-related construction capabilities in the Mumbai area.

questions.question: Which country recorded the highest absolute rise in greenhouse gas emissions in 2023–24, according to the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025?
questions.explanation: According to the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025, titled Off Target, India registered the highest absolute increase in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions during 2023–24, amounting to 165 million tonnes. Despite this rise, India continues to maintain one of the lowest per capita emissions among major global economies. The report highlights that the G20 nations collectively saw an emissions increase of 22 million tonnes in the same period. With the world projected to warm by 2.8°C—far exceeding the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C goal—India faces growing pressure ahead of the COP30 climate summit to adopt stronger mitigation measures.

questions.question: Which state government released a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for making farm tools more women-friendly?
questions.explanation: The Odisha government introduced a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on November 4, 2025, to ensure farm equipment is ergonomically designed for women farmers. The initiative focuses on reducing physical strain, pain, and health issues faced by women due to the use of tools originally made for men. Since more than half of women farmers experience musculoskeletal disorders from male-centric implements, this SOP—developed under the Shree Anna Abhiyan pilot projects—will help test and refine both existing and new farm tools to promote inclusivity and improve agricultural productivity in Odisha.

questions.question: On which date is World Radiography Day observed every year to commemorate the discovery of X-rays?
questions.explanation: World Radiography Day is celebrated annually on November 8 to mark the discovery of X-rays by German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen in 1895. The day honours radiographers and radiologists for their critical role in healthcare, highlighting how imaging technologies such as X-rays, CT, MRI, and AI-driven diagnostics revolutionize medical science by enabling early detection and accurate treatment. It also emphasizes the importance of safety, precision, and compassionate care in radiological practices. Observed globally since 2007, the day reminds the world of radiography’s essential contribution to saving lives and advancing modern medicine.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian para-archer to be selected for the able-bodied national archery team?
questions.explanation: Sheetal Devi, an 18-year-old para-archer from Jammu and Kashmir, made history by becoming the first Indian para-athlete to join the able-bodied national archery team. Born with phocomelia, a condition that left her without arms, she adapted her technique to shoot using her legs and shoulders. Her remarkable performances—winning medals at the Asian Para Games, World Championships, and Paralympics—earned her a spot in the compound women’s team for the Asia Cup 2025 in Jeddah. Her selection reflects a monumental step toward inclusivity, merit-based recognition, and breaking barriers in Indian sports.

questions.question: Which country commissioned its third and most advanced aircraft carrier, the Fujian, equipped with EMALS technology?
questions.explanation: China has commissioned its third and most advanced aircraft carrier, Fujian, marking a significant milestone in its naval modernization and maritime power projection. Launched in November 2025 at Sanya Port, Hainan, the Fujian is China’s first flat-deck carrier equipped with the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS)—a cutting-edge technology previously used only by the U.S. Navy. With a displacement of around 80,000 tonnes and all-electric propulsion, it enables smoother and faster aircraft launches, enhancing strike range and combat readiness. The Fujian joins Liaoning and Shandong in China’s carrier fleet, showcasing Beijing’s growing ambitions in the South China Sea and Indo-Pacific region.

questions.question: Which Indian aerospace company signed a $1 billion deal with GE for 113 F404 engines to power the LCA Tejas Mk 1A jets?
questions.explanation: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) signed a $1 billion agreement with General Electric (GE) for the supply of 113 F404-GE-IN20 engines, which will power 97 LCA Tejas Mk 1A fighter jets of the Indian Air Force. This deal marks a crucial milestone in India’s quest for self-reliance in defence manufacturing and strengthens the indigenous aircraft production ecosystem. The F404 engines are known for their reliability, high performance, and compatibility with advanced fighter systems. This partnership not only supports Tejas Mk 1A production but also paves the way for future collaboration on F414 engines for the LCA Mk 2, enhancing India’s aerospace capabilities.

questions.question: In which year is India scheduled to conduct the next All India Tiger Estimation (AITE), the world’s largest wildlife survey?
questions.explanation: The next All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) will be conducted in 2026, marking it as the world’s largest wildlife survey. India, home to over 75% of the global wild tiger population, will use a mix of ground tracking, satellite technology, and AI-based camera traps to ensure scientific accuracy and ecosystem-wide assessment. Building on the 2022 survey that recorded 3,682 tigers, the 2026 census aims to evaluate not just tiger numbers but also habitat health, prey density, and human-wildlife interactions. With participation from over 60,000 forest personnel, this massive operation reinforces India’s leadership in global wildlife conservation.

questions.question: Who became India’s 91st Chess Grandmaster after winning the ASEAN Championship 2025?
questions.explanation: Raahul VS became India’s 91st Chess Grandmaster after an impressive performance at the 6th ASEAN Individual Championship 2025, where he clinched the title with a round to spare. His victory highlights India’s continued dominance and depth in global chess. Raahul had earlier achieved his International Master title in 2021 and demonstrated consistent progress toward the GM title through his exceptional tournament performances. This accomplishment follows recent successes by Illamparthi AR and S Rohith Krishna, showcasing a strong new generation of Indian chess players achieving international recognition and strengthening India’s position as a powerhouse in the chess world.

questions.question: Which country conducted the strategic Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) test designated GT-254 from Vandenberg Space Force Base in November 2025?
questions.explanation: The United States conducted the Minuteman III ICBM test (GT-254) from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California, on November 5, 2025. The test involved launching an unarmed missile toward the central Pacific near the Ronald Reagan Ballistic Missile Defense Test Site (Kwajalein Atoll) to validate reliability, accuracy, and readiness of the US land-based nuclear deterrent. The launch also verified the Airborne Launch Control System (ALCS) using an E-6B aircraft, ensuring redundant command-and-control capability. While the timing drew global attention due to concurrent nuclear policy debates, US officials clarified that it was a routine operational readiness test supporting strategic stability and deterrence credibility.

questions.question: In which city was India’s first fully digital museum dedicated to tribal freedom fighters inaugurated?
questions.explanation: India’s first Digital Museum of Tribal Freedom Fighters was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Nava Raipur, Atal Nagar, Chhattisgarh. Officially named the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Memorial and Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum, it honours tribal warriors who resisted British rule and contributed to India’s independence movement. The museum uses cutting-edge digital technology, including VFX projections, QR-coded storytelling, and interactive screens, to create an immersive educational experience. It celebrates figures like Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh and showcases historic tribal revolts such as the Halba Rebellion and Bhumkal Movement, promoting both cultural preservation and tourism in Nava Raipur.

questions.question: Which Indian bank became the first to cross both $100 billion in market capitalisation and ₹100 trillion in total business?
questions.explanation: The State Bank of India (SBI) achieved a landmark milestone by surpassing $100 billion in market capitalisation and ₹100 trillion in total business, marking a historic first in India’s banking history. This achievement highlights SBI’s dominant position in retail, SME, and corporate lending, backed by strong Q2 FY26 financial performance and 12.7% year-on-year credit growth. With total deposits around ₹55.9 lakh crore and advances of ₹44.2 lakh crore, SBI’s robust digital transformation, improving asset quality, and investor confidence have propelled it into the elite global banking league. Headquartered in Mumbai, SBI continues to be the backbone of India’s financial ecosystem.

questions.question: How many new Vande Bharat Express trains were flagged off by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from Varanasi?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off four new Vande Bharat Express trains from Varanasi, marking a significant milestone in India’s ongoing railway modernization efforts. The newly launched routes include Banaras–Khajuraho, Lucknow–Saharanpur, Firozpur–Delhi, and Ernakulam–Bengaluru. These trains are designed to enhance regional connectivity, reduce travel time, and offer modern comfort through energy-efficient and high-speed rail technology. The initiative strengthens intercity travel, boosts tourism, and supports economic growth across northern and southern India. Each route strategically connects cultural, commercial, and technological hubs, aligning with the government’s broader vision for efficient and self-reliant rail infrastructure.

questions.question: Who was the pioneering molecular biologist credited with co-discovering the double helix structure of DNA and later leading the Human Genome Project?
questions.explanation: James D. Watson was an American molecular biologist who, along with Francis H.C. Crick, discovered the double helix structure of DNA in 1953 — a groundbreaking model that transformed the study of genetics. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962 for this discovery. Watson later became the director of Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory and led the Human Genome Project, contributing to the mapping of over 3 billion base pairs of human DNA. His legacy, while marked by controversy, remains central to modern molecular biology.

questions.question: How many new butterfly species were discovered in Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang Valley, linking the ecosystems of Tibet and India?
questions.explanation: Six new butterfly species have been discovered in Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang Valley, highlighting the region’s exceptional ecological diversity. This discovery establishes a biological link between Tibet’s Yarlung Tsangpo and India’s Brahmaputra basin, emphasizing the shared evolutionary and environmental characteristics of the two regions. The finding also underscores the importance of community-based conservation efforts, which play a crucial role in protecting this biodiversity hotspot from threats like hydropower projects and climate change. Such studies not only expand scientific knowledge of Himalayan fauna but also strengthen global conservation strategies for fragile mountain ecosystems.

questions.question: Which Indian AI platform developed by the Indus Valley Group aims to become the world’s most affordable homegrown AI solution ensuring data sovereignty?
questions.explanation: Atomesus is an Indian AI platform developed by the Indus Valley Group, designed to be the world’s most affordable and secure homegrown AI system. Built by young innovators with ISRO-linked experience, it employs a hybrid intelligence model that merges proprietary technologies with India-based secure integration. The project emphasises data sovereignty and aims to democratise access to AI for students, startups, and enterprises worldwide. By focusing on affordability, accessibility, and local innovation, Atomesus seeks to position India as a global leader in ethical and inclusive artificial intelligence development.

questions.question: The Ramnami tribe, known for tattooing the name “Ram” on their bodies and homes, originates from which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Ramnami tribe originates from Chhattisgarh and is renowned for its unique devotional practice of inscribing the name “Ram” on their bodies and homes as an expression of faith. Founded in the 19th century by Parsuram Bhardwaj, the community emphasises devotion, equality, and rejection of caste hierarchy. They follow a formless concept of divinity and uphold gender equality as part of their spiritual philosophy. Each year, the tribe celebrates their faith through the Bhajan Mela in Sarsiwa, where devotees gather to sing hymns from the Ramcharitmanas and honour the “Ram” jayostambh, symbolizing unity and devotion.

questions.question: What is the name of the global campaign launched by UPL to recognise farmers as key agents of climate resilience ahead of COP30 in Brazil?
questions.explanation: #AFarmerCan is a global campaign launched by UPL to celebrate farmers as central figures in driving climate resilience and sustainable agriculture. Introduced ahead of COP30 in Brazil, the campaign shares 20 farmer stories worldwide, demonstrating how local practices can contribute to global climate goals. UPL’s initiative is built on a four-pillar framework — Pay, Protect, Procure, Promote — designed to empower and reward climate-smart farming. By highlighting the critical role of farmers in environmental stewardship, the campaign aims to shift public perception and promote a more sustainable and equitable global food system.

questions.question: Which country, along with the United States, signed a joint framework to strengthen critical mineral and rare earth supply chains?
questions.explanation: Japan partnered with the United States to establish a joint framework focused on securing and strengthening the supply chains of critical minerals and rare earth elements essential for advanced technologies such as electric vehicles, batteries, and renewable energy systems. The agreement emphasises coordinated investment, fair market practices, and resilient bilateral supply chains across the stages of extraction, separation, and processing. Through this collaboration, both countries aim to reduce dependency on single-source suppliers, diversify global mineral resources, and enhance economic and strategic stability in the rapidly evolving clean technology and semiconductor sectors.

questions.question: On which date is National Legal Services Day observed every year in India?
questions.explanation: National Legal Services Day is observed annually on November 9 to commemorate the enforcement of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, which came into effect on this day in 1995. The day highlights India’s commitment to ensuring equal access to justice for all, especially the poor and disadvantaged. It promotes awareness about citizens’ legal rights and strengthens mechanisms for free legal aid through the three-tier system — National, State, and District Legal Services Authorities. The observance reinforces the principle that justice must be affordable, accessible, and inclusive for every citizen.

questions.question: By which year has the European Union set its target to achieve a 90% reduction in emissions from 1990 levels?
questions.explanation: The European Union has established 2040 as the target year to achieve a 90% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions compared to 1990 levels. This goal includes an allowance for up to 5% of reductions through foreign carbon credits, effectively making domestic cuts 85%. The agreement introduces a carbon credit pilot phase (2031–2035), aiming to balance environmental responsibility with economic realities. Although the plan demonstrates strong climate ambition, some critics express concern that the flexibility provided by carbon credits may weaken the EU’s overall emission integrity. Nonetheless, the 2040 goal marks a critical step toward carbon neutrality.

questions.question: Which African nation is set to receive a USD 200 million Line of Credit from India to support its defence modernisation efforts?
questions.explanation: Angola is the African nation partnering with India to strengthen cooperation in defence and energy sectors. India is finalising a USD 200 million Line of Credit to assist Angola’s defence modernisation, reflecting growing strategic and developmental ties. The two countries are also expanding their USD 5 billion energy partnership, primarily driven by oil trade, which plays a crucial role in India’s energy security. This collaboration aligns with India’s broader South-South cooperation framework, aimed at fostering sustainable development, capacity building, and mutual growth with partner nations across Africa and the Global South.

questions.question: Which Indian state, known as the "Land of the Gods," celebrates its Foundation Day on November 9 to mark its formation in the year 2000?
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand celebrates its Foundation Day every year on November 9, commemorating its creation as India’s 27th state in the year 2000, after being carved out of Uttar Pradesh. Originally named Uttaranchal, it was officially renamed Uttarakhand in 2007 to reflect its cultural and historical identity. In 2025, the state observes its Silver Jubilee (25 years) of formation with grand celebrations highlighting its progress in tourism, education, infrastructure, and sustainability. Known as Devbhoomi, or the Land of the Gods, Uttarakhand holds immense spiritual and ecological significance in India’s landscape.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority’s (IEPFA) financial awareness drive held in Karnal, Haryana?
questions.explanation: The Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA), under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, organized a financial awareness drive aimed at empowering rural women. Conducted in Karnal, Haryana, under the theme “Viksit Bharat ke path par Saksham Naari,” the initiative focused on enhancing financial literacy, promoting safe investment practices, and fostering digital inclusion among women Self-Help Groups. Partnering with SEBI, AMFI, NCAER, and HSRLM, the program sought to strengthen financial independence and informed decision-making among rural women, contributing to inclusive economic growth and women’s empowerment in India.

questions.question: In which country was a new natural gas discovery announced in the Western Desert’s Badr-15 area?
questions.explanation: Egypt announced a major natural gas discovery in the Badr-15 area of its Western Desert, tapping into the Lower Bahariya reservoir. The find is expected to add approximately 15 billion cubic feet to Egypt’s gas reserves, with an initial production rate of about 16 million cubic feet per day. This discovery strengthens Egypt’s strategy to boost domestic energy production, reduce reliance on imports, and position itself as a key energy hub in the region. The Western Desert continues to be an important frontier for hydrocarbon exploration, offering significant economic and strategic benefits through expanded reserves and increased energy security.

questions.question: Which Indian Naval Ship arrived at Port Louis, Mauritius as part of an operational deployment?
questions.explanation: INS Savitri, an indigenously built Offshore Patrol Vessel constructed by Mazagon Dock Ltd, Mumbai, arrived at Port Louis, Mauritius as part of an operational deployment. Commissioned on 7 June 1990, the vessel operates under the Eastern Naval Command based at Visakhapatnam. Equipped with a 40×60 Bofors Gun and a helicopter deck for Chetak helicopter operations, INS Savitri is designed for aerial surveillance, search and rescue, and patrol missions. Its visit to Mauritius underscores India’s commitment to maritime cooperation, regional security, and fostering strong bilateral ties with Indian Ocean nations.

questions.question: In which city did the 18th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference 2025 conclude?
questions.explanation: The 18th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference 2025 was held in Gurugram, a rapidly developing city known for its modern infrastructure and urban mobility advancements. Hosting this prestigious event highlights Gurugram’s growing role as a hub for discussions and innovations in sustainable and smart urban transport solutions. The conference brought together policymakers, experts, and industry leaders to recognize and celebrate excellence in urban transport across Indian cities, promoting best practices and future-ready mobility systems.

questions.question: Where was the National Urban Conclave 2025 inaugurated by Union Minister Manohar Lal?
questions.explanation: The National Urban Conclave 2025 was inaugurated at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, by Union Minister Manohar Lal under the theme “Sustainable Urban Development and Governance.” The event marked the launch of several key initiatives, including the Dumpsite Remediation Accelerator Programme (DRAP), Urban Invest Window (UiWIN), Swachh Bharat Knowledge Management Unit, and Jal Hi Janani. DRAP aims to remediate 214 major dumpsites accounting for 80% of legacy waste. With participation from over 2,500 experts and policymakers, the conclave emphasized collaborative efforts toward cleaner, sustainable, and efficiently governed urban ecosystems in India.

questions.question: On which date is World Science Day for Peace and Development observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Science Day for Peace and Development is celebrated annually on November 10, as established by UNESCO in 2001. The day highlights the essential role science plays in promoting peace, sustainability, and global cooperation. It encourages young minds and students to explore how scientific innovation can solve real-world challenges such as climate change, health crises, and resource management. The 2025 theme, “Trust, transformation, and tomorrow: The science we need for 2050,” inspires youth to build trust in science, foster creativity, and use knowledge as a tool for advancing peace and sustainable development worldwide.

questions.question: Where was the two-day National Conference on India’s new criminal laws held on 8–9 November 2025?
questions.explanation: The two-day National Conference on the three new criminal laws was held at the National Judicial Academy in Bhopal. Organized by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Academy, the event focused on ushering India into a new era of criminal justice marked by transparency, technology, and victim-centric reforms. Home Secretary Govind Mohan emphasized the government’s commitment to a secure and efficient justice system. Key discussions revolved around initiatives like e-Sakshya, e-Summon, and Nyay Shruti, which aim to modernize legal processes and ensure swift, accessible, and fair delivery of justice across the country.

questions.question: Which Indian naval ship represented India at Exercise Malabar 2025 held in Guam, North Pacific?
questions.explanation: INS Sahyadri, an indigenously built Guided Missile Stealth Frigate, represented India at Exercise Malabar 2025 in Guam, North Pacific. This exercise, the 28th edition under the Quad framework involving India, the U.S., Japan, and Australia, focuses on strengthening naval cooperation and enhancing maritime interoperability. INS Sahyadri’s participation demonstrates India’s commitment to regional security, technological self-reliance, and operational readiness. The event included both a Harbour Phase for planning and a Sea Phase with joint fleet maneuvers, anti-submarine warfare, and gunnery operations, emphasizing collaboration among Quad nations.

questions.question: Which institute partnered with C-DOT to establish a Centre of Excellence in telecom and cybersecurity research?
questions.explanation: The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier R&D centre under the Department of Telecommunications, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with IIT Gandhinagar to establish a Centre of Excellence (CoE) dedicated to telecom and cybersecurity research. This collaboration aims to integrate C-DOT’s technological expertise with IIT Gandhinagar’s strong academic and research foundation. The CoE will focus on advancing innovation in areas such as artificial intelligence, quantum communication, and next-generation mobile networks, thereby enhancing India’s capabilities in secure and future-ready telecom infrastructure and fostering deeper academia-industry cooperation.

questions.question: Which Indian state launched the country’s first tribal-focused genome sequencing project?
questions.explanation: Gujarat became the first Indian state to launch a tribal-focused genome sequencing project aimed at tackling genetic disorders such as sickle cell anaemia and thalassemia through precision medicine. Implemented by the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC), the initiative forms part of the national Genome India Project. It focuses on sequencing 2,000 tribal genomes across 17 districts to identify genetic mutations and hereditary disease patterns. By developing affordable diagnostic kits and promoting genetic counselling, the project aims to improve healthcare access for tribal populations while advancing India’s capabilities in biotechnology-driven public health innovation and preventive medicine.

questions.question: Which country became the first South Asian nation to join the UN Water Convention in 2025?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh became the first South Asian country to join the UN Water Convention in 2025, marking a major milestone in transboundary water governance. Officially known as the Convention on the Protection and Use of Transboundary Watercourses and International Lakes, it provides a legally binding framework for the equitable and sustainable management of shared water bodies. By acceding to this treaty, Bangladesh aims to strengthen its position in addressing cross-border river issues, particularly with India, and to promote cooperative water management aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. This move enhances Bangladesh’s global engagement on environmental diplomacy and regional water security.

questions.question: Which country is participating with India in the joint military exercise Mitra Shakti 2025?
questions.explanation: Exercise Mitra Shakti 2025 is the 11ᵗʰ edition of the bilateral joint military exercise conducted between the armies of India and Sri Lanka. Held from 10 to 23 November 2025 at the Foreign Training Node in Belagavi, Karnataka, the exercise focuses on counter-terrorism, drone warfare, and UN peacekeeping operations. Indian troops from the Rajput Regiment and Sri Lankan soldiers from the Gajaba Regiment are participating in this edition. The exercise aims to strengthen interoperability, mutual trust, and coordination between the two nations, reflecting their shared commitment to regional peace, security, and defence cooperation in South Asia.

questions.question: What was India’s unemployment rate in the second quarter (Q2) of 2025 according to MoSPI’s Periodic Labour Force Survey?
questions.explanation: In Q2 2025, India’s unemployment rate for individuals aged 15 years and above fell to 5.2%, reflecting a modest but positive improvement in the labour market. This decline from 5.4% in Q1 2025 indicates better job creation and higher labour absorption, especially in rural areas supported by agricultural and government-led employment schemes like MGNREGA. The data, based on the Current Weekly Status (CWS) approach of MoSPI’s Periodic Labour Force Survey, also highlighted a rise in the female labour participation rate to 33.7% and a slight increase in the overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) to 55.1%, showing signs of gradual employment recovery.

questions.question: Which company launched the 7th-generation Ironwood TPU to compete with Nvidia’s AI dominance?
questions.explanation: Google introduced its 7th-generation Ironwood TPU, a cutting-edge AI processing unit designed to enhance the company’s cloud computing and machine learning capabilities. The Ironwood TPU is optimised for training and deploying large-scale AI models such as chatbots and digital assistants. Each Ironwood pod interconnects 9,216 TPUs, significantly reducing data bottlenecks and enabling seamless scaling of massive workloads. This innovation underscores Google’s commitment to advancing AI infrastructure and positioning itself as a formidable competitor to Nvidia in the field of high-performance computing and artificial intelligence development.

questions.question: Which organization has been granted Mini Ratna (Category-I) status by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh?
questions.explanation: Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), a public sector shipyard located in Visakhapatnam, has been granted Mini Ratna (Category-I) status by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The recognition was presented to HSL’s CMD, Cmde Girideep Singh, during the DPSU Annual Review Meeting held in New Delhi. Established originally as the Scindia Shipyard by industrialist Walchand Hirachand under The Scindia Steam Navigation Company Ltd, HSL has played a pivotal role in shipbuilding and naval support operations, significantly contributing to India’s maritime and defence capabilities over the decades.

questions.question: Which Indian state approved the Prohibition of Polygamy Bill 2025 to criminalise multiple marriages?
questions.explanation: The Assam government has approved the Assam Prohibition of Polygamy Bill 2025, marking a historic move to criminalise the practice of multiple marriages while a first marriage is still legally valid. The Bill proposes imprisonment of up to seven years for offenders and establishes a special compensation fund to support women affected by polygamous unions. It excludes Scheduled Tribes and areas under the Sixth Schedule, as well as certain pre-2005 Muslim marriages in Scheduled Areas. The legislation reinforces gender justice, promotes uniform marriage laws, and could serve as a legislative model for other Indian states pursuing similar reforms.

questions.question: Who has been selected as the next Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of GAIL (India) Limited?
questions.explanation: Deepak Gupta, currently serving as Director (Projects) at GAIL (India) Limited, has been recommended by the Public Enterprises Selection Board (PESB) to be the next Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of the Maharatna PSU under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas. With over 35 years of experience in the oil and gas sector, he is recognised for his expertise in project and construction management, digitization, and strategic reforms. A Mechanical Engineer from DTU and a PMP-certified professional, Gupta’s leadership is expected to strengthen GAIL’s project execution and innovation initiatives.

questions.question: In which country did India operate the Ayni Airbase, its only overseas military base, before withdrawing in 2022?
questions.explanation: The Ayni Airbase, located near Dushanbe in Tajikistan, was India’s only overseas military facility until its quiet withdrawal in 2022. Originally a Soviet-era base, Ayni was renovated by India’s Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in the early 2000s with an investment of around $80 million. The base featured a 3,200-metre runway, hangars, and fuel storage, and served as a key strategic outpost near Afghanistan, Pakistan, and China. India’s withdrawal followed the non-renewal of its lease by Tajikistan, reportedly under Russian and Chinese pressure, marking a significant reduction in India’s military footprint in Central Asia.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the first woman to lead UN Tourism?
questions.explanation: Shaikha Nasser Al Nowais from the United Arab Emirates has been appointed as the first woman to head UN Tourism, marking a historic breakthrough in global tourism leadership. Her appointment was confirmed during the 123rd UN Tourism Executive Council session in Segovia, Spain, and she will assume office in January 2026 for a four-year term. With over 16 years of experience in corporate governance and tourism development, Al Nowais has held key roles including Corporate Vice President at Rotana Hotels and Chair of the Abu Dhabi Chamber’s Tourism Working Group. Her leadership emphasises sustainability, digital innovation, and women’s empowerment in global tourism.

questions.question: Which company partnered with Engineers India Limited (EIL) to collaborate on onshore projects in Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: Engineers India Limited (EIL), a Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with NMDC Energy, a UAE-based company, to jointly undertake onshore projects in Saudi Arabia. The partnership covers a wide range of sectors, including oil and gas, refineries, petrochemicals, pipelines, storage, and energy transition. The MoU was formalised at the ADIPEC 2025 event in Abu Dhabi, marking a significant collaboration in advancing cross-border energy infrastructure initiatives.

questions.question: With which country did India sign a Memorandum of Agreement on Mutual Submarine Search and Rescue Support in November 2025?
questions.explanation: India signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) on Mutual Submarine Search and Rescue Support with Vietnam during the 15th India–Vietnam Defence Policy Dialogue held in Hanoi in November 2025. The agreement, co-chaired by India’s Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and Vietnam’s Deputy Defence Minister Sr Lt Gen Hoang Xuan Chien, aims to enhance cooperation in submarine rescue operations, ensure rapid assistance in emergencies, and strengthen interoperability between the two navies. Alongside, a Letter of Intent (LoI) was also signed to deepen collaboration in defence manufacturing and technology, reinforcing the India–Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and Indo-Pacific maritime security.

questions.question: On which date is National Education Day celebrated in India?
questions.explanation: National Education Day is celebrated every year on November 11 to commemorate the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, India’s first Education Minister. The observance was initiated in 2008 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, now known as the Ministry of Education. Maulana Azad played a vital role in laying the foundation of India’s modern education system and establishing key institutions such as the University Grants Commission (UGC), Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), and the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), promoting learning and cultural development across the nation.

questions.question: In which city will the 2nd WHO Traditional Medicine Global Summit be held from December 17–19, 2025?
questions.explanation: The 2nd WHO Traditional Medicine Global Summit is scheduled to be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from December 17 to 19, 2025. Co-hosted by the World Health Organization (WHO) and India’s Ministry of AYUSH, the summit will bring together around 7,000 participants, including global health leaders, researchers, and traditional medicine practitioners. The event, themed “Restoring Balance: The Science and Practice of Health and Well-being,” aims to promote evidence-based traditional medicine, strengthen universal health coverage, and foster collaboration between science, innovation, and indigenous wisdom for sustainable healthcare development worldwide.

questions.question: On which date was World Pneumonia Day 2025 observed to raise global awareness about pneumonia and its prevention?
questions.explanation: World Pneumonia Day 2025 was observed on November 12 to draw global attention to pneumonia, which remains the leading infectious cause of death among children under five and a serious health threat to adults. The observance emphasises prevention through vaccination, improved nutrition, and access to healthcare, aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to reduce child mortality. It also serves as a reminder for governments and health organizations to strengthen efforts toward respiratory disease management and promote awareness of pneumonia’s symptoms, causes, and treatment options for better global health outcomes.

questions.question: With which country did India launch a real-time UPI–EFTS payment link to enhance digital financial cooperation?
questions.explanation: India and Bahrain jointly launched a real-time cross-border payment system linking India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) with Bahrain’s Electronic Funds Transfer System (EFTS) through Fawri+. This initiative, facilitated by the NPCI International and BENEFIT, and guided by the RBI and Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB), marks a significant milestone in fintech cooperation between the two nations. The integration enables instant, secure, and low-cost remittances, advancing digital financial inclusion. Building upon the 2019 MoU and the 2024 Joint Commission pledge, the partnership deepens economic engagement and strengthens people-to-people and financial connectivity between India and Bahrain.

questions.question: Which country has been selected to host the 2027 U.N. Climate Change Conference (COP32)?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia has been chosen to host the 2027 U.N. Climate Change Conference (COP32) in its capital city, Addis Ababa. The announcement was made during Brazil’s COP30 by COP30 President André Corrêa do Lago. This selection marks a significant moment for Africa, highlighting the continent’s growing role in global climate action and sustainable development discussions. Hosting COP32 will allow Ethiopia to spotlight regional environmental challenges, renewable energy initiatives, and resilience strategies. The decision also reflects the UN’s aim to ensure regional balance and representation in major international climate forums.

questions.question: Which sector aims to be digitally transformed through the Sahakar Digi Pay and Sahakar Digi Loan apps launched by Amit Shah?
questions.explanation: Union Cooperation Minister Amit Shah launched two major digital platforms — Sahakar Digi Pay and Sahakar Digi Loan — to modernise urban cooperative banks (UCBs). These initiatives focus on integrating digital payment and lending systems to help UCBs remain competitive in India’s evolving cashless economy. The plan includes onboarding 1,500 banks within two years and ensuring at least one UCB operates in every town with a population exceeding two lakh within five years. The move also supports financial inclusion, youth entrepreneurship, and sectoral revival while reinforcing cooperative banking reforms to strengthen the sector’s financial health and governance standards.

questions.question: What type of battery system did India inaugurate at NTPC NETRA as its first MWh-scale energy storage innovation?
questions.explanation: India inaugurated its first MWh-scale Vanadium Flow Battery at NTPC NETRA, Greater Noida, marking a significant advancement in renewable energy storage technology. The 3 MWh Vanadium Redox Flow Battery (VRFB) system was launched on November 11, 2025, by Shri Manohar Lal, Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs. This innovative system enables long-duration energy storage (LDES), crucial for integrating intermittent renewable sources like solar and wind. Unlike lithium-ion batteries, VRFBs are non-flammable, durable, and allow scalable power and energy capacities. The project enhances India’s energy security, reduces dependence on imported materials, and strengthens its clean energy transition goals.

questions.question: Which state announced plans to establish Old Age Homes in all its districts to support the welfare of senior citizens?
questions.explanation: Nagaland has announced a comprehensive initiative to establish Old Age Homes across all its districts, reflecting the state’s commitment to enhancing elderly welfare and protection. Spearheaded by Advisor Wangpang Konyak, the plan emphasises providing care, nutrition, and social security for vulnerable senior citizens. It aligns with existing welfare programmes such as the Old Age Pension, Elderly Helpline, and Charity Care initiatives. This effort seeks to ensure dignified living conditions and community support for the aged population, showcasing a proactive approach to inclusive governance and social responsibility toward the elderly in Nagaland.

questions.question: Along which highway did SECI and NHAI sign an MoU to install solar power plants for promoting sustainable infrastructure?
questions.explanation: The Solar Energy Corporation of India Ltd. (SECI) and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) signed a Memorandum of Understanding to set up solar power installations along the elevated Delhi section of the Delhi–Dehradun Highway (NH-709B). This project is a step toward integrating renewable energy with transport infrastructure. By harnessing solar energy to power highway systems, the initiative contributes to lowering carbon emissions, promoting green mobility, and advancing India’s commitment toward achieving Net Zero emissions by 2070. It also serves as a benchmark for sustainable infrastructure development across the nation.

questions.question: In which city did the Indian Air Force organise its first-ever full-scale air show to celebrate the IAF’s 93rd anniversary?
questions.explanation: The Indian Air Force’s Eastern Air Command conducted its inaugural full-scale air show in Guwahati to commemorate the 93rd anniversary of the IAF. The spectacular event featured over 75 aircraft, including Rafale, Sukhoi, Mirage, and C-17, executing 25 coordinated formations above the Brahmaputra River. Operations were supported by seven regional bases to ensure precision and safety. The air show also included a cultural tribute to the late Assamese singer Zubeen Garg, with his popular song “Mayabini Ratir Bukut,” blending regional pride with national celebration and showcasing India’s growing air power and aviation excellence.

questions.question: Who won the 2025 Booker Prize for the novel "Flesh"?
questions.explanation: Hungarian-British writer David Szalay won the 2025 Booker Prize for his novel "Flesh", marking a historic win as the first author of his background to receive the honour. The novel is celebrated for its minimalist prose and powerful exploration of class, ambition, and masculinity. It follows a man’s rise from a modest Hungarian housing estate to the sophisticated world of London’s elite, reflecting themes of identity and power. Alongside the prestigious recognition, Szalay received a £50,000 cash prize, earning global literary acclaim and cementing his place among contemporary literary greats.

questions.question: Who won the silver medal in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions event at the ISSF World Championships in Cairo?
questions.explanation: Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, an Indian Olympian shooter, won the silver medal in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions event at the ISSF World Championships held in Cairo. He showcased remarkable consistency by equalling the world record in the qualification round with a score of 466.9, narrowly missing the gold to China’s Yukun Liu, who scored 467.1. This achievement reinforces Tomar’s reputation as one of India’s leading rifle shooters and adds to the country’s growing success in international shooting competitions, highlighting India’s rising stature in precision shooting sports globally.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian to be elected as President of the Organisation Internationale des Constructeurs d’Automobiles (OICA)?
questions.explanation: Shailesh Chandra, Managing Director and CEO of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Tata Electric Mobility, has become the first Indian to be elected President of OICA (Organisation Internationale des Constructeurs d’Automobiles). Headquartered in Paris and founded in 1919, OICA represents the global automobile manufacturers’ community on key issues such as safety, emissions, and trade policy. Chandra’s appointment signifies India’s growing influence in global automotive governance, especially in electric mobility and sustainable transport. His leadership will help align India’s fast-evolving vehicle ecosystem with global standards while promoting EV innovation, cybersecurity, and sustainable manufacturing in the international automotive industry.

questions.question: In which state did MeitY and CERT-In launch the “Cyber Bharat Setu: Bridging States, Securing Bharat” workshop to enhance cyber resilience?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), in collaboration with CERT-In, organised the “Cyber Bharat Setu: Bridging States, Securing Bharat” workshop in Agartala, Tripura. The two-day event, held on November 11–12, 2025, aimed to strengthen cybersecurity awareness and capacity across government officials, law enforcement agencies, and students. Through practical drills and simulated cyber-attack exercises, the initiative sought to improve India’s digital defence preparedness, promote innovation in cyber practices, and build a cohesive national framework for proactive cyber resilience.

questions.question: On which date is World Kindness Day observed each year?
questions.explanation: World Kindness Day is observed annually on November 13 as part of a broader effort to encourage global kindness and compassion. Established in 1998 by the World Kindness Movement, this day highlights the significance of empathy, understanding, and small gestures that help build a more harmonious world. It serves as a reminder for individuals and communities to reflect on their actions and the impact they have on others. By dedicating a specific day to kindness, the initiative inspires people to adopt compassionate behavior in their daily lives, strengthening social bonds and promoting unity across cultures.

questions.question: What is the projected real GDP growth rate for India in Q2 FY26?
questions.explanation: India’s real GDP growth for Q2 FY26 is estimated at 7.2%, reflecting a strengthening economic environment supported by robust private consumption, steady services sector performance, and sustained investment demand. Private consumption saw improved momentum due to rising real incomes, rural wage growth, low inflation, and tax relief measures from the FY26 Budget. On the supply side, both services and manufacturing contributed to higher output, aided by lower input costs. Investment activity remained stable, driven by government infrastructure spending and private sector capital formation. Despite global uncertainties, these factors combined to support India’s strong real GDP expansion for the quarter.

questions.question: Who has been selected for a 4-year US astronaut training program leading to a 2029 space mission?
questions.explanation: Kunchala Kaivalya Reddy, a 17-year-old from Nidadavole in Andhra Pradesh, has earned a place in an elite four-year astronaut training program conducted by Titans Space Industries in Florida. Selected among 150 candidates from 36 countries, she represents the aspirations of India’s growing scientific spirit. Her training will involve spaceflight simulations, survival modules, technical lessons in orbital mechanics, and zero-gravity adaptation. Upon completion, she is slated to participate in a 2029 mission that will orbit Earth twice at about 300 km. Her achievement highlights both individual excellence and the increasing global presence of young Indian talent in space science.

questions.question: Who is invited as the Chief Guest for the Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2025 ceremony?
questions.explanation: Varsha Das, a renowned Gujarati writer, has been invited as the Chief Guest for the Bal Sahitya Puraskar 2025 ceremony. The event, scheduled for 14 November 2025, celebrates outstanding contributions to children’s literature across 24 Indian languages. The award spans various literary forms such as poetry, stories, novels, memoirs, and plays, highlighting the richness and diversity of children’s writing in India. Each awardee receives ₹50,000 along with a bronze plaque, making it a prestigious recognition. Varsha Das’s presence underscores the importance of literary influence and cultural contribution in shaping young readers.

questions.question: Which pair of space missions has contributed to refining estimates of Earth-like planet frequency, thereby supporting the Rare Earth Hypothesis?
questions.explanation: Kepler and the James Webb Telescope have significantly advanced the study of exoplanets by providing detailed data about distant planetary systems. Their observations help scientists estimate how frequently Earth-like planets occur in the galaxy. This evidence strengthens the Rare Earth Hypothesis, which suggests that while simple microbial life may be relatively common, complex life requires a highly specific combination of planetary conditions. These include stable orbital dynamics, a strong magnetic field, plate tectonics, and the presence of a large moon. By improving the understanding of how rare such conditions may be, the findings support the hypothesis that complex life is exceptionally uncommon.

questions.question: From which country is India set to receive 8 cheetahs under Project Cheetah?
questions.explanation: Botswana is contributing 8 cheetahs to support India’s Project Cheetah, a major conservation initiative aimed at reintroducing the species decades after their extinction in India in 1952. This donation strengthens not only India’s efforts to restore ecological balance in grassland ecosystems but also highlights the deepening environmental and diplomatic ties between India and Botswana. The cheetahs being transferred are significant for ensuring stronger genetic diversity and come from one of the world’s most stable wild cheetah populations. The move forms part of a broader conservation partnership, underscored by President Droupadi Murmu’s state visit and the scheduled symbolic handover ceremony in Gaborone.

questions.question: Which country, along with Australia, agreed to a new security treaty aimed at enhancing regional peace and stability?
questions.explanation: Indonesia collaborated with Australia to establish a new security treaty focused on strengthening regional peace and fostering closer cooperation between the two nations. The agreement outlines commitments for both sides to consult one another in the event of emerging security threats, reinforcing trust and strategic communication. It also includes provisions for regular high-level dialogues and enhanced defence interaction, reflecting a renewed warmth in bilateral relations. Although modeled on the 1995 agreement, this updated version does not impose mandatory joint action, allowing both countries flexibility while still deepening their strategic partnership in a rapidly evolving regional environment.

questions.question: Which state government has launched an incentive scheme featuring annual awards for top-performing sugar factories based on parameters like AI usage, financial health, and carbon footprint?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra has introduced a comprehensive incentive scheme aimed at boosting the performance and efficiency of sugar factories across the state. The scheme evaluates factories on nine diverse parameters, including operational efficiency, environmental responsibility, financial stability, and technological adoption such as the use of AI. By recognizing three cooperative and three private factories annually, the initiative encourages healthy competition and continuous improvement. A two-tier evaluation framework ensures transparency and fairness through dedicated Screening and Steering Committees. This structured assessment approach helps the state promote sustainable and innovative practices within the sugar industry.

questions.question: Which institution developed India’s first Quantum Diamond Microscope under the National Quantum Mission?
questions.explanation: IIT Bombay, through its P-Quest Group, developed India’s first Quantum Diamond Microscope, marking a major milestone in indigenous quantum technology. The microscope leverages nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond to perform advanced magnetic imaging with nanoscale precision. Its ability to visualise 3D magnetic fields using optically detected magnetic resonance makes it a powerful tool across scientific domains. Potential applications range from studying neural activity in neuroscience to analyzing magnetic properties of materials and performing non-destructive 3D mapping of semiconductor chips. This achievement strengthens India’s technological capabilities under the National Quantum Mission and advances research in cutting-edge quantum sensing technologies.

questions.question: Which country celebrated its 50th Independence anniversary attended by President Droupadi Murmu?
questions.explanation: Angola marked its 50th year of independence with significant global participation, including the historic first visit by an Indian President, Droupadi Murmu. The occasion also highlighted four decades of diplomatic ties between India and Angola, underscoring a growing partnership. During the visit, key areas such as governance, infrastructure development, defence cooperation, and the energy sector were appreciated and discussed. India further strengthened bilateral engagement by proposing a USD 200 million Line of Credit aimed at supporting joint defence and energy initiatives. This milestone celebration not only commemorated Angola’s independence but also reinforced a deepening India–Angola relationship.

questions.question: On which date will World Diabetes Day be observed in 2025?
questions.explanation: World Diabetes Day 2025 will be observed on November 14, a date chosen to honour Sir Frederick Banting, whose work led to the discovery of insulin one of the most significant medical breakthroughs for diabetes treatment. Celebrated globally, this day highlights the urgent need for improved diabetes awareness, prevention, and patient support. The theme for 2025, “Diabetes and Well-being,” emphasises the importance of holistic care, focusing not only on medical treatment but also on mental health, lifestyle balance, and long-term well-being. Organised by IDF and WHO, the campaign unites communities worldwide in the fight against diabetes.

questions.question: Which country signed a Letter of Exchange with India to expand rail freight connectivity through the Jogbani–Biratnagar link?
questions.explanation: India and Nepal recently signed a Letter of Exchange aimed at enhancing bilateral rail-based trade by expanding freight movement through the Jogbani–Biratnagar rail link. This agreement enables containerised and bulk cargo to move more efficiently and opens additional routes such as Kolkata–Jogbani, Kolkata–Nautanwa, and Visakhapatnam–Nautanwa. By improving multimodal logistics and offering more streamlined pathways for third-country trade, the pact significantly boosts economic cooperation between the two nations. Strengthened rail connectivity is expected to reduce transit time, improve trade volumes, and deepen strategic and economic partnership between India and Nepal.

questions.question: Which country completed its first-ever government transaction using the Digital Dirham in under two minutes?
questions.explanation: The UAE achieved a major milestone by executing its first government transaction using the Digital Dirham, a central bank digital currency issued by the Central Bank of the UAE. Completed in less than two minutes through the mBridge settlement platform, the event demonstrated the nation’s readiness to adopt next-generation financial systems. This development supports the country’s broader Financial Infrastructure Transformation Programme, which aims to enhance transparency, efficiency, and financial inclusion. By embracing secure, regulated digital currency systems and collaborating with other central banks on cross-border digital settlements, the UAE continues to strengthen its position as a leading global hub for digital finance and technological innovation.

questions.question: Which country ended its longest-ever government shutdown after 42 days when a temporary funding bill was signed into law?
questions.explanation: The United States ended its longest government shutdown after a 42-day political standoff, which severely disrupted federal operations and affected hundreds of thousands of government employees. The shutdown was rooted in disagreements between Democrats and Republicans over healthcare subsidy provisions linked to the Affordable Care Act. Progress stalled in the Senate due to the 60-vote requirement, but bipartisan support emerged when eight Democratic senators crossed party lines, allowing the bill to move forward. Following congressional approval, President Donald Trump signed a temporary funding bill that reopened government services. Although the measure provided only short-term relief, it restored essential services and allowed federal agencies to resume normal operations while budget negotiations continued.

questions.question: Which country was elected to UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere Council for the 2025–2029 term, showcasing leadership in sustainability and biodiversity?
questions.explanation: Oman has been selected to serve on UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Council for the 2025–2029 term, reflecting its expanding role in global environmental stewardship. This position allows Oman to contribute to advancing protected area management, climate research initiatives, and long-term sustainability objectives aligned with its Vision 2040 strategy. The country’s commitment is further reinforced through significant conservation sites such as the Al-Sareen Reserve and Al Jabal Al Akhdar, which highlight ongoing efforts to preserve biodiversity. This election strengthens Oman’s influence in shaping international discussions on ecological preservation and sustainable development.

questions.question: In which location was Operation Akhand Prahar conducted under Exercise Trishul to test India’s multi-domain warfare capabilities?
questions.explanation: Operation Akhand Prahar was carried out in Jaisalmer as part of Exercise Trishul, demonstrating India’s ability to coordinate across multiple domains of warfare. The exercise involved close synchronisation between the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force, highlighting improved joint operational readiness. It also validated the capabilities of the newly established RUDRA Brigade, an integrated formation combining infantry, armoured units, mechanised forces, and air defence assets. Advanced technologies such as drones, counter-drone systems, and indigenous equipment further strengthened the exercise’s objective of showcasing next-generation combat preparedness and modernised battlefield effectiveness.

questions.question: Which city is set to host the 22nd All India Annual TDS Conference organised by the CBDT?
questions.explanation: Bhopal has been chosen as the venue for the 22nd All India Annual TDS Conference, an important national gathering organised by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT). The event brings together senior tax administrators, including Principal Chief Commissioners, Chief Commissioners, Directors General, and other top officials responsible for shaping TDS policies. The conference will focus on recent amendments made to the Income Tax Act, 2025, promote voluntary tax compliance, and highlight new digital tools for monitoring and data-driven enforcement. By hosting this conference, Bhopal becomes a key center for discussions aimed at improving transparency, simplifying regulations, and strengthening India’s TDS administration system.

questions.question: In which region was the Nyoma Airbase inaugurated by the IAF Chief, strengthening India’s strategic presence near the LAC?
questions.explanation: The Nyoma Airbase was inaugurated in Ladakh, a region of immense strategic importance due to its proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC) with China. Situated at an altitude of 13,700 feet, the airbase significantly enhances India’s air combat readiness and logistical capabilities in high-altitude terrain. With a 2.7-km runway capable of handling aircraft such as the C-130J and various fighter jets, the base allows quicker troop movement, improved surveillance, and rapid response to frontier developments. Developed by the Border Roads Organisation, the project also showcased women-led engineering excellence. The airbase stands as a major leap in strengthening India’s frontier infrastructure and operational preparedness.

questions.question: Which cooperative organization partnered with BBSSL to strengthen India’s potato value chain through a comprehensive seed-to-market strategy?
questions.explanation: Banas Dairy, Asia’s largest dairy cooperative and a key member of the Amul network, partnered with Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) to enhance India’s potato value chain. Through this MoU, Banas Dairy is contributing technical expertise, tissue culture facilities, aeroponic systems, and strong market-linkage support. This collaboration aligns with the national vision of “Sahakar se Samriddhi,” which encourages cooperation among cooperatives to empower farmers. By focusing on disease-free seed potato production, scientific cultivation methods, and contract farming, the partnership aims to reduce crop losses, increase productivity, uplift rural incomes, and build a more resilient agricultural value chain.

questions.question: When is Children’s Day celebrated in India in 2025?
questions.explanation: Children’s Day in India is observed every year on November 14 to honour the birth anniversary of Jawaharlal Nehru, who emphasised the importance of children’s education, development, and welfare. Celebrating this day reinforces the nation’s responsibility toward nurturing young minds and ensuring their rights and opportunities. In 2025, the theme “For Every Child, Every Right” highlights the commitment to protecting and promoting children’s well-being across all domains. Schools across the country typically organize cultural events and engaging activities that recognize children’s potential and encourage society to create an environment where they can thrive and grow holistically.

questions.question: In which state did Amit Shah inaugurate the Motibhai R. Chaudhary Sagar Sainik School and the Sagar Organic Plant?
questions.explanation: The Motibhai R. Chaudhary Sagar Sainik School and the Sagar Organic Plant were inaugurated in Gujarat by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, with Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel in attendance. The Sainik School, developed under the PPP model as part of the initiative to establish 100 new Sainik Schools, is designed to prepare young students in the state for careers in the Armed Forces. Alongside this, the Sagar Organic Plant, with a production capacity of 30 MT per day and certifications from NPOP and APEDA, will support the expansion of Amul’s organic product line, boosting the region’s agricultural and economic ecosystem.

questions.question: Which state became the first in India to fully implement the amended Bharat Net Scheme?
questions.explanation: Punjab became the first state in India to fully implement the amended Bharat Net Scheme, marking a major step forward in enhancing digital connectivity across rural regions. With the scheme’s rollout, the state enabled live monitoring of sensitive border areas while extending broadband services to 43 shadow zones that previously lacked dependable connectivity. The initiative aims to cover every village by the end of November 2025, ensuring digital inclusion for households and Gram Panchayats. Through improved access to e-health, e-governance, and digital services, Punjab is strengthening grassroots development and building a more connected rural ecosystem.

questions.question: In which state did the Union Finance Minister unveil new development initiatives including an Industrial Training Institute in Kiphire?
questions.explanation: The Union Finance Minister launched several developmental initiatives in Nagaland, reflecting the government's focus on strengthening infrastructure and financial inclusion in the Northeast. A new Industrial Training Institute was inaugurated in Kiphire to enhance local skill development. Additionally, ₹9 lakh was released under SBI’s CSR initiatives to support training programmes. During a Credit Outreach Programme, nine new bank branches were virtually launched across the region, and sanction letters were issued to beneficiaries. Loans totalling ₹28.02 crore were distributed to 350 individuals, demonstrating a significant push toward economic empowerment and improved access to banking services in the state.

questions.question: Which organisation has developed the next-generation man-portable autonomous underwater vehicles for mine detection?
questions.explanation: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), through its Naval Science & Technological Laboratory (NSTL) in Visakhapatnam, has successfully created next-generation Man-Portable Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (MP-AUVs). These systems are designed to significantly enhance underwater mine countermeasure capabilities. Equipped with side scan sonar, underwater cameras, deep learning-based target recognition, and acoustic communication, the AUVs enable accurate detection and classification of mine-like objects while coordinating effectively with multiple units. Field trials validated their ability to autonomously execute complex missions with minimal human involvement. This development strengthens India’s underwater defence preparedness and supports the nation’s broader goal of indigenising critical military technologies.

questions.question: Which port recently saw the launch of ₹1,500 crore modernisation projects during its Golden Jubilee 2025 celebration?
questions.explanation: The ₹1,500 crore modernisation initiative was launched at New Mangalore Port during its Golden Jubilee celebrations in 2025. This port, located at Panambur in Mangaluru along the Arabian Sea, holds the distinction of being Karnataka’s only major port. Recognised as India’s 9th major port in 1974 and inaugurated the following year, it has grown into one of the top 10 ports in the country. Its all-weather deep inner harbour enables efficient maritime operations year-round, and the new modernisation projects aim to further enhance capacity, improve logistics, and support regional economic growth.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the United States Ambassador to India on November 11, 2025?
questions.explanation: Sergio Gor assumed office as the United States Ambassador to India on November 11, 2025, marking a notable moment in the expanding Indo-US relationship. At 38, he brings extensive experience from his previous role as Director of Presidential Personnel in the Trump administration, where he oversaw significant staffing decisions and strategic coordination. His appointment was confirmed by the US Senate in October 2025, and his swearing-in ceremony at the Oval Office was attended by top US leadership, reflecting the importance of the India-US partnership. Gor aims to strengthen cooperation in defence, regional security, trade, technology, and supply chain resilience.

questions.question: Who was the 114-year-old Padma Shri environmentalist known for planting hundreds of banyan trees?
questions.explanation: Saalumarada Thimmakka was an iconic environmentalist admired for her extraordinary contribution to afforestation. She became widely known for planting 385 banyan trees along a 4.5-kilometre stretch, a feat that earned her the name “Saalumarada,” meaning a row of trees. Over her long lifetime, she received numerous prestigious recognitions, including the Padma Shri in 2019, the Nadoja Award in 2010, the National Citizen Award in 1995, and the Indira Priyadarshini Vrikshamitra Award in 1997. Her work became a symbol of dedication to nature conservation, inspiring many to engage in environmental protection and sustainable practices.

questions.question: Which company plans to set up India’s largest 10 GW solar wafers and ingots manufacturing plant?
questions.explanation: Tata Power has announced a major step toward strengthening India’s renewable energy manufacturing ecosystem by planning a 10 GW solar wafers and ingots plant. This facility will complete the company’s solar manufacturing chain, as it already operates around 4.9 GW of integrated cell and module production capacity. By moving into upstream components such as ingots and wafers, the company aims to reduce the nation’s reliance on imports and support the Make-in-India initiative. The project also aligns with government incentives promoting domestic manufacturing and clean energy. Once operational, it will significantly enhance India’s capability to build a self-reliant solar supply chain.

questions.question: What is the name of the AI-based system introduced by Indian Railways to monitor wagon door locking status in real time?
questions.explanation: The Indian Railways has introduced an advanced AI-powered system called DRISHTI to enhance the safety and monitoring of freight operations. This system uses real-time surveillance supported by computer vision technology to keep track of the locking status of wagon doors, ensuring better security and operational efficiency. DRISHTI was created through collaborative innovation between the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) and IIT Guwahati – TIDF. By integrating artificial intelligence with railway logistics, the system aims to reduce human error, improve monitoring accuracy, and offer a proactive approach to safeguarding freight movement across the network.

questions.question: Who was felicitated by the UP Police for her achievements in the Women’s ODI World Cup?
questions.explanation: Deepti Sharma, who earned the title of Player of the Tournament in the Women’s ODI World Cup, was honoured at the UP Police Headquarters in Gomtinagar Extension. Her recognition reflects her outstanding contributions to Indian cricket as well as her commitment to public service, having recently joined the Uttar Pradesh Police as a Deputy Superintendent of Police under the sports quota. DGP Rajeev Krishna commended her for bringing pride to both the state and the nation. This felicitation highlights the growing support for athletes who excel internationally while also serving in administrative or public roles.

questions.question: Which countries will jointly host the 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup?
questions.explanation: Belgium and the Netherlands have been selected to jointly host the 2026 FIH Hockey World Cup, creating the first-ever edition that is both dual-host and dual-gender. The event will take place from 15–30 August 2026 and will feature tournaments for both men and women. Additionally, this edition introduces the first ParaHockey World Cup, expanding inclusivity within the sport. The competition format has also been updated to include 16 teams per gender, with a system that allows top teams to carry forward results into a second group stage, ultimately determining the semi-finalists.

questions.question: What is the new reduced GI tag application fee aimed at supporting tribal artisans and traditional crafts?
questions.explanation: The government has lowered the Geographical Indication (GI) tag application fee from ₹5,000 to ₹1,000 to make the process more accessible for tribal artisans and those engaged in traditional crafts. This reduction is intended to encourage more communities to register their unique products, thereby helping preserve cultural heritage and promoting regional identity. GI tags play an essential role in safeguarding items whose reputation, quality, or characteristics are linked to their place of origin. Products such as Kannadippaya, Apatani textile, Marthandam honey, Lepcha Tungbuk, Bodo Aronai, Ambaji Marble, and Badri cow ghee exemplify this cultural and geographical significance.

questions.question: Where was the 30th CII Partnership Summit 2025 inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The 30th CII Partnership Summit 2025 was inaugurated in Visakhapatnam, a major industrial and port city in Andhra Pradesh. This location was chosen as the state is emerging as a fast-growing investment hub with strong support from both the central and state governments. The summit brought together global delegates, industry leaders and policymakers to deepen discussions around trade, technology and investment. With over 2,500 participants from 77 countries, the event highlighted Andhra Pradesh’s ambition to accelerate economic growth through sectors like drones, aerospace, semiconductors and defence. Visakhapatnam served as a strategic venue showcasing the region’s potential, infrastructure and investor-friendly governance.

questions.question: What was the year-on-year bank credit growth reported for October 2025?
questions.explanation: The bank credit growth for October 2025 stood at 11.3%, reflecting a slowdown in lending activity across the financial sector. This moderation is linked to factors such as reduced loan demand, cautious lending behaviour by banks, and broader global economic uncertainties. Slower credit growth can impact industries, MSMEs, NBFCs and retail borrowers by delaying investment cycles and affecting expansion plans.
