questions.explanation: The ACITI Partnership brings together India, Australia, and Canada to enhance collaboration in critical and emerging technologies, green innovation, and resilient supply chains. This trilateral initiative aims to leverage the combined technological strengths and strategic priorities of the three nations. By focusing on green energy solutions, responsible AI development, and diversification of critical mineral supply chains, the partnership supports broader goals of sustainability and net-zero emissions. It also promotes joint research, innovation-driven cooperation, and coordinated policy frameworks. The initiative represents a long-term vision for technological progress, economic resilience, and shared global leadership in addressing future challenges.

questions.question: Which country won the inaugural Blind Women’s T20 World Cup 2025 by defeating Nepal in Colombo?
questions.explanation: India secured a landmark achievement by winning the first-ever Blind Women’s T20 World Cup 2025, held in Colombo, Sri Lanka. The team showcased exceptional skill and determination, successfully chasing Nepal’s target of 115 runs in just 12 overs and winning by seven wickets. This historic victory highlights India’s growing prominence in inclusive and disability sports, reinforcing its commitment to promoting equal opportunities for athletes with visual impairments. The triumph also sets a strong foundation for future international competitions, increased visibility for blind women’s cricket, and expanded support systems such as infrastructure, tournaments, and sponsorships that can further elevate the sport globally.

questions.question: Which Indian Institute of Management received AMBA accreditation and 4 Palmes of Excellence in the Eduniversal 2025 Rankings?
questions.explanation: IIM Ranchi earned international recognition by receiving the prestigious AMBA accreditation, placing it among the top 2% of business schools worldwide. This accreditation reflects excellence in curriculum innovation, teaching quality, student learning experience, and career outcomes. Additionally, the institute was awarded 4 Palmes of Excellence in the Eduniversal Best Business Schools Ranking 2025, signifying significant international influence and growing global engagement. These achievements highlight IIM Ranchi’s commitment to developing globally competent leaders and expanding its international collaborations, while maintaining a strong reputation within India’s competitive management education landscape.

questions.question: Which country was declared polio-free by WHO after successfully ending its type-2 polio outbreak?
questions.explanation: Indonesia achieved a major public health milestone when WHO declared the end of its type-2 polio outbreak. This success followed extensive immunisation efforts, including the administration of more than 60 million vaccine doses, multiple nOPV2 campaigns, and strengthened routine immunisation. The rollout of the hexavalent vaccine and the improvement of IPV coverage from 63% to 73% in 2024 played an important role. Although the government continues to highlight risks in areas with low vaccination coverage, the achievement reinforces the Western Pacific region’s broader polio-free status and demonstrates Indonesia’s commitment to disease prevention and strong public health systems.

questions.question: Who has been nominated as the next Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)?
questions.explanation: Justice Vikram Nath, a sitting judge of the Supreme Court of India, has been nominated as the new Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The nomination was made by the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. This role is significant because NALSA is responsible for ensuring free legal aid and promoting access to justice for the disadvantaged sections of society. Justice Nath succeeds Justice Surya Kant, who recently assumed the position of the 53rd Chief Justice of India. The appointment highlights continuity in judicial leadership and reinforces India’s commitment to strengthening legal aid mechanisms nationwide.

questions.question: Who won the women’s title at the Indian Open squash tournament in Indore?
questions.explanation: Anahat Singh secured the women’s title at the Indian Open squash tournament after a hard-fought 3–2 victory over Joshna Chinappa in the final. At just 17 years old, she is India’s top-ranked women’s squash player and entered the tournament as the top seed, demonstrating her rising stature in the sport. Her journey to the title included a challenging semi-final win against Irish third seed Hannah Craig. The final match highlighted her determination, skill, and composure under pressure, establishing her as one of the most promising young athletes in Indian squash.

questions.question: In which state did the Dr Talimeren Ao Junior Girls National Football Championship 2025–26 (Tier-2) begin?
questions.explanation: The Dr Talimeren Ao Junior Girls National Football Championship 2025–26 (Tier-2) commenced at the Chümoukedima Football Stadium in Nagaland, marking a significant milestone for the state. This edition is especially notable because it is the first time Nagaland has hosted a national-level football tournament. The event also carries cultural and historical importance, as it honours Dr. Talimeren Ao, a renowned footballer and physician from Nagaland. By hosting this championship, the state showcases its growing sports infrastructure and commitment to promoting youth football, while also celebrating the legacy of one of its most respected sporting icons.

questions.question: What GDP growth rate has S&P projected for India for FY2025-26?
questions.explanation: S&P Global Ratings has projected that India will record a GDP growth rate of 6.5% in FY2025-26. This projection reflects confidence in India’s strong domestic consumption, expected tax cuts, and supportive monetary policy, all of which are anticipated to boost demand and investment. The growth forecast positions India as one of the fastest-growing major economies, even amid global challenges such as inflation and geopolitical uncertainties. Additionally, the outlook suggests that internal economic drivers will continue to play a central role in sustaining growth, with potential policy developments like an India–US trade agreement—offering further momentum despite risks like US tariff pressures.

questions.question: Which country won its fourth Davis Cup title with a 2–0 victory over Spain?
questions.explanation: Italy clinched its fourth Davis Cup title by defeating Spain 2–0 in a dominant performance on home soil. The victory was secured through strong singles matches played by Matteo Berrettini and Flavio Cobolli. Berrettini delivered an impressive win over Pablo Carreno Busta, while Cobolli completed the triumph with a hard-fought comeback against Jaume Munar. This achievement also marked a historic milestone, as Italy became the first team since the United States to win three Davis Cups in a row. The result highlights Italy’s growing strength and consistency in international tennis competitions.

questions.question: Which Indian organization will lead the final assembly, testing, and quality assurance for the HAMMER precision-guided weapon under the new JV?
questions.explanation: Bharat Electronics Limited is set to play a key role in the new joint venture with Safran Electronics and Defence of France by taking charge of the final assembly, testing, and quality assurance of the HAMMER precision-guided air-to-ground weapon. This collaboration signifies an important step toward enhancing indigenous defence manufacturing capabilities. By handling crucial stages of the weapon’s production, BEL strengthens India’s technological self-reliance and supports the broader vision of developing advanced defence systems within the country.

questions.question: On which date is the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women observed each year?
questions.explanation: The International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women is observed every year on November 25. This date commemorates the assassination of the Mirabal Sisters in 1960, whose activism against dictatorship made them symbols of resistance and courage. The observance marks the beginning of the global 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence, culminating on December 10, Human Rights Day. The annual campaign brings together governments, communities, and global organisations to address violence in all its forms—physical, emotional, economic, and now increasingly digital. The 2025 theme emphasizes combating online abuse, reflecting the evolving landscape of threats faced by women worldwide.

questions.question: In which state did Union Minister Pralhad Joshi inaugurate a pellet plant and lay the foundation stone for the K2 Bio-Ethanol plant?
questions.explanation: The pellet plant and the K2 Bio-Ethanol plant were inaugurated in Rewari, Haryana, marking a significant step toward sustainable environmental practices in the region. The pellet plant aims to produce 240 tonnes of biomass pellets per day using stubble, helping reduce the issue of crop residue burning. By converting agricultural waste into ethanol and biomass pellets, the project supports India’s E20 Mission and long-term Net Zero 2070 commitments. Such initiatives not only promote cleaner energy alternatives but also create local economic opportunities while addressing environmental challenges linked to air pollution and waste management.

questions.question: Which city served as the primary host for the 5th Khelo India University Games 2025?
questions.explanation: Jaipur served as the main host city for the 5th Khelo India University Games, with the grand inauguration held at the iconic Sawai Mansingh Stadium on November 24, 2025. The city hosted major sporting disciplines such as athletics, shooting, archery, badminton, and hockey. This edition marked the first time Rajasthan hosted the Games, extending events across multiple cities including Udaipur, Ajmer, Jodhpur, Bikaner, Kota, and Bharatpur. With nearly 7,000 participants, the event celebrated youth sports, Rajasthan’s cultural heritage, and India’s commitment to nurturing university-level athletes under the Khelo India initiative.

questions.question: In which country is the Hayli Gubbi volcano located?
questions.explanation: The Hayli Gubbi volcano is located in Ethiopia’s Rift Valley, a region well known for its intense tectonic activity as part of the larger Erta Ale volcanic range. This volcano, dormant for nearly 12,000 years, recently erupted, sending massive ash plumes high into the atmosphere. Due to strong upper-level winds, the ash drifted thousands of kilometres toward India and Pakistan, affecting major aviation routes that connect East Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia. The eruption’s geographic location makes it particularly significant, as disruptions in this corridor impact international flights, necessitating precautionary advisories from aviation authorities and meteorological agencies.

questions.question: What is India’s overall rank in the Commitment to Development Index (CDI) 2025?
questions.explanation: India holds the 36th position in the Commitment to Development Index (CDI) 2025, which evaluates how effectively countries contribute to global development through a variety of policy measures rather than focusing solely on foreign aid. The index, published by the Centre for Global Development, assesses eight different policy components, offering a comprehensive perspective on each nation’s developmental engagement. India’s placement at 36th among 38 countries highlights both its strengths and areas needing improvement. While the nation demonstrates progress in certain policy areas, it still faces challenges that limit its overall ranking compared to the top performers like Sweden, Germany, and Norway.

questions.question: Which country launched a set of classified military satellites using the Angara-1.2 launch vehicle?
questions.explanation: Russia successfully deployed a set of undisclosed military satellites using its Angara-1.2 light launch vehicle, highlighting its ongoing efforts to strengthen space-based defence capabilities. The launch took place from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome in the Arkhangelsk region, which is the northernmost spaceport in the world. The operation was executed by a combat crew from the Russian Aerospace Forces, reflecting the strategic importance of military satellites in surveillance, reconnaissance, and secure communications. This development underscores Russia’s commitment to expanding its military presence in space and enhancing national security through advanced satellite technology.

questions.question: In which country was the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol 2025 held?
questions.explanation: The ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol 2025 took place from 6 to 18 November 2025 in Cairo, the capital of Egypt. The event, organised by the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF), featured 720 shooters from 70 National Olympic Committees competing in individual and team rifle and pistol events. India performed strongly, finishing third in the medal tally with 13 medals. Hosting the championship in Egypt highlighted the country’s role in facilitating major international shooting competitions and provided a platform for record-breaking performances by shooters from around the world. Egypt’s selection as the host also emphasised its infrastructure and capability in global sports events.

questions.question: On which date is National Milk Day celebrated in India each year?
questions.explanation: National Milk Day is observed annually on November 26 to honour the birth anniversary of Dr. Verghese Kurien, the Father of India’s White Revolution. The day celebrates his pivotal role in transforming India from a milk-deficient nation to the world’s largest milk producer, contributing nearly 25% of global milk output. National Milk Day highlights achievements in dairy production, livestock care, and rural livelihoods, as well as initiatives like Operation Flood, the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, and the National AI Programme. The observance also emphasises women’s empowerment in dairy cooperatives and India’s advancements in infrastructure, technology, and GST reforms within the dairy sector.

questions.question: On which date is National Constitution Day observed in India each year?
questions.explanation: National Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Divas, is observed every year on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly in 1949. The day honours the efforts of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and other framers of the Constitution, highlighting the values of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. It aims to deepen constitutional literacy among citizens, especially students and public servants, by encouraging engagement with India’s democratic principles. National Constitution Day also reinforces the importance of fundamental rights, duties, and the moral foundations of governance in contemporary Indian society.

questions.question: In which host city did the Indian shooting team win 16 medals at the 2025 Deaflympics?
questions.explanation: The Indian shooting team delivered an outstanding performance at the 2025 Deaflympics, securing a total of 16 medals—7 gold, 6 silver, and 3 bronze. These achievements took place in Tokyo, where the athletes competed over ten days of intense events. The results highlighted India's growing strength in Deaflympics shooting disciplines, with standout performers like Mahit Sandhu contributing multiple medals. This medal haul also represented significant progress compared to the previous edition in Brazil, underlining improved preparation, better training systems, and the rising prominence of Indian shooters on the global stage.

questions.question: Which state declared Anandpur Sahib, Talwandi Sabo, and the Galiara around the Golden Temple as holy cities?
questions.explanation: Punjab declared Anandpur Sahib, Talwandi Sabo, and the Galiara surrounding the Golden Temple as holy cities through a unanimous resolution passed in a historic Assembly session held at Anandpur Sahib. This decision reflects the state’s commitment to preserving the sanctity of significant Sikh religious sites. The resolution also imposed a complete ban on liquor, meat, and tobacco within these holy areas to maintain their spiritual and cultural purity. The session was convened to commemorate the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur, emphasizing his ideals of sacrifice, religious freedom, and universal brotherhood.

questions.question: Which team won the Women’s Kabaddi World Cup 2025 in the final?
questions.explanation: India’s women’s kabaddi team won the 2025 Women’s Kabaddi World Cup, defeating Chinese Taipei 35–28 in the final held in Dhaka, Bangladesh. This victory marked India’s second consecutive World Cup title, reinforcing its dominance in international women’s kabaddi. The team combined disciplined defence, calculated raids, and effective coaching strategies to maintain control throughout the match. Key contributions came from captain Ritu Negi, vice-captain Pushpa Rana, and standout raider Sanju Devi, whose performance in the final earned widespread recognition. The triumph reflects India’s consistent preparation, tactical execution, and emergence as a global powerhouse in women’s kabaddi.

questions.question: Which country participates with India in the 19th edition of Exercise Suryakiran?
questions.explanation: Exercise Suryakiran is a bilateral military training exercise conducted between India and Nepal, aimed at strengthening cooperation and interoperability between their armed forces. The 19th edition of the exercise commenced in Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand, continuing the tradition of alternating locations each year. Launched in 2011, this annual exercise allows both armies to engage in joint drills, share operational expertise, and enhance coordination in mountain warfare and other tactical operations. Such exercises play a key role in reinforcing defence diplomacy, fostering mutual trust, and promoting regional security in the strategically important Himalayan region.

questions.question: Which state launched the ‘Rythanna Meekosam’ initiative to empower farmers in November 2025?
questions.explanation: The ‘Rythanna Meekosam’ initiative was launched by the Andhra Pradesh government on November 24, 2025, aiming to support farmers through a comprehensive Five-Point Formula. The program focuses on water security, demand-based cultivation, agri-tech adoption, food processing expansion, and government backing. It also includes financial support, technology adoption, and market linkages to modernise agriculture and improve farm profitability. Spearheaded by Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu, the initiative seeks to create a sustainable and resilient agricultural ecosystem in Andhra Pradesh, directly benefiting farmers across the state.

questions.question: Which Indian naval ship arrived in Colombo to participate in the International Fleet Review 2025?
questions.explanation: INS Vikrant, India’s first fully indigenous aircraft carrier, arrived at the Port of Colombo to take part in the International Fleet Review (IFR) 2025. The event is part of the Sri Lanka Navy’s 75th-anniversary celebrations and showcases naval capabilities and regional maritime cooperation by bringing together fleets from multiple countries. Commissioned in 2022, INS Vikrant represents a significant achievement in India’s naval self-reliance and technological advancement. Its participation in IFR 2025 highlights India’s commitment to strengthening maritime diplomacy, interoperability with international navies, and projecting strategic presence in the Indian Ocean region.

questions.question: Which organization partnered with UNICEF to secure an affordable malaria vaccine deal?
questions.explanation: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, partnered with UNICEF to announce a breakthrough pricing agreement for the R21/Matrix-M™ malaria vaccine on November 24, 2025. This deal lowers the vaccine cost to US$ 2.99 per dose, saves up to $90 million, and enables 7 million additional children to be vaccinated by 2030. Gavi’s role includes advance financing and supporting vaccine delivery in over 24 African countries, which bear 70% of the global malaria burden. The collaboration ensures greater accessibility, equity, and rapid deployment of life-saving vaccines in high-need regions.

questions.question: Which institution launched the Impact RISE initiative focusing on sustainable technology and skilling?
questions.explanation: IIT Kharagpur has launched Impact RISE, an initiative designed to promote sustainable technology, modern management practices, and broader societal transformation. Built on four key pillars—research, innovation, skilling, and entrepreneurship—the programme aims to create a collaborative environment that nurtures solutions for long-term development. A significant component of Impact RISE includes missions that address climate resilience in sensitive regions such as the Sundarbans. By integrating academic excellence with real-world challenges, the initiative seeks to empower communities, drive inclusive growth, and support the nation’s sustainability goals through skill-building and innovation-driven approaches.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the ‘Nayi Chetna 4.0’ campaign launched by the Centre?
questions.explanation: ‘Nayi Chetna 4.0’ is a national campaign launched to strengthen gender equality and empower women across communities. Led by Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and organised by DAY-NRLM under the Ministry of Rural Development, the month-long initiative focuses on encouraging community-level action and awareness to combat gender-based violence. The campaign aims to inspire collective responsibility, promote safer environments for women, and reinforce the importance of equal opportunities. By engaging rural communities, the programme works toward long-term social transformation and supports broader national goals related to gender justice and empowerment.

questions.question: Which organisation approved the $400 million loan to enhance climate-resilient and inclusive road infrastructure in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank approved a $400 million results-based lending program aimed at strengthening rural and state road networks across Maharashtra. The initiative focuses on improving nearly 2,577 km of rural roads and 350 km of state highways, enhancing access to markets, education, healthcare, and public services for more than 1.7 million people. It also integrates climate-resilient designs, multi-hazard risk assessments, and advanced maintenance systems to address extreme weather challenges. Additionally, the project emphasizes gender inclusion, youth engagement, road safety enhancements through iRAP methodologies, and the development of digital planning systems, ensuring comprehensive and sustainable regional growth.

questions.question: Which organisation approved $776 million in funding for reforms in Punjab and Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: The World Bank approved a total of $776 million to support major reform-oriented projects in Punjab and Maharashtra. The funding is divided between two key initiatives: the POISE project in Punjab aimed at improving education quality through digital tools, teacher training, and performance-based systems, and the POCRA Phase II project in Maharashtra designed to promote climate-resilient agriculture using precision-farming technologies. These projects collectively aim to benefit more than 60 lakh people, including students, farmers, and early childhood learners. With long-term loan tenures and a strong emphasis on innovation, inclusion, and sustainability, the World Bank intends to drive measurable improvements in learning outcomes and agricultural resilience.

questions.question: In which Indian state were breast milk samples found to contain detectable levels of uranium according to a recent study?
questions.explanation: A recent Scientific Reports study identified the presence of uranium (U-238) in breast milk samples collected from multiple districts in Bihar. Researchers used ICP-MS technology to test 40 samples, all of which showed detectable levels of uranium, raising concerns about potential exposure risks for infants. The highest concentrations were found in districts like Katihar and Khagaria, reaching up to 5.25 µg/L. These findings highlight the need for thorough investigation into environmental contamination sources, improved water safety measures, and targeted public health interventions to protect vulnerable populations, especially nursing mothers and infants.

questions.question: Who delivered an outstanding performance by winning eight consecutive games at the UK Women’s Blitz Championship?
questions.explanation: Bodhana Sivanandan, a remarkable 10-year-old chess prodigy from Harrow, London, delivered an extraordinary performance at the UK Women’s Blitz Championship by defeating experienced adult players in eight consecutive games. Her success in the event elevated her into the ranks of the top 50 female blitz players worldwide, highlighting her exceptional skill and maturity at such a young age. She also holds the distinction of becoming the youngest ever Woman International Master (WIM) at the age of nine, further showcasing her rapid rise and immense potential within the global chess community.

questions.question: Which organisation has set up a four-member committee for cadre restructuring to improve efficiency and services?
questions.explanation: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has established a four-member committee to undertake comprehensive cadre restructuring with the goal of improving operational efficiency and service delivery. Led by BP Sharma, the committee will evaluate the current organisational structure, identify gaps, streamline workflows, and propose reforms that align with the organisation’s growing responsibilities in a rapidly digitising ecosystem. With rising demands from EPF subscribers and new service expansions to gig and unorganised sector workers, the restructuring aims to ensure timely claim processing, enhanced grievance redressal, and improved customer support. The committee is expected to submit its detailed recommendations by March 31, 2026.

questions.question: Which state approved the formation of three new districts Polavaram, Markapuram, and Madanapalle raising its total to 29?
questions.explanation: The Andhra Pradesh government approved the creation of three new districts Polavaram, Markapuram, and Madanapalle bringing the total number of districts in the state to 29. This restructuring was cleared by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and also included the establishment of five new revenue divisions: Nakkapalli, Addanki, Pileru, Banaganapalle, and Madakasira. Additionally, a new mandal named Pedda Harivanam was created by carving it out of Adoni in Kurnool district. The decision aims to improve administrative efficiency, enhance governance, and ensure better access to public services across the state.

questions.question: Who has been appointed the official tournament ambassador for the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma has been appointed as the official ambassador for the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026, reflecting his exceptional legacy and achievements in the T20 format. As a two-time T20 World Cup champion in 2007 and 2024, and the captain who led India to the 2024 title, he has cemented his status as one of the greatest performers in the shortest format. His impressive tally of 4,231 T20I runs further strengthens his reputation, making him an ideal representative for a tournament jointly hosted by India and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Which city has been officially confirmed as the host of the 2030 Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad has secured the opportunity to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, marking a significant achievement for India on the global sporting stage. The decision was finalised during the Commonwealth Sport’s General Assembly in Glasgow, where Ahmedabad’s bid surpassed that of Abuja, Nigeria. With most of the venues already prepared and funding secured, officials have expressed strong confidence in delivering a well-organised event. The Games are expected to feature 15 to 17 sports and will align with the centenary celebrations of the Commonwealth Games Movement. This hosting decision also strengthens India’s long-term ambition to bid for the 2036 Summer Olympics.

questions.question: What is the name of the cyclonic storm approaching the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coast in late November 2025?
questions.explanation: Cyclone Ditwah is the cyclonic storm forming over the southwest Bay of Bengal and moving toward the coastal regions of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and southern Andhra Pradesh. It intensified from a deep depression into a cyclonic storm on November 27, 2025, and prompted the IMD to issue an orange alert for Puducherry from November 28 to December 1. The system’s projected path places several districts of Andhra Pradesh under the risk of heavy rainfall and strong winds. With increasing post-monsoon cyclonic activity in the North Indian Ocean, Ditwah has become the third storm of the season and underscores the need for enhanced disaster preparedness.

questions.question: According to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) Annual Article IV Consultation, what is the projected GDP growth rate for India in the fiscal year 2025–26?
questions.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects India’s GDP growth at 6.6% for the fiscal year 2025–26, reflecting strong domestic demand, strategic reforms, and resilience against global economic uncertainties. This comes after a 6.5% growth in FY 2024–25 and a robust 7.8% expansion in Q1 of 2025–26. Key factors supporting this growth include GST reforms, which improve tax compliance and fiscal stability, as well as public infrastructure investment, digital transformation, and formalisation of the economy. Structural reforms in labour, land, education, health, and finance are also expected to sustain long-term growth.

questions.question: In which city is the $11 billion AI-native data centre campus planned to be built by 2030?
questions.explanation: A joint venture named Digital Connexion, involving Brookfield, Reliance Industries, and Digital Realty, announced a $11 billion investment to establish a 1 GW AI-native data centre campus in Visakhapatnam by 2030. Spanning 400 acres, the facility is designed specifically for AI workloads, equipped with GPUs, TPUs, and advanced AI processors. Its modular infrastructure will include redundant power systems and renewable-integrated cooling to ensure operational efficiency and sustainability. This investment highlights Visakhapatnam’s emergence as a key hub for high-tech infrastructure and AI-driven innovation in India, contributing significantly to the country’s digital and technological growth.

questions.question: Which AI tool developed by Indian scientists analyses cancer at the molecular level for personalised treatment?
questions.explanation: OncoMark is an AI-powered diagnostic tool developed by Indian researchers from the S N Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences in collaboration with Ashoka University. It maps cancer’s molecular hallmarks to provide highly personalised treatment strategies and more precise diagnosis. Unlike conventional staging methods, OncoMark identifies key biological programs such as metastasis, immune evasion, genomic instability, and uncontrolled proliferation, enabling individualised therapy plans. Trained on 3.1 million single cells across 14 cancer types and validated on 20,000 patient samples, it achieves over 99% internal accuracy and more than 96% accuracy across independent datasets, marking a major advancement in precision medicine in India.

questions.question: Who became the 2025 FIDE World Cup Champion after a dramatic tiebreak victory in Goa?
questions.explanation: Javokhir Sindarov secured the 2025 FIDE World Cup title after an intense final against Wei Yi, where both classical games ended in draws, leading to rapid tiebreaks. Sindarov displayed exceptional composure and tactical sharpness, ultimately winning the tiebreaks 1½–½. His achievement is historic, as he became the youngest player to claim the World Cup title. The tournament, featuring 206 participants, included several dramatic encounters, major upsets, and strong performances from elite players. Sindarov’s victory, celebrated with his family and supporters, marks a defining milestone in his rapidly rising chess career.

questions.question: Which company partnered with MapmyIndia Mappls to launch India’s first indigenous geo-smart CRM?
questions.explanation: Zoho collaborated with MapmyIndia Mappls to introduce India’s first fully indigenous geo-smart CRM, strengthening the country’s Atmanirbhar Bharat technology ecosystem. This partnership enhances Zoho CRM by integrating advanced geospatial intelligence tools such as Address Capture, Nearby Lead Finder, Location Visualisation, and Sales Route Optimisation. These features allow businesses to utilize real-time location-based insights for improved customer engagement, more efficient field operations, and smarter sales planning. The launch marks a significant milestone in India’s digital innovation landscape by merging homegrown CRM capabilities with indigenous mapping and geospatial technologies.

questions.question: Which city has become the world’s most populous, surpassing Tokyo, according to the UN World Urbanisation Prospects 2025 report?
questions.explanation: Jakarta has overtaken Tokyo to become the world’s most populous city, with an estimated population of 42 million in 2025, according to the UN World Urbanisation Prospects report. This change results from updated UN methodology that standardises urban population measurements and accounts for functional urban areas, including urban sprawl and regional connectivity. Jakarta’s rapid urban growth reflects broader trends in Asian megacities, where nine of the ten largest cities are located. The report highlights the increasing significance of urbanisation globally, with nearly half the world’s population now residing in cities, and projections indicating continued urban concentration by 2050.

questions.question: In which city was the India Internet Governance Forum (IIGF) 2025 held?
questions.explanation: The fifth edition of the India Internet Governance Forum (IIGF) 2025 was held in New Delhi from 27–28 November. The event focused on “Advancing Internet Governance for an Inclusive and Sustainable Viksit Bharat” and included four major panels and twelve workshops addressing key aspects of digital governance. Day 1 took place at the India Habitat Centre, while Day 2 was held at the India International Centre. The forum was inaugurated by Union Minister of State Jitin Prasada, highlighting the importance of internet policy, digital inclusion, and governance in shaping India’s technological and socio-economic landscape.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Managing Director of PUMA India, effective December 2025?
questions.explanation: Ramprasad Sridharan has been appointed as the new Managing Director of PUMA India, bringing with him more than 25 years of retail and brand leadership experience. His career includes senior roles at United Colors of Benetton, Clarks, and Reebok India. With his background in brand transformation, digital expansion, and consumer-focused strategy, he is expected to guide PUMA India toward stronger market positioning, enhanced digital initiatives, and a more robust retail presence. His leadership aligns with PUMA’s ambition to grow rapidly in India’s fast-expanding sportswear and lifestyle market.

questions.question: Which company has become Team India’s official colour partner under a three-year BCCI deal?
questions.explanation: Asian Paints has signed a three-year partnership with the BCCI to become Team India’s official colour partner, covering 110 matches across men’s, women’s, and domestic cricket in India. The deal integrates the brand’s home décor identity with cricket through initiatives like the Asian Paints Colour Cam and Colour Countdown, enhancing fan engagement both digitally and on-ground. This collaboration highlights the trend of non-traditional sectors leveraging cricket’s massive fanbase to create emotional connections with audiences while strengthening brand visibility. Asian Paints joins other official partners, reflecting cricket’s significance as a marketing platform in India.

questions.question: What was India’s GDP growth in Q2 FY26?
questions.explanation: India’s economy recorded a robust GDP growth of 8.2% in the second quarter of FY26, driven primarily by strong performance in the manufacturing, construction, and services sectors. Manufacturing grew by 9.1%, construction by 7.2%, and services by 9.2%, reflecting broad-based recovery. The increase in Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE) by 7.9% also contributed to the overall growth, signaling improving consumer demand. This marks a significant rise from 5.6% in Q2 FY25, indicating accelerated economic activity. The real GDP in Q2 FY26 stood at ₹48.63 lakh crore, demonstrating the economy’s resilience and strength across sectors.

questions.question: What is the name of the operation launched by India to provide cyclone relief to Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: India launched Operation Sagar Bandhu to provide humanitarian assistance to Sri Lanka following the devastation caused by Cyclone Ditwah. The operation involved the deployment of Indian naval ships, including INS Vikrant and INS Udaygiri, to deliver essential relief materials to affected areas in Colombo. Cyclone Ditwah led to heavy rainfall, landslides, and flooding, creating an urgent need for support. Operation Sagar Bandhu exemplifies India’s commitment to regional disaster relief and cooperation, showcasing how timely aid and coordination can help neighboring countries recover from natural calamities.

questions.question: Where did the 56th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) conclude?
questions.explanation: The 56th edition of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) was held in Goa, a state renowned for hosting this prestigious event. IFFI is one of the most significant film festivals in India, attracting filmmakers and cinema enthusiasts from around the world. Goa has consistently been chosen as the venue due to its international appeal, infrastructure, and popularity as a cultural hub. This edition concluded with the Vietnamese film Skin of Youth winning the Golden Peacock award, highlighting the global nature of the festival and Goa’s continued importance in promoting international cinema.

questions.question: On which date is International Jaguar Day observed each year?
questions.explanation: International Jaguar Day is observed annually on November 29 to raise awareness about the conservation of jaguars and their habitats. Jaguars, the largest wild cats in the Americas, play a crucial role as apex predators and umbrella species, helping maintain biodiversity and ecological balance. The day highlights threats such as deforestation, poaching, and habitat fragmentation, and promotes global conservation efforts, including wildlife corridors, legal protection, and community engagement. Observing this day encourages environmental education, sustainable practices, and international collaboration to ensure the survival of jaguars and the ecosystems they support.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as Temasek’s non-executive India Chairman?
questions.explanation: Temasek Holdings, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund, appointed Piyush Gupta, former CEO of DBS Bank, as its non-executive Chairman for India, effective December 1, 2025. In this role, Gupta will guide India-focused investment strategies, support portfolio companies, and strengthen engagement with government and business stakeholders. Gupta’s extensive experience, including leading DBS Bank through a digital transformation and regional expansion across Asia-Pacific, positions him to provide strategic insight and deepen Temasek’s presence in India. His appointment reflects the firm’s commitment to long-term growth in key sectors such as financial services, technology, healthcare, and clean energy.

questions.question: Which country received 73 tonnes of medicines and vaccines from India to support its healthcare system?
questions.explanation: India delivered 73 tonnes of essential medicines, vaccines, and nutritional supplements to Afghanistan to support its struggling healthcare system. This shipment, sent to Kabul, represents one of the largest recent humanitarian efforts by India in the region. Beyond immediate medical relief, India’s aid reflects its longstanding commitment to Afghanistan’s development, including infrastructure, education, energy, and healthcare initiatives. Such humanitarian assistance strengthens regional diplomacy, builds trust, and underscores India’s role as a reliable partner providing non-interventionist support to meet urgent public health needs.

questions.question: What GDP growth rate has Moody’s projected for India in 2025?
questions.explanation: Moody’s projects India to achieve a 7% GDP growth rate in 2025, making it the fastest-growing economy among emerging markets and the Asia-Pacific region. This growth is fueled by strong domestic demand, including sustained private consumption, robust investment activity, government infrastructure initiatives, and expanding manufacturing and services sectors. Despite global uncertainties and currency fluctuations, India’s economic fundamentals remain resilient, supported by corporate financial discipline and access to international capital markets. The 7% growth rate highlights India’s strategic edge and consistent performance compared to regional peers, positioning it as a leader in emerging market growth.

questions.question: With which country did India sign a ₹7,900 crore deal for MH-60R naval helicopter support?
questions.explanation: India signed a ₹7,900 crore agreement with the United States under the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programme to support its MH-60R Seahawk helicopter fleet. The deal includes spare parts, technical assistance, maintenance training, and the establishment of repair facilities in India. It strengthens India’s maritime defence capabilities and aligns with the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative by promoting local MSME participation in defence logistics. The MH-60R helicopters, developed by Lockheed Martin, are advanced multi-role platforms for anti-submarine warfare, surveillance, and naval operations. This agreement reflects the deepening strategic and defence partnership between India and the United States.

questions.question: Who became the costliest player at the WPL 2026 auction?
questions.explanation: Deepti Sharma made history at the WPL 2026 auction by becoming the costliest player, securing a record price of ₹3.2 crore. The UP Warriorz utilized the Right-to-Match (RTM) option to retain her, matching the opening bid from Delhi Capitals. Deepti Sharma, an accomplished all-rounder, achieved the distinction of becoming the second-highest paid player in WPL history, just behind Smriti Mandhana’s ₹3.4 crore deal from 2023. This milestone highlights the growing recognition and value of women cricketers in India, reflecting the increasing competitiveness and investment in the Women’s Premier League.

questions.question: By which year does the Army aim to build a future-ready force under its three-phase roadmap?
questions.explanation: The Army has laid out a three-phase roadmap to develop a future-ready force by 2047. The first phase, HOP 2032, focuses on transformation under the Army’s Decade of Transformation (2023–2033). The second phase, STEP 2037, involves consolidating the progress made in the initial phase. The final phase, JUMP 2047, envisions the Army as an integrated and technologically advanced force capable of addressing future security challenges. This long-term plan underscores India’s commitment to modernizing its armed forces, leveraging advanced technology, and ensuring operational readiness for emerging threats.

questions.question: Which country developed the Highly Agile Modular Munition Extended Range (HAMMER) system mentioned in the agreement with India?
questions.explanation: The HAMMER system is a precision-guided air-to-ground weapon created by Safran Electronics & Defence, a major French defence and aerospace manufacturer. Its modular design allows standard unguided bombs to be transformed into high-accuracy strike weapons capable of operating effectively even in GPS-denied or electronic warfare environments. With a stand-off range of up to 70 km, it enhances the ability of combat aircraft such as the Rafale and Tejas to engage targets while staying outside enemy air defence coverage. The India–France agreement to co-produce HAMMER components further strengthens bilateral defence cooperation and boosts India’s technological indigenisation.

questions.question: Which ministry released the revised draft of Bharat NCAP 2.0 expanding vehicle safety assessment and crash-test protocols?
questions.explanation: The revised draft of Bharat NCAP 2.0 has been issued by the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, which oversees regulatory frameworks related to transport safety, vehicle standards, and road-crash prevention measures in India. By expanding the scope of safety assessment areas, increasing mandatory crash tests, introducing advanced test devices, and adding structured evaluation criteria for pedestrian and post-crash protection, the ministry aims to push India’s automobile ecosystem closer to global safety benchmarks. This strengthens public safety, encourages manufacturers to adopt robust safety technologies, and enhances consumer awareness, ultimately contributing to safer mobility and improved road-transport infrastructure across the country.

questions.question: How many new Indian names were approved by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) for Martian geological features?
questions.explanation: A total of 7 new Indian names were approved by the International Astronomical Union for Martian surface features, reflecting India’s growing contributions to planetary science. These names include locations from Kerala such as Valiamala, Thumba, Bekal, Varkala, and Periyar, along with two features honouring geologist M. S. Krishnan. The approvals highlight India’s scientific heritage, the significance of its geological and space research sites, and the role of Indian institutions in deepening Martian geological understanding. The global naming process, overseen by the IAU, ensures that culturally meaningful and scientifically relevant names gain international recognition.

questions.question: Which sector in India is planned to be opened to private players under the upcoming Atomic Energy Bill, 2025?
questions.explanation: India is preparing to introduce the Atomic Energy Bill, 2025 to enable private participation in the civil nuclear power sector, which has historically been dominated by government control under NPCIL. Opening this sector will help mobilise large-scale investments, address capital shortages, accelerate construction timelines, and support the development of advanced reactor technologies, including Small Modular Reactors. Private involvement is also expected to improve uranium supply chains, enhance localisation of reactor components, and strengthen India’s long-term energy security. These reforms are aligned with national goals of expanding nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047 and supporting India’s net-zero vision for 2070.

questions.question: In which city will the Vision for Sujalam Bharat Summit 2025 be hosted by the Ministry of Jal Shakti?
questions.explanation: The Vision for Sujalam Bharat Summit 2025 will be hosted in New Delhi, reflecting the central government’s commitment to unifying national efforts on water security and sustainability. The summit aims to accelerate reforms across crucial thematic areas such as river rejuvenation, greywater management, technology-enabled water governance, aquifer recharge, and climate-resilient drinking water systems. It brings together policymakers, implementers, central ministries, state departments, and community institutions to build a cohesive strategy under a whole-of-government approach. By focusing on evidence-based policymaking, cooperative federalism, and community participation, the event seeks to advance India’s journey toward long-term water security and a truly Sujalam Bharat.

questions.question: Who has taken additional charge as the CMD of THDC India Ltd following the vacancy created in November 2025?
questions.explanation: Sipan Garg has taken on the additional responsibility of CMD of THDC India Ltd beginning November 16, 2025, after the sudden passing of R K Vishnoi. Alongside this new role, he continues to serve as Director (Finance), a position he has held since August 17, 2024. With over 24 years of experience in finance, taxation, and power-sector operations, he brings deep expertise to this leadership post. His earlier engagements as CFO in prominent NTPC subsidiaries further strengthen his capability to guide THDC during a crucial period of operational continuity and strategic expansion.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the newly approved scheme aimed at strengthening India’s domestic manufacturing ecosystem?
questions.explanation: The approved scheme centres on building a robust domestic ecosystem for manufacturing Rare Earth Permanent Magnets, which are crucial for advanced technologies including electric vehicles, defence systems, renewable energy equipment, and high-precision industrial applications. By promoting complete value-chain integration—from oxide conversion to finished sintered magnets—the programme aims to reduce India’s heavy import dependence, especially amid global supply chain constraints dominated by China. The scheme’s incentive structure, long-term duration, and phased implementation are designed to attract major investors, enhance self-reliance, support clean mobility, and strengthen India’s path toward energy security and strategic technological independence.

questions.question: Which banned industrial dye has been repeatedly detected in Indian sweets, savouries, street foods, and spice powders?
questions.explanation: Auramine O is an industrial-grade synthetic yellow dye commonly used in textiles, leather, paper, and printing inks, but it is completely prohibited in food products under Indian regulations. Its recurring presence in Indian foods reflects deeper issues such as weak enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards Act, inadequate chemical-market regulation, and widespread use of informal supply chains. Vendors often adopt it because it is cheap, visually vibrant, and easily accessible, while consumers typically lack awareness of the health risks. Prolonged exposure can cause liver and kidney toxicity, mutagenic effects, and possible carcinogenicity, making its continued use a significant public-health concern.

questions.question: In which city did the Prime Minister inaugurate Safran’s largest global MRO facility for LEAP aircraft engines?
questions.explanation: The newly inaugurated MRO facility for LEAP aircraft engines is located in Hyderabad, marking a transformative moment for India’s aviation ecosystem. As Safran’s largest global facility of its kind, it strengthens India’s shift from merely assembling components to designing and maintaining advanced aerospace technologies. With India being one of the fastest-growing aviation markets and a large share of its narrow-body aircraft fleet powered by LEAP engines, domestic MRO capacity significantly reduces costs, turnaround time, and dependence on foreign facilities. It also boosts foreign investment, supports the broader aerospace supply chain, and aligns with national ambitions in defence manufacturing and high-tech capability building.

questions.question: Which institute’s Quantum Research Laboratories were visited by the Union Minister of Science & Technology during the inauguration of a new Liquid Helium Facility?
questions.explanation: The Union Minister of Science & Technology visited IIT Bombay to inaugurate its new Liquid Helium Facility, a major advancement for India’s quantum research ecosystem. This facility supports ultra-low-temperature experiments essential for cutting-edge quantum technologies, including superconductivity, quantum computing, sensing, and advanced materials research. The institute has also developed pioneering tools such as QMagPI—the nation’s first portable magnetometer—and India’s first indigenous Quantum Diamond Microscope for nanoscale magnetic imaging. These innovations place IIT Bombay at the forefront of India’s quantum mission, strengthening national capabilities in cryogenics, defence applications, healthcare diagnostics, and high-precision scientific instrumentation.

questions.question: Which GI-tagged aromatic rice from Assam was exported to the United Kingdom and Italy for the first time?
questions.explanation: Joha Rice is a traditional aromatic rice variety from Assam that received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in 2017. Known for its distinctive fragrance, fine-grain texture, and rich taste, it is highly valued in regional cuisine. Recently, 25 metric tonnes of Joha Rice were exported for the first time to the United Kingdom and Italy, marking an important milestone for Assam’s agricultural exports. The shipment was facilitated by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) in collaboration with the Department of Agriculture, Government of Assam. This development helps promote Joha Rice as a premium product in international markets, particularly in Europe.

questions.question: Which state emerged as the largest wool-producing state in India in FY24 with a 47.5% share of national output?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan recorded the highest wool production in India during FY24, contributing 16,013.50 thousand kg, which accounted for approximately 47.53% of the total national output of 33.69 million kg. The state’s arid climate and vast grazing lands create favourable conditions for sheep rearing. Indigenous breeds such as Marwari and Chokla produce mainly coarse wool, widely used in carpet and blanket manufacturing. With India ranking ninth globally in wool production and second in sheep population, Rajasthan’s dominant contribution significantly strengthens rural livelihoods, textile industries, and the broader wool economy.

questions.question: Which state has the Balaghat district selected as the pilot district for the World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in the cooperative sector?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has selected the Balaghat district selected as the pilot district for implementing the World’s Largest Grain Storage Plan in the cooperative sector. A 500 MT godown was inaugurated in February 2024 under this initiative. The plan is implemented through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and cooperative societies by converging schemes such as the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF), Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI), Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM), and PMFME. Reforms include reducing the beneficiary margin from 20% to 10%, revising construction costs, and enhancing scientific storage capacity to reduce post-harvest losses and support farmers.

questions.question: Which Indian state has declared 2026 as the ‘Year of Agriculture’ with a significantly increased budget to enhance farmer prosperity?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has announced 2026 as the ‘Year of Agriculture’ as part of a long-term strategy to strengthen its agricultural sector and improve farmer livelihoods. The state has increased its agriculture budget to ₹27,000 crore, marking a substantial rise compared to allocations made two decades earlier. The initiative focuses on technology transfer, income enhancement, promotion of natural farming practices, innovation, and wider access to e-Mandi platforms for nearly 40 lakh farmers. Guided by the theme ‘prosperous farmers–prosperous state’, the policy also aims to boost agricultural productivity and exports, reinforcing agriculture as a key driver of economic growth.

questions.question: Which organization launched the “Reimagining Agriculture: A Roadmap for Frontier Technology Led Transformation” initiative to modernise Indian farming using AI and advanced technologies?

options.B: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog launched the “Reimagining Agriculture: A Roadmap for Frontier Technology Led Transformation” to accelerate India’s agricultural modernization through the integration of AI, digital twins, and precision farming. The initiative emphasises climate-resilient crops, sustainability, and increased farmer income by leveraging frontier technologies. It introduces a farmer segmentation model with three archetypes—Aspiring, Transitioning, and Advanced—to enable targeted interventions. By focusing on innovation and data-driven agricultural practices, the roadmap aims to enhance productivity, resource efficiency, and long-term resilience against climate challenges, marking a major policy push toward tech-enabled, inclusive agricultural growth in India.

questions.question: In which state was the Ekatma Parv cultural festival inaugurated at Omkareshwar in 2026?
questions.explanation: The Ekatma Parv cultural festival was inaugurated in Omkareshwar, a significant spiritual site known for its association with Adi Guru Shankaracharya. The event highlights the principles of Advaita Vedanta and aims to connect traditional philosophy with contemporary themes such as artificial intelligence, environmental sustainability, and youth engagement. The festival also includes initiatives like the ‘Shankardoot’ pledge and features landmarks such as the Statue of Oneness and the upcoming Advaita Lok museum. This initiative promotes cultural heritage, spiritual learning, and global dialogue on peace and unity.

questions.question: In which city was a life-size bronze statue of Swami Vivekananda unveiled at Westlake Square in April 2026?
questions.explanation: A life-size bronze statue of Swami Vivekananda was unveiled at Westlake Square in Seattle on April 12, 2026. This marked a historic moment as it became the first instance of a US city government hosting such a monument dedicated to the Indian spiritual leader. The statue was sculpted by Indian artist Naresh Kumar Kumawat and gifted by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR). The unveiling coincided with ICCR Day, highlighting efforts to strengthen cultural ties between India and the United States, while also honouring Vivekananda’s global influence and teachings.

questions.question: Across how many locations in India will Bharat Rang Mahotsav 2026 be held, making it the largest theatre festival in the world?
questions.explanation: Bharat Rang Mahotsav 2026 is recognised as the world’s largest international theatre festival because of its massive scale and nationwide reach. The festival will take place across 40 locations in India, covering metropolitan cities as well as remote and culturally significant regions. This extensive spread allows the theatre to reach diverse audiences and promotes cultural inclusivity. By bringing performances to multiple regions simultaneously, the festival strengthens artistic exchange, supports regional theatre, and highlights India’s rich theatrical heritage on a global platform.

questions.question: In which city does the annual Magh Mela take place on the banks of the sacred Sangam during the month of Magh?
questions.explanation: The Magh Mela is an important annual religious festival celebrated at the Sangam, the holy confluence of the Ganges, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati rivers. It is held in Prayagraj from Paush Purnima to Mahashivratri during the Hindu month of Magh. Devotees gather to take ritual baths, offer donations, and perform religious practices believed to bring spiritual merit. Many pilgrims observe Kalpavas, living simply on the riverbanks with disciplined routines involving meditation, chanting, charity, and early morning bathing at Brahma Muhurat.

questions.question: The Ramnami tribe, known for tattooing the name “Ram” on their bodies and homes, originates from which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Ramnami tribe originates from Chhattisgarh and is renowned for its unique devotional practice of inscribing the name “Ram” on their bodies and homes as an expression of faith. Founded in the 19th century by Parsuram Bhardwaj, the community emphasises devotion, equality, and rejection of caste hierarchy. They follow a formless concept of divinity and uphold gender equality as part of their spiritual philosophy. Each year, the tribe celebrates their faith through the Bhajan Mela in Sarsiwa, where devotees gather to sing hymns from the Ramcharitmanas and honour the “Ram” jayostambh, symbolizing unity and devotion.

questions.question: On which date does the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) observe its Incorporation Day?
questions.explanation: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) observes its Incorporation Day on May 17 every year. GeM was incorporated on May 17, 2017, as a Section 8 non-profit company under the Companies Act, 2013, to create and manage India’s national public procurement portal. Operating under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, the platform promotes transparent and efficient digital procurement for government departments and public sector organisations. Over the years, GeM has significantly supported Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs), women entrepreneurs, SC/ST businesses, and startups by providing large-scale procurement opportunities, thereby strengthening local supply chains and supporting the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Managing Director of Jio Platforms in April 2026 for a five-year term?
questions.explanation: Akash Ambani was appointed as the Managing Director of Jio Platforms on April 9, 2026, for a five-year term. The appointment came at a significant time as the company prepared for its upcoming Initial Public Offering (IPO), with plans to file draft papers by May or June 2026. Akash Ambani has been associated with Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL) since October 2014 as a board member and has played an important role in the company’s expansion. Reliance Jio, launched in 2016, rapidly transformed India’s telecom sector by achieving 100 million subscribers in less than six months after its launch.

questions.question: Who formally assumed charge as India’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom on May 15, 2026?
questions.explanation: P Kumaran, a senior 1992-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer, formally took charge as India’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom on May 15, 2026. Before this appointment, he served as Secretary (East) in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). He succeeded Vikram Doraiswami, who was appointed as India’s Ambassador to China during a senior diplomatic reshuffle. P Kumaran has also held important diplomatic positions earlier, including serving as India’s Ambassador to Qatar and High Commissioner to Singapore. The role of High Commissioner is specifically used between Commonwealth nations such as India and the United Kingdom.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the next Chief Minister of Kerala by the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) on May 14, 2026?
questions.explanation: VD Satheesan was appointed as the next Chief Minister of Kerala after the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) achieved a decisive victory in the 2026 Kerala Assembly elections. The alliance secured 102 out of 140 seats, while the Indian National Congress emerged as the single largest party with 63 seats. VD Satheesan also won his sixth consecutive term as an MLA from the Paravur constituency. This result marked the end of the second consecutive term of the Left Democratic Front (LDF) government led by Pinarayi Vijayan. Kerala’s capital is Thiruvananthapuram, and the state was formed on November 1, 1956.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairman of the BRISEC Chamber of Commerce & Industry in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Dr Harvansh Chawla was appointed as the Chairman of the BRISEC Chamber of Commerce & Industry (CCI) on May 11, 2026. Before taking up this position, he stepped down as the Chairman of the BRICS CCI. The BRISEC Chamber focuses on promoting cross-border trade, investment, and economic collaboration among emerging and established markets. It also works to expand policy dialogue beyond the traditional BRICS framework into broader global economic corridors. The organisation is officially recognised by NITI Aayog and regularly organises forums, trade delegations, and policy interactions to strengthen international business cooperation.

questions.question: Which bank became the first Taiwanese bank to establish a branch in GIFT City, Gujarat, in May 2026?
questions.explanation: CTBC Bank became the first Taiwanese bank to establish a branch in GIFT City, Gujarat, on May 13, 2026. This marked a significant milestone as it was also the first Taiwanese bank to set up operations anywhere in India. The branch was opened to strengthen cross-border financing, trade, and investment activities between India, Taiwan, and other Asian markets. CTBC Bank has maintained a financial presence in India for around 30 years through branches in New Delhi and Kattupakkam (Chennai). Headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, the bank was established in 1966 and currently operates under the leadership of CEO Tanmoy Adhikari in India.

questions.question: Which bank launched a new credit card portfolio with variants such as AU Ananta, AU Laksya, AU Tejas, and AU Prathama in May 2026?
questions.explanation: AU Small Finance Bank launched a new credit card portfolio on May 14, 2026, introducing four variants tailored to different customer segments and lifestyle needs. The portfolio includes AU Ananta for affluent users, AU Laksya for digitally active professionals and Gen Z customers, AU Tejas for young salaried individuals, and AU Prathama for first-time credit users. These cards provide benefits such as reward points, cashback offers, airport lounge access, EMI facilities, and fuel surcharge waivers. AU Small Finance Bank is recognised as India’s largest Small Finance Bank and is also notable for receiving in-principle approval to transition into a Universal Bank.

questions.question: Which bank received RBI approval to acquire up to 9.99% stake in AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India approved Kotak Mahindra Bank to acquire up to 9.99% stake in both AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The approval allowed the Kotak Mahindra Group to increase its aggregate holding in the two banking institutions through paid-up share capital or voting rights. Following the announcement, market valuations of the involved banks witnessed positive movement. Kotak Mahindra Bank, founded by Uday Kotak in 1985, became the first Non-Banking Financial Company in India to convert into a commercial bank in 2003. The development highlights ongoing consolidation and strategic investments within India’s banking and financial sector.

questions.question: What was the non-food credit growth recorded by Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) for the financial year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) recorded a strong non-food credit growth of 15.9% during the financial year 2025-26. This marked a significant improvement compared to the previous year’s growth rate of 10.9%. The increase was driven by rising demand for credit across the industrial, agricultural, and services sectors. Industrial credit saw notable expansion in infrastructure and manufacturing, while agriculture benefited from improved rural consumption and formal credit systems. The services sector also experienced strong growth due to NBFCs, trade, and commercial real estate activities. Overall, the data reflect increased economic activity and stronger lending momentum within the Indian banking sector.

questions.question: Which organisation announced a $70 billion investment plan by 2035 to develop cross-border power grids and digital infrastructure across Asia and the Pacific?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) announced a $70 billion investment initiative aimed at strengthening cross-border power grids and digital infrastructure across Asia and the Pacific by 2035. The announcement was made during the ADB Annual Meeting held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The initiative includes the Pan-Asia Power Grid project, which seeks to integrate renewable energy systems and transmission networks, and the Asia-Pacific Digital Highway project, focused on improving broadband access, data infrastructure, and AI readiness. The ADB also established a Centre for AI Innovation and Development in Seoul to promote responsible AI adoption and digital skill training. Founded in 1966, the ADB is headquartered in Metro Manila, Philippines.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution can Parliament alter the name, area, or boundaries of a State, as in the proposal to rename Kerala as “Keralam”?
questions.explanation: Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to alter the name, area, or boundaries of a State by law. In the case of renaming Kerala as “Keralam,” the constitutional procedure requires the President to refer the Bill to the concerned State Legislature for expressing its views. After receiving those views, the Central Government may proceed to introduce the Bill in Parliament with the President’s recommendation. The proposal also involves amending the First Schedule of the Constitution, where the names of States are officially listed, ensuring that any change follows due constitutional process.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution grants plenary powers to the Election Commission over electoral rolls and the conduct of elections?
questions.explanation: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission of India (ECI). These plenary powers enable the Commission to oversee electoral rolls and conduct elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President. The authority under Article 324 supplements statutory provisions such as the Representation of the People Act, 1950, ensuring that elections remain free, fair, and credible. It also empowers the ECI to adjust procedural timelines, including Special Intensive Revision processes, to maintain transparency and effective electoral roll management.

questions.question: Under which Act is Bharat Taxi registered as India’s first cooperative-based ride-hailing platform?
questions.explanation: The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, provides the legal framework under which Bharat Taxi has been registered as a cooperative ride-hailing platform. This Act enables cooperatives to operate across multiple states while ensuring democratic governance and member ownership. By registering under this Act, Bharat Taxi functions as a driver-owned entity rather than a privately controlled company. The structure supports fair income distribution, low commissions, and collective decision-making. It reflects the government’s broader push to strengthen the cooperative sector and promote inclusive, people-centric economic models in emerging digital and mobility services.

questions.question: Under which constitutional provision did the Supreme Court direct the continued application of the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2012?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court exercised its extraordinary constitutional powers under Article 142 to ensure complete justice while issuing an interim stay on the UGC Regulations, 2026. Since the earlier 2012 Regulations had already been repealed, the Court relied on Article 142 to prevent a regulatory vacuum by directing that the 2012 framework would continue until further orders. This provision empowers the Supreme Court to pass any order necessary for doing complete justice in matters before it, even if such directions go beyond existing statutory provisions, reinforcing its role as the final constitutional arbiter.

questions.question: Which provision of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, requires prior approval before initiating an inquiry or investigation into a public servant’s official acts and was recently subject to a split Supreme Court verdict?
questions.explanation: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, was introduced through the 2018 amendment with the objective of protecting honest public servants from frivolous and vexatious investigations related to decisions taken in good faith. It mandates that investigative agencies obtain prior approval from the competent authority before initiating an inquiry or investigation into official acts of a public servant. The provision has sparked intense legal debate, as reflected in the Supreme Court’s split verdict balancing the need to safeguard bureaucratic decision-making while ensuring that anti-corruption investigations remain independent, effective, and consistent with the constitutional principle of equality before law.

questions.question: Which Indian company signed an MoU with ASML to develop a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Dholera, Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Tata Electronics signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with ASML on May 17, 2026, to establish a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Dholera, Gujarat. The agreement was witnessed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten during a bilateral engagement. The project aims to strengthen India’s domestic semiconductor ecosystem and boost technological capabilities in chip manufacturing. ASML, a Netherlands-based company and global leader in photolithography technology, will provide strategic support for setting up and scaling semiconductor operations. Tata Electronics, a wholly owned venture of Tata Sons established in 2020, focuses on semiconductor and precision component manufacturing in India.

questions.question: Which company has proposed a $11.75 billion all-cash acquisition of Organon & Co., marking one of the largest overseas deals by an Indian firm?
questions.explanation: Sun Pharma has announced a major international acquisition plan to purchase Organon & Co. for $11.75 billion in an all-cash deal. This move represents one of the largest overseas acquisitions by an Indian company and highlights its strategy to expand globally. The acquisition will significantly strengthen its footprint across multiple countries and enhance its presence in high-growth segments like women’s health and biosimilars. With Organon’s extensive product portfolio and global reach, Sun Pharma aims to become a leading global pharmaceutical player while reducing dependence on traditional generics.

questions.question: Which company signed an agreement with SMS Group to deploy the world’s first EASyMelt decarbonisation technology at its Jamshedpur Works?
questions.explanation: Tata Steel entered into a definitive agreement with SMS Group (through Paul Wurth S.A.) to implement the innovative EASyMelt technology at its Jamshedpur plant. This project represents the first industrial-scale deployment of this electrically-assisted syngas smelter technology, designed to significantly reduce carbon emissions in ironmaking. The initiative is expected to cut CO2 emissions by over 50% compared to conventional blast furnace operations. It also aligns with Tata Steel’s long-term sustainability goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2045, marking a major advancement in green steel production and environmentally responsible industrial practices.

questions.question: Which company received the GreenPro ecolabel certification from the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for sustainable steel manufacturing on April 18, 2026?
questions.explanation: The GreenPro ecolabel certification, awarded by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), recognises environmentally sustainable products and manufacturing practices. Rathi Steel And Power Limited earned this certification for its Fe 550 Grade TMT rebars, marketed under the brand Rathi Powertech. This achievement highlights the company’s commitment to green steel production, reduced carbon emissions, and environmentally responsible construction materials. The certified products also contribute to green building standards by offering credits under LEED and aligning with Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) norms, reinforcing sustainable infrastructure development in India.

questions.question: Which companies signed MoUs with the Ministry of Labour & Employment to enhance digital job matching through the NCS portal in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Porter and Gigin are the companies that entered into agreements with the Ministry of Labour & Employment to improve employment opportunities through the National Career Service portal. These collaborations aim to strengthen digital job matching by connecting jobseekers with verified opportunities in sectors like logistics and gig work. The initiative focuses on generating large-scale employment, increasing employer participation, and enhancing transparency using technology such as Artificial Intelligence. It also supports skill development and integrates with multiple platforms to expand access and improve the efficiency of the employment ecosystem in India.

questions.question: In which city did the Indian Navy inaugurate its premier Naval Sailing Node on 17 May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Indian Navy inaugurated its premier Naval Sailing Node at the Upper Lake, also known as Bhojtal, in Bhopal on 17 May 2026. The inauguration ceremony was presided over by Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, the Chief of the Naval Staff. The state-of-the-art facility was established to support advanced training activities for the Indian Navy Sailing Team, rowing, canoeing, and kayaking teams, along with NCC cadets. The initiative aligns with India’s National Sports Policy by promoting world-class sports training and encouraging youth participation in defence services. Bhojtal, where the facility is located, is historically significant and recognised internationally as part of the Ramsar-listed Bhoj Wetland.

questions.question: In which city was the third edition of the Kalam & Kavach strategic defence conference inaugurated on May 14, 2026?
questions.explanation: The third edition of the Kalam & Kavach strategic defence conference was inaugurated at the Manekshaw Centre in New Delhi by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth. The conference focused on the vision of Jointness, Aatmanirbharta, and Innovation (JAI), while promoting indigenisation and international collaboration in defence technologies.
