Discussions covered AI-enabled warfare, autonomous systems, hypersonic technologies, quantum-enabled C4ISR capabilities, and emerging space threats. The event also highlighted the role of iDEX, MSMEs, and defence industrial corridors in strengthening India’s defence ecosystem. The initiative supports India’s long-term strategic objective of achieving Viksit Bharat@2047 through advanced indigenous defence capabilities.

questions.question: What is the name of the strategic initiative aimed at establishing manufacturing and integration partnerships across 7 continents and 77 countries for the Kaal Bhairava combat aircraft?
questions.explanation: Operation 777 is a strategic initiative launched in connection with the Kaal Bhairava autonomous combat aircraft programme developed by Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace (FWDA). The initiative focuses on creating manufacturing and integration partnerships across 7 continents and 77 countries, strengthening India’s global defence manufacturing presence. Under this initiative, FWDA established its first overseas manufacturing facility in Portugal in collaboration with SKETCHPIXEL LDA. The Kaal Bhairava platform is a Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) autonomous combat aircraft equipped with advanced features such as AI-driven target recognition, encrypted communication systems, and swarm coordination capabilities, representing a significant milestone in India’s indigenous defence technology development.

questions.question: Which Indian Naval Ship completed the IOS SAGAR initiative port call at Chattogram, Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: INS Sunayna successfully completed its maritime port call at Chattogram, Bangladesh, under the Indian Ocean Ship (IOS) SAGAR initiative. The deployment was carried out under the Ministry of Defence and included joint naval activities with the Bangladesh Navy, such as a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) and coordinated maritime manoeuvres with BNS Protoy. The ship also carried personnel from 16 partner nations during the mission, highlighting regional maritime cooperation. After concluding its Bangladesh visit, the vessel proceeded toward Colombo, Sri Lanka, as part of its operational route. The initiative strengthens India’s maritime partnerships and regional security collaboration in the Indian Ocean region.

questions.question: Which organization successfully conducted the long-duration test of an Actively Cooled Full Scale Scramjet Combustor for hypersonic missiles?
questions.explanation: DRDO, the Defence Research and Development Organisation, successfully carried out a major long-duration test of an Actively Cooled Full Scale Scramjet Combustor for hypersonic missile technology on May 09, 2026. The test was conducted at the Scramjet Connect Pipe Test Facility in Hyderabad and achieved a continuous engine runtime of more than 1,200 seconds, surpassing the earlier benchmark set in January 2026. The project involved advanced indigenous technologies such as liquid hydrocarbon endothermic fuel and high-temperature thermal barrier coatings. This achievement strengthens India’s Hypersonic Cruise Missile Development Program and highlights the country’s growing capability in advanced aerospace and missile technologies.

questions.question: Which airport received Union Cabinet approval for modernisation under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the modernisation of Nagpur International Airport through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model by extending the lease period of the Airports Authority of India land granted to MIHAN India Limited. The project operations will be managed by GMR Nagpur International Airport Limited (GNIAL) for a concession period of 30 years. The modernisation aims to expand the airport’s capacity to handle up to 30 million passengers annually while strengthening cargo logistics in the Vidarbha region. The airport, officially known as Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, is also a major component of the Multi-modal International Cargo Hub and Airport at Nagpur (MIHAN) project.

questions.question: Until when has India prohibited sugar exports under the amended trade policy announced in May 2026?
questions.explanation: India prohibited the export of raw, white, and refined sugar until September 30, 2026, through an amendment to the trade policy announced by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The decision was taken to ensure adequate domestic supply and stabilise sugar prices in the local market. The prohibition applies to specific ITC (HS) codes under Chapter 17 of the trade classification system. Certain exemptions continue for quota-based exports to the European Union and the United States, shipments under the Advance Authorisation Scheme, and consignments related to international food security commitments. If not extended further, the export status will revert to “Restricted” after September 2026.

questions.question: What was India's annual WPI inflation rate in April 2026?
questions.explanation: India’s annual inflation rate based on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) stood at 8.3% in April 2026 on a provisional basis. The increase was mainly driven by higher prices of mineral oils, crude petroleum, natural gas, basic metals, and manufactured products. Fuel and power recorded a particularly sharp rise due to higher mineral oil prices, while primary articles also witnessed strong inflationary pressure. The WPI is released every month by the Office of the Economic Adviser under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Manufactured products carry the highest weightage in the WPI basket, making them a key factor in overall inflation trends.

questions.question: What is the revised import duty rate on gold and silver announced by the Centre in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Centre revised the customs duty on precious metals on May 13, 2026, to safeguard macroeconomic stability and conserve foreign exchange reserves. Under the revised structure, the import duty on gold and silver was increased significantly from 6% to 15%, while platinum duty was raised to 15.4%. The policy aims to reduce non-essential imports and ease pressure on India’s Current Account Deficit (CAD). The decision was also influenced by global crude oil volatility and supply-side disruptions affecting international trade and shipping. The Ministry of Finance manages such economic and taxation policies to maintain financial stability in the country.

questions.question: What is the revised annual release date for the Provisional Estimates of Annual GDP and Q4 GDP announced by the NSO?
questions.explanation: The National Statistics Office (NSO) revised the annual release schedule for the Provisional Estimates of Annual GDP and Fourth Quarter GDP to June 7 each year. Earlier, the data was released on the last working day of May. The revision was made after consultations with the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS). The new schedule allows the inclusion of important corporate financial data and finalised Central Government account figures such as taxes, subsidies, and capital expenditure. The NSO, functioning under the Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation, is responsible for compiling national accounts and major macroeconomic indicators in India.

questions.question: Which institution announced the establishment of its first international deep-tech centre in Menlo Park, California?
questions.explanation: IIT Madras announced the creation of its first international deep-tech center in Menlo Park, California, with an investment plan of US$ 7.5 million. The initiative was introduced at the SelectUSA Investment Summit and aims to support Indian deep-tech startups by providing access to mentorship, funding opportunities, and global markets. Developed in collaboration with CA Startups, the centre is designed to encourage translational research, innovation, and international talent exchange. IIT Madras, established in 1959 with support from West Germany, is recognised as one of India’s leading engineering and research institutions and is headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which institution signed an MoU with the Ministry of Minority Affairs under the PM VIKAS scheme to provide technology-driven skill training to minority youth?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Minority Affairs collaborated with IIT Patna under the PM VIKAS scheme to enhance skill development among minority youth in Bihar. The initiative aims to train 600 individuals in advanced and industry-relevant fields such as Artificial Intelligence and Business Analytics. This partnership reflects the government’s focus on bridging the skill gap and improving employability through modern technological education. IIT Patna, established in 2008, is one of India’s premier institutions and plays a key role in delivering high-quality technical training, thereby supporting sustainable livelihood opportunities for underrepresented communities.

questions.question: Which state launched a statewide AI literacy programme in 2026 to educate nearly 2 million government school students?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, Telangana introduced a large-scale AI literacy programme aimed at equipping nearly 2 million students in government schools with foundational knowledge in artificial intelligence. The initiative involves partnerships with organisations like Amazon Future Engineer and Pi Jam Foundation, ensuring both technological and educational support. The curriculum, designed by SCERT Telangana, targets students from Classes 5 to 9 and includes structured hours of AI learning annually. With additional measures such as teacher training and laptop distribution, the programme strengthens digital education infrastructure and prepares students for future technological advancements.

questions.question: Which university signed an MoU with the National Council for Cement and Building Materials to strengthen research and training in the construction sector?
questions.explanation: Delhi Technological University is the academic institution that partnered with the National Council for Cement and Building Materials through a Memorandum of Understanding. This collaboration focuses on enhancing research, innovation, and skill development in cement and construction technologies. It aims to bridge the gap between industry and academia by promoting joint research initiatives, training programs, and knowledge exchange. The partnership also contributes to building sustainable infrastructure by equipping students and professionals with the modern technical expertise required to meet the evolving demands of the construction sector in India.

questions.question: Which institution launched the Krishnamurthy Tandon School of Artificial Intelligence with a ₹100 crore endowment?
questions.explanation: IIM Ahmedabad has launched the Krishnamurthy Tandon School of Artificial Intelligence with a ₹100 crore endowment to strengthen India’s AI and education ecosystem. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between advanced AI research and real-world applications in business and governance. It focuses on areas such as ethical AI use, workforce readiness, and strategic integration of AI in organisations. By promoting translational research, the institution seeks to convert innovations into practical solutions. This move highlights the growing importance of AI in shaping industries and reflects India’s commitment to becoming a leader in emerging technologies.

questions.question: In which national park was India’s first satellite-tagged Ganges softshell turtle released?
questions.explanation: India’s first satellite-tagged Ganges softshell turtle was released in Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve as part of a major wildlife conservation initiative. The project was launched on Endangered Species Day to monitor the movement, habitat use, breeding sites, and seasonal migration patterns of the endangered freshwater turtle species. The Ganges softshell turtle, scientifically known as Nilssonia gangetica, is listed as endangered on the IUCN Red List despite being widely distributed across India. The initiative was jointly carried out by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Assam Forest Department, Kaziranga authorities, and supported by the National Geographic Society to strengthen conservation planning in the Brahmaputra river basin.

questions.question: In which Indian state was the ‘Lion’ Species Spotlight Programme inaugurated at Sasan Gir in 2026?
questions.explanation: The ‘Lion’ Species Spotlight Programme was inaugurated at Sasan Gir in Gujarat by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav as a precursor to the IBCA Summit 2026. The programme highlighted the success of Asiatic lion conservation efforts in the Greater Gir Landscape, where the lion population reached an estimated 891 individuals in 2025, reflecting a 32% increase since the 2020 census. The initiative aligns with Project Lion, launched in 2020 for long-term conservation and habitat restoration. Gujarat remains the only natural habitat of Asiatic lions in the world, making the state globally significant for wildlife conservation and biodiversity protection.

questions.question: Which airport in Mumbai achieved the Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) Platinum – Class I Rating for diverting over 99% of its waste from landfills?

options.D: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport

questions.explanation: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) in Mumbai achieved the prestigious Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) Platinum – Class I Rating on May 12, 2026. The recognition was awarded by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for successfully diverting more than 99 percent of airport waste away from landfills. This achievement highlights the airport’s strong commitment to sustainable waste management and environmental conservation. CSMIA is also one of India’s busiest airports, handling over 50 million passengers annually. The airport is operated by Mumbai International Airport Limited, where Adani Airport Holdings Limited holds the majority stake.

questions.question: What was the percentage drop in snow persistence recorded in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region during the winter season of 2025–2026?
questions.explanation: The Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region witnessed a significant environmental change with a 27% decline in snow persistence during the winter season of November 2025 to March 2026. This marks the fourth consecutive year of declining snow levels, highlighting a worrying trend linked to climate change. Reduced snow persistence affects water availability as it lowers early summer river flows, which are crucial for agriculture, hydropower, and drinking water supply. The decline also increases dependence on groundwater and raises drought risks in several basins. This situation underscores the urgent need for climate adaptation and sustainable water management strategies.

questions.question: What percentage of land animal habitats are projected to be threatened by extreme climate events by 2085?
questions.explanation: A global study published in May 2026 highlights the severe impact of climate change on biodiversity, projecting that 36% of terrestrial vertebrate habitats will be affected by extreme weather events by 2085. The research covered thousands of species across multiple ecosystems and revealed that rising temperatures, heatwaves, wildfires, droughts, and floods will increasingly overlap, intensifying risks to wildlife. Regions like the Amazon Basin, Africa, and Southeast Asia are particularly vulnerable. Amphibians are expected to face the highest level of exposure. These findings emphasise the urgent need for climate action and biodiversity conservation strategies worldwide.

questions.question: In which Indian state was the Indian Orchid Festival 2026 held after four days of exhibitions and expert sessions?
questions.explanation: The Indian Orchid Festival 2026 concluded in the Pakyong district of Sikkim after four days of activities that included exhibitions, expert discussions, and participation from farmers and entrepreneurs. The event was organised by the ICAR-National Research Centre for Orchids with the theme “Orchids for Beauty & Prosperity.” It brought together orchid growers, nursery owners, researchers, and floriculture experts from across the country. The festival promoted orchid cultivation, sustainable horticulture practices, and floriculture entrepreneurship. Participants exchanged knowledge on modern orchid farming techniques, breeding innovations, and commercial opportunities. Such initiatives support the growth of India’s floriculture industry and highlight the rich orchid diversity found particularly in the northeastern and Himalayan regions.

questions.question: In which region does the Spituk Gustor festival mark the beginning of the annual monastic celebrations?
questions.explanation: Ladakh is the region where the Spituk Gustor festival is celebrated as the first monastic festival of the year. Held at the historic Spituk Monastery, the event begins after a week-long period of prayers focused on peace, prosperity, and relief from the harsh winter season. The festival is known for its sacred masked dances, ceremonial rituals, and the unveiling of deities, which attract monks, devotees, and tourists alike. As one of Ladakh’s 16 annual monastic festivals, it plays a key role in preserving Buddhist cultural traditions and spiritual heritage.

questions.question: In which city did the four-day international dance and music festival ‘Udbhav Utsav’ begin?
questions.explanation: The international dance and music festival ‘Udbhav Utsav’ commenced in Gwalior with a colorful carnival that started from Captain Roop Singh Stadium and proceeded to Jiwaji University. The festival was inaugurated at the Atal Auditorium, Jiwaji University, by Padma Shri awardees Dr. Nalini and Dr. Kamalini, both eminent Kathak dancers. This grand cultural event celebrates global art forms and promotes cross-cultural exchange through performances by artists from various countries. Gwalior, known for its deep cultural and musical heritage, serves as an ideal venue for such an international celebration of dance and music.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the festival of Ningol Chakouba celebrated?
questions.explanation: Ningol Chakouba is a traditional festival celebrated in the northeastern state of Manipur, symbolizing the deep bond between married women and their brothers. Observed on the second day of the Meitei month of Hiyangei, the festival involves married women (Ningols) visiting their parental homes, where they are warmly welcomed and treated to a grand feast (Chakouba). The celebration reflects the values of love, respect, and family unity deeply rooted in Manipuri culture. Beyond its social significance, Ningol Chakouba also reinforces community harmony and preserves the rich cultural heritage of Manipur through shared familial traditions.

questions.question: On which date will Bandi Chhor Divas be celebrated in 2025?
questions.explanation: Bandi Chhor Divas in 2025 falls on October 21. This Sikh festival commemorates the release of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji from Gwalior Fort along with 52 princes. The day coincides with Diwali but has its own unique spiritual significance, symbolizing liberation, justice, and selflessness. Sikhs celebrate it with prayers, devotional singing, lighting of lamps, and community service through langar. The festival honours the Guru’s act of ensuring freedom for others, highlighting values of equality, compassionate leadership, and collective responsibility. Its observance is widespread both in India and across the global Sikh diaspora.

questions.question: Which Financial Technology company announced the launch of the Artificial Intelligence-native lending infrastructure suite named Atlas?
questions.explanation: FinBox announced the launch of Atlas, an Artificial Intelligence-native lending infrastructure suite designed to transform the digital lending ecosystem. The platform significantly reduces loan processing time from nearly three weeks to just 24 hours by automating traditional lending operations. Atlas replaces manual workflows with AI-driven agents capable of handling borrower onboarding, document verification, and operational decision-making throughout the credit lifecycle. This innovation aims to improve efficiency, speed, and accuracy in digital lending services. The launch reflects the growing role of Artificial Intelligence in the fintech sector, where automation and data-driven systems are increasingly being used to streamline financial services and customer experiences.

questions.question: Which company launched India's first compliant stablecoin cross-border payments platform in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Xflow launched India’s first compliant stablecoin-based cross-border payments infrastructure on May 14, 2026. The platform allows Indian businesses to accept international payments in stablecoins such as USDC and USDT and convert them into Indian Rupees through authorised banking channels. The system ensures regulatory compliance by conducting stablecoin transactions and off-ramping processes outside India, while only fiat currency enters the country through AD Category I banks. The platform mainly supports MSMEs, SaaS companies, and service exporters facing challenges in global payments. Xflow was co-founded by Anand Balaji and Ashwin Bhatnagar and is backed by investors such as Lightspeed, General Catalyst, and Stripe.

questions.question: Which mutual fund company launched the dedicated Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) brand named RedHex SIF in India in May 2026?
questions.explanation: HSBC Mutual Fund launched RedHex SIF, a dedicated Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) brand in India, on May 4, 2026. The SEBI-approved investment structure is designed for experienced investors, institutional participants, and High Net-Worth Individuals (HNIs). The fund requires a minimum investment of ₹10 lakh and combines the transparency and governance standards of mutual funds with the flexibility of advanced asset management strategies. RedHex SIF focuses on theme-based portfolio construction along with strong risk management practices. HSBC Holdings plc, headquartered in London, operates in 56 countries and territories and is one of the world’s leading banking and financial services organisations.

questions.question: Which organisations collaborated to launch a biometric authentication system for card transactions in 2026?

options.B: Google Pay, ICICI Bank, and PhonePe

questions.explanation: Flipkart, Axis Bank, and PayU jointly introduced a biometric authentication system aimed at enhancing the security of digital transactions. This system replaces traditional SMS-based OTP verification with advanced methods such as fingerprint and facial recognition. The initiative addresses the rising concerns of digital fraud, which has significantly increased in recent years. By implementing device-binding protocols and secure authentication flows, the system reduces risks like SIM-swap and OTP interception. It also aligns with regulatory guidelines issued by the Reserve Bank of India, ensuring safer and more reliable digital payment experiences for users.

questions.question: Which fintech company became the first private-sector entity to secure direct membership in the RBI’s Centralised Payment System (CPS)?
questions.explanation: Pay Point India Network achieved a significant milestone by becoming the first private-sector fintech to gain direct access to the RBI’s Centralised Payment System. This allows it to operate independently within RTGS and NEFT networks without depending on partner banks. The development marks a shift from the earlier system, where only banks and select institutions could participate. With direct membership, Pay Point benefits from reduced transaction costs, faster settlements, and enhanced data security. This move also reflects the RBI’s evolving approach to integrating fintech players into core financial infrastructure.

questions.question: On which date is the International Day of Families observed globally every year?
questions.explanation: The International Day of Families is observed globally every year on May 15 to recognise the importance of families in society and their role in social development. The 2026 theme, “Families, Inequalities and Child Wellbeing,” highlighted how social and economic inequalities affect family life and children’s futures. The observance encourages governments and institutions to adopt policies supporting family welfare, education, health, employment, and social inclusion. The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed the day in 1993, and the first global observance took place in 1994. It serves as an important platform for promoting awareness about issues affecting families worldwide.

questions.question: On which date is World Thalassemia Day officially observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Thalassemia Day is observed every year on May 8 to spread awareness about thalassemia, a hereditary blood disorder that affects haemoglobin production and requires lifelong medical care. The 2026 theme, “Hidden No More: Finding the Undiagnosed. Supporting the Unseen,” highlighted the importance of identifying undiagnosed patients and improving support systems. The observance also promotes prenatal screening to reduce the number of affected births. Established officially on May 8, 1994, by Panos Englezos, the day honours patients battling thalassemia and encourages global healthcare communities to improve treatment, care, and advocacy efforts worldwide.

questions.question: On which date was Mother’s Day celebrated across the world in 2026?
questions.explanation: Mother’s Day 2026 was celebrated globally on May 10, which fell on the second Sunday of May. The occasion honours the unconditional love, sacrifices, care, and support provided by mothers and maternal figures. People celebrate the day through family gatherings, heartfelt wishes, gifts, flowers, and expressions of gratitude. The modern celebration of Mother’s Day began in the early 20th century due to the efforts of American social activist Anna Jarvis, who organised the first official observance in 1908 in memory of her mother. Today, Mother’s Day is recognised worldwide as one of the most meaningful family-oriented celebrations.

questions.question: On which date is World Ovarian Cancer Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: World Ovarian Cancer Day is observed annually on May 8 to raise awareness about ovarian cancer and promote better healthcare access for women worldwide. In 2026, the World Ovarian Cancer Coalition marked the 14th observance of the day by launching new initiatives focused on health equity. The campaign theme “No Woman Left Behind” emphasised equal access to diagnosis and quality treatment irrespective of geographic location. Awareness activities, including the #ReachForTheScars campaign and the WOCD 2026 toolkit, aimed to educate people about early symptoms, the importance of timely medical care, and the risks associated with delayed diagnosis.

questions.question: On which date is World Athletics Day observed annually?
questions.explanation: World Athletics Day is observed every year on May 7 to promote athletics and encourage young people to participate in sports and physical activities. The day is regulated by World Athletics, the international governing body for athletics headquartered in Monaco. In 2026, the theme for the observance is “Sport: Building Bridges, Breaking Barriers.” The celebration aims to spread awareness about the importance of fitness, teamwork, discipline, and sportsmanship while encouraging schools and institutions to organise athletic events and grassroots competitions. It also highlights the role of sports in building healthier communities and fostering social and environmental awareness among youth.

questions.question: In which countries did the WHO declare the Ebola outbreak a public health emergency of international concern in May 2026?

options.B: emocratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda

questions.explanation: The World Health Organisation (WHO) declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern on May 17, 2026. The outbreak began in the mining region of Mongwalu in the Ituri province of the DRC and later spread to the capitals Kinshasa and Kampala. The disease involved the rare Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which currently has no approved vaccine or specific treatment. WHO recommended emergency management measures, cross-border screening, and temporary travel restrictions for exposed individuals to contain the spread of the deadly virus across the affected region.

questions.question: Who was sworn in for a seventh term as the President of Uganda in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Yoweri Museveni was officially sworn in for a historic seventh term as the President of Uganda on May 12, 2026. The oath-taking ceremony took place at the Kololo Independence Grounds in Kampala, the capital city of Uganda. Museveni secured a decisive electoral victory with more than 71 percent of the votes, while opposition leader Bobi Wine received around 25 percent. Museveni is regarded as one of Africa’s longest-serving leaders, and his latest victory extends his continuous tenure in office to nearly four decades. Uganda continues to play an important role in East African politics and regional affairs.

questions.question: Which country developed an AI-driven electrochemical process to convert nitrate-polluted wastewater into sustainable agricultural ammonia?
questions.explanation: China developed an advanced Artificial Intelligence-driven electrochemical process to transform nitrate-polluted wastewater into sustainable agricultural ammonia. The innovation uses machine learning to identify the most effective Dual-Atom Catalyst (DAC) for nitrate electroreduction. This technology operates at room temperature with renewable electricity and achieves nearly three times the efficiency of earlier methods. The process is environmentally significant because it helps reduce water pollution, limits eutrophication in aquatic ecosystems, and lowers carbon emissions associated with traditional ammonia production. It also serves as an eco-friendly alternative to the conventional Haber-Bosch process, which requires fossil fuels, high temperatures, and extreme pressure.

questions.question: Who became one of the first openly transgender candidates elected to the Scottish Parliament in 2026?
questions.explanation: Q Manivannan, originally from Tamil Nadu, achieved a historic milestone by winning a seat in the Scottish Parliament in 2026 as a representative of the Scottish Green Party. This victory made Manivannan one of the first openly transgender and non-binary individuals elected to Holyrood. An important aspect of this achievement was that the election was won without permanent UK residency or British citizenship. Eligibility was possible because of a 2025 rule change allowing individuals with legal immigration status to contest public office. The event highlights progress in political inclusivity, representation, and equal opportunities within Scotland’s democratic system.

questions.question: Which country hosted the ISO TC 20 / SC 14 international subcommittee meetings on space systems and operations for the first time in 2026?
questions.explanation: India hosted the ISO TC 20 / SC 14 international subcommittee meetings on space systems and operations for the first time on May 08, 2026, in New Delhi. The meetings were organized by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) at Bharat Mandapam and witnessed participation from 131 delegates representing 13 countries. The event focused on creating global standards for mission safety, interoperability, and mitigation of space debris. The conference also highlighted India’s rapidly growing private space ecosystem, encouraged through IN-SPACe policy reforms. Experts from ISRO and several international space agencies participated, strengthening India’s role in global space governance and technological cooperation.

questions.question: What was the name of the operation under which the NCB carried out India’s first-ever seizure of the psychotropic drug Captagon?
questions.explanation: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) conducted India’s first-ever seizure of the psychotropic drug Captagon under Operation RAGEPILL. Announced on May 16, 2026, the operation led to the recovery of 227.7 kg of Captagon tablets and powder valued at approximately ₹182 crore in the illegal market. The drugs were seized from locations in New Delhi and Mundra, Gujarat, where they were concealed in machinery and imported cargo from Syria. Captagon, commonly known as the “Jihadi Drug,” contains substances such as Fenetylline and Amphetamine. The operation exposed an international trafficking network attempting to use India as a transit hub for smuggling narcotics to Gulf countries, especially Saudi Arabia.

questions.question: What was the guiding theme of the National Conclave on Minorities Welfare convened by the Ministry of Minority Affairs in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The National Conclave on Minorities Welfare organized by the Ministry of Minority Affairs (MoMA) in May 2026, was conducted under the theme “Bhagidari Se Bhagyoday,” which means “Prosperity through Participation.” The conclave focused on improving minority welfare through participative governance and the integration of artificial intelligence in public service delivery. Discussions included the use of AI-powered conversational bots for grievance redressal and welfare scheme implementation, as well as AI applications for Hajj 2027 management. Several technology partners, such as Generation India, EkStep Foundation, Gnani, and Sarvam, showcased innovative AI-enabled governance solutions to improve citizen-centric services and inclusive development initiatives.

questions.question: Which country signed 8 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with India during Dr S. Jaishankar's diplomatic visit in May 2026?
questions.explanation: India and Trinidad and Tobago strengthened their bilateral relationship by signing eight MoUs covering sectors such as infrastructure, security, healthcare, tourism, and capacity building. The agreements were signed during External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar’s official visit in May 2026. A significant part of the visit included paying tribute at Nelson Island, the historic site where the first Indian indentured labourers, known as Girmitiyas, arrived in Trinidad and Tobago during British colonial rule. The visit highlighted the deep cultural and historical connections between the two nations, while also promoting stronger diplomatic, economic, and people-to-people ties for future cooperation.

questions.question: Which university became India's first Institution of Eminence to receive accreditation from the Data Science Council of America (DASCA)?
questions.explanation: O.P. Jindal Global University (JGU), located in Sonipat, Haryana, became the first Institution of Eminence in India to receive accreditation from the Data Science Council of America (DASCA). The accreditation was granted under the World Data Science & AI Initiative (WDSAI) to align academic programs with international industry standards. The certification remains valid until 2031 and covers residential, non-residential, and online learning formats. Several AI and Data Science-related programs, including MBA, M.Sc., and undergraduate courses, received recognition under this framework. The achievement highlights the university’s growing focus on advanced technology education, ethical AI practices, and globally benchmarked academic excellence.

questions.question: From which year did the Supreme Court propose the creation of a permanent Vice-President post reserved for women in the SCBA?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court proposed the establishment of a permanent Vice-President post reserved exclusively for women in the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) beginning from the 2027-28 term. The move is aimed at improving women’s representation in legal institutions and encouraging greater participation in leadership roles within the legal profession. The court also retained the reservation of the Secretary post for women in the 2026-27 SCBA elections. These reforms are part of broader judicial efforts to strengthen gender inclusion, including reservations for women in bar associations and bar councils, ultimately paving the way for increased representation of women in senior legal positions.

questions.question: Who was Bangladesh’s first woman Prime Minister who passed away at the age of 80 after a prolonged illness?
questions.explanation: Khaleda Zia was a towering figure in Bangladesh’s political history and served as the country’s first female Prime Minister. She led the nation during two separate terms from 1991 to 1996 and again from 2001 to 2006, playing a crucial role in restoring parliamentary democracy after military rule. As leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, she shaped the country’s two-party system through a long-standing rivalry with Sheikh Hasina. Her passing at the age of 80 marked the end of an era defined by democratic struggle, political transitions, and enduring influence on Bangladesh’s governance.

questions.question: Who was the 114-year-old Padma Shri environmentalist known for planting hundreds of banyan trees?
questions.explanation: Saalumarada Thimmakka was an iconic environmentalist admired for her extraordinary contribution to afforestation. She became widely known for planting 385 banyan trees along a 4.5-kilometre stretch, a feat that earned her the name “Saalumarada,” meaning a row of trees. Over her long lifetime, she received numerous prestigious recognitions, including the Padma Shri in 2019, the Nadoja Award in 2010, the National Citizen Award in 1995, and the Indira Priyadarshini Vrikshamitra Award in 1997. Her work became a symbol of dedication to nature conservation, inspiring many to engage in environmental protection and sustainable practices.

questions.question: Who was the pioneering molecular biologist credited with co-discovering the double helix structure of DNA and later leading the Human Genome Project?
questions.explanation: James D. Watson was an American molecular biologist who, along with Francis H.C. Crick, discovered the double helix structure of DNA in 1953 — a groundbreaking model that transformed the study of genetics. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962 for this discovery. Watson later became the director of Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory and led the Human Genome Project, contributing to the mapping of over 3 billion base pairs of human DNA. His legacy, while marked by controversy, remains central to modern molecular biology.

questions.question: Zubeen Garg, the legendary singer of “Ya Ali” fame who passed away in 2025, was an icon of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Zubeen Garg, one of India’s most versatile and celebrated musicians, was an icon of Assam and the greater Northeast. Born in 1972, he built an extraordinary career spanning over three decades, with more than 38,000 songs recorded across 40 languages. He gained national recognition through the Bollywood hit “Ya Ali” from Gangster (2006), but his contribution to Assamese music and culture was unparalleled. Beyond singing, he was also a composer, actor, filmmaker, and philanthropist. His sudden passing in Singapore at age 52 left a deep void in Indian music. Leaders and fans across the country paid heartfelt tributes, acknowledging his role in carrying Assam’s cultural legacy to the national and global stage.

questions.question: L. Ganesan, who recently passed away at the age of 80, was serving as the Governor of which state at the time of his death?
questions.explanation: L. Ganesan, a veteran BJP leader and former Rajya Sabha member, passed away at the age of 80 while serving as the 21st Governor of Nagaland. Born in Thanjavur in 1945, he had a long political career, including his tenure as a Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh in 2016. He also held key gubernatorial responsibilities, serving as the Governor of Manipur from August 2021 to February 2023 and taking additional charge of West Bengal between July and November 2022. Since February 2023, he had been serving in Nagaland, where his sudden demise marked the end of his public service journey.

questions.question: Who became the first transgender umpire in Indian cricket history after qualifying through state panel examinations in 2026?
questions.explanation: Rithika Sri achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first transgender umpire in Indian cricket. After successfully passing the state panel examinations, she earned official recognition to officiate matches. Her journey reflects determination and resilience, as she has been actively involved in umpiring local and district-level games for several years. This achievement also highlights progressive steps taken by cricket authorities, such as inclusive application policies that recognise diverse gender identities. Her accomplishment not only marks personal success but also promotes inclusivity and equal opportunities in sports, encouraging broader participation across different sections of society.

questions.question: Who concluded the official economic delegation visit to the Czech Republic on 22–23 April 2026?
questions.explanation: Jitin Prasada, Union Minister of State for Commerce & Industry, led and concluded the official economic delegation visit to the Czech Republic during April 22–23, 2026. During this visit, he co-chaired the 13th session of the India–Czech Republic Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation and engaged in multiple high-level meetings with Czech officials. He also inaugurated the India–Czech Business Forum and explored opportunities in sectors like automotive manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics, and advanced laser science. His visit aimed at strengthening bilateral trade, investment ties, and technological collaboration between India and the Czech Republic.

questions.question: Who felicitated top-performing ministries, states, and departments at the SADHANA Saptah 2026 ceremony?
questions.explanation: The SADHANA Saptah 2026 ceremony recognized excellence in digital capacity building across government institutions, with Union Minister Jitendra Singh leading the felicitation. The initiative saw massive participation, with millions of government employees engaging in structured learning programs under the Mission Karmayogi framework. It emphasised inclusivity by involving employees across all levels, including frontline workers. The program also highlighted the importance of adopting emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence to make the workforce future-ready. Coordinated by the Capacity Building Commission, it aims to institutionalise continuous skill development in governance.

questions.question: Who assumed the charge of Chief Adviser (Cost) in the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Anand Kumar Pal took over as the Chief Adviser (Cost) in the Department of Expenditure under the Ministry of Finance on April 10, 2026. A 1997-batch officer of the Indian Cost Accounts Service, he brings extensive experience in financial analysis, costing methodologies, and international trade policy. Prior to this role, he served as Additional Chief Adviser (Cost) in the Ministry of Defence and held positions in organisations like the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority and the Directorate General of Trade Remedies. His appointment reflects the importance of expert financial oversight in managing public expenditure and policy implementation.

questions.question: Who was re-elected to a major UN committee during India’s unopposed victories in the ECOSOC elections in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Preeti Saran was re-elected to a major United Nations committee as part of India’s successful and unopposed performance in the ECOSOC elections held in April 2026. Her re-election to the Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights reflects her extensive diplomatic experience and global recognition. She has previously served in key roles such as Secretary (East) in the Ministry of External Affairs and as Ambassador to Vietnam. This achievement underscores India’s growing influence in global governance and highlights international confidence in its leadership and contributions to multilateral institutions.

questions.question: Between which two cities did CSIR-NGRI discover a 200 km-long underground palaeo-channel in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Scientists from the CSIR-National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) discovered a massive underground palaeo-channel stretching between Prayagraj and Kanpur in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab region. The channel, buried 10 to 15 metres below the surface and extending nearly 200 km, represents an ancient independent river system distinct from the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. The discovery was made using advanced Heliborne transient electromagnetic technology (H-TEM) along with confirmatory drilling. Researchers identified highly porous clay and sand layers within the channel, making it suitable for groundwater recharge projects. The initiative involved collaboration between CSIR-NGRI, the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG), and the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB).

questions.question: In which Union Territory was the Mahey Tokpo-Raldho irrigation canal inaugurated on May 15, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Mahey Tokpo-Raldho irrigation canal was inaugurated in the Union Territory of Ladakh by Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena on May 15, 2026. The canal, located in the high-altitude Changthang district at over 14,000 feet, was constructed to address persistent water shortages in the region. Stretching 2.10 km and supplied by Yaya Lake, the project is designed to support irrigation across nearly 100 acres of agricultural land in the Mahey region. Alongside the inauguration, a plantation drive involving 15,000 trees was also organised to promote slope stabilisation and soil conservation in the ecologically sensitive Himalayan region.

questions.question: In which city was the MoU signed on 20 April 2026 to develop India’s first Mega Greenfield Shipyard?
questions.explanation: India’s first Mega Greenfield Shipyard will be developed at Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu under a tripartite agreement involving HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering, NSHIP-TN, and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited. The project was established under the India-ROK ‘VOYAGES’ framework during the South Korean President’s state visit. The shipyard is expected to have an annual capacity of 2.5 Million Gross Tonnage and generate around 15,000 direct jobs. This initiative supports the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, which aims to make India one of the top five global shipbuilding nations by significantly increasing domestic shipbuilding capacity and maritime infrastructure development.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) located?
questions.explanation: The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) is headquartered in Pune, Maharashtra. It is a premier research and development organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). C-DAC is widely known for developing India’s first indigenous supercomputer, PARAM 8000, in 1991. The organisation plays a significant role in advanced computing, electronics, and information technology research in India. In the IP Catalyst initiative launched in 2026, C-DAC Pune was entrusted with the implementation of the programme aimed at promoting patent commercialisation and supporting innovation-driven technology development across the country.

questions.question: In which city was the National Conference on Laboratory Animal Welfare organised by the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) on May 11, 2026?
questions.explanation: The National Conference on Laboratory Animal Welfare was organised in New Delhi by the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) on May 11, 2026. The conference focused on promoting ethical research practices and ensuring animal welfare in scientific experiments. It was conducted under the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying with the theme “Policies and Best Practices of Research on Animals and their Welfare.” The event highlighted humane treatment of animals during vaccine development and drug discovery trials while also encouraging institutions to align with international animal welfare standards and responsible scientific research practices.

questions.question: Who is set to take oath as the new Chief Minister of Bihar after the resignation of the previous Chief Minister in 2026?
questions.explanation: In April 2026, Bihar witnessed a significant political transition as the long-serving Chief Minister resigned from office. Following this development, Samrat Choudhary, who was serving as the Deputy Chief Minister, was chosen to take over the top post. His appointment marks a notable shift in the state’s leadership and political dynamics. The change comes after years of continuity in governance and is expected to influence policy direction and administrative priorities. This transition reflects evolving political alignments and signals the beginning of a new phase in Bihar’s governance.

questions.question: Which country announced that former US President Donald Trump will receive its highest civilian honour in the newly created Peace category in 2026?
questions.explanation: Israel announced that Donald Trump will be awarded the Israel Prize for Peace in 2026, marking a historic departure from tradition. This is the first time in 80 years that Israel’s highest civilian honour will be given to a non-Israeli and also the first-ever awarding of the Peace category under the Israel Prize. The decision reflects Israel’s recognition of Trump’s role in Middle East peace initiatives and strong support for Israel’s security. The announcement followed high-level talks in Florida, underscoring continued diplomatic engagement between Israel and Trump-era leadership.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar for a historic 10th term in 2025?
questions.explanation: Nitish Kumar’s swearing-in for a record 10th term as Bihar’s Chief Minister marks an extraordinary milestone in Indian state politics. His leadership once again emerged at the forefront following the NDA’s commanding victory, which secured 202 seats in the 2025 Assembly elections. The grand ceremony at Patna’s Gandhi Maidan showcased the political weight of the event with participation from top national leaders, reflecting the stability and continuity he brings to Bihar’s governance. His long tenure symbolises sustained public trust, consistent administrative focus, and a political presence that has shaped Bihar’s development trajectory across multiple terms.

questions.question: How many seats did the NDA win in the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections?
questions.explanation: The NDA secured a decisive victory in the 2025 Bihar Assembly Elections by winning 202 out of 243 seats, far surpassing the required majority. This overwhelming mandate reflected a combination of strong political organization, effective campaigning, and significant support from key voter groups, especially women and youth. The impressive female voter turnout, which reached a historic high, played a crucial role in boosting the alliance’s performance. The BJP emerged as the single-largest party, and the combined strength of its partners further solidified the alliance’s dominance, marking a major shift in Bihar’s political landscape.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the 21st President of South Korea, pledging to reopen dialogue with North Korea and maintain a strong alliance with the United States?
questions.explanation: Lee Jae-myung, leader of the Liberal Democratic Party, was sworn in as South Korea’s 21st President for a five-year term. His election marked a commitment to balancing diplomacy by reopening dialogue with North Korea while maintaining a strong security alliance with the United States. His main competitor was Kim Moon-soo from the conservative People Power Party. Lee’s presidency is expected to influence South Korea’s domestic and international policies, especially concerning peace efforts on the Korean Peninsula and relations with global powers.

questions.question: What percentage of all diseases in India is accounted for by cardiovascular diseases according to the NSO Survey 2025?
questions.explanation: Cardiovascular diseases have emerged as a major health concern in India, showing a significant increase over recent years. According to the NSO Survey 2025, these diseases now account for 25.6% of all reported illnesses, making them the leading category among various health conditions. This rise reflects changing lifestyles, increased stress levels, and other risk factors such as poor diet and lack of physical activity. Notably, the impact is not limited to older populations, as younger age groups are also increasingly affected. The data highlights the urgent need for improved public health strategies, awareness campaigns, and preventive healthcare measures to address this growing burden.

questions.question: Which disease is Coartem Baby specifically developed to treat in newborns and infants?
questions.explanation: Malaria is the disease targeted by Coartem Baby, the first WHO-prequalified drug specifically designed for newborns and infants. Developed by Novartis in collaboration with the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV), this medication addresses a critical gap in pediatric treatment. It uses an artemether-lumefantrine combination and is suitable for infants weighing between 2 to 5 kilograms. The disease remains a major global health concern, causing millions of cases and deaths annually, especially among children under five in Africa, making this innovation a significant breakthrough.

questions.question: Into how many regional languages will Ayurveda research materials be translated under the CCRAS and Anuvadini AI partnership?
questions.explanation: The collaboration between the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) and Anuvadini AI focuses on making Ayurveda research widely accessible by translating it into multiple regional languages. The initiative specifically targets 13 languages, including Hindi, to ensure that valuable scientific and educational content reaches a broader audience across India. This effort helps bridge linguistic barriers, making traditional medical knowledge more inclusive and understandable. By leveraging artificial intelligence, the program enhances the dissemination of authentic information, supports regional outreach, and reduces misinformation, especially in rural and linguistically diverse populations.

questions.question: Which disease is the focus of the collaborative clinical study announced by the Ministry of Ayush and DBT using Ayurveda as an adjunct therapy?
questions.explanation: The collaborative clinical study launched by the Ministry of Ayush and the Department of Biotechnology focuses on Tuberculosis, aiming to integrate Ayurveda with standard Anti-Tuberculosis Treatment. This approach seeks to enhance recovery outcomes, improve nutrition, and elevate the quality of life for patients. A major focus is on managing TB-related cachexia, a condition involving severe weight and muscle loss. Conducted over a 24-month period across leading medical institutions such as AIIMS and JIPMER, the study reflects a scientific effort to validate traditional medicine through evidence-based research and promote holistic healthcare solutions.

questions.question: Which company has launched an affordable Semaglutide injection in India using an innovative multi-dose pen?
questions.explanation: Zydus has introduced an affordable Semaglutide injection in India, targeting the treatment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and obesity. The innovation includes a reusable multi-dose pen, allowing patients to adjust dosages conveniently from a single device, unlike traditional single-use pens. This significantly improves ease of use and reduces treatment costs, with an average monthly expense of around ₹2,200. Manufactured at the Zydus Biotech Park in Ahmedabad, the product aims to make GLP-1 therapies more accessible, especially in a country facing a growing burden of diabetes and rising obesity rates.

questions.question: How many total medals did India win at the Asian Boxing U15 Championships held in Tashkent in 2026?
questions.explanation: India delivered an impressive performance at the Asian Boxing U15 Championships held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, by winning a total of 27 medals. The medal tally included 9 gold medals across different categories, highlighting the country’s growing strength in youth boxing. The Indian U-15 girls’ team dominated the tournament by securing 7 gold medals and topping the overall standings. Notable performers included Anzee and Angel, who won gold medals in their respective weight categories. In the boys’ division, Yash Kumar and Mohd Yasser also secured gold medals. The championship showcased India’s strong potential in international amateur boxing competitions.

questions.question: Which platform partnered with SAI to launch CWG 2030 engagement initiatives in 2026?
questions.explanation: MyBharat, officially known as Mera Yuva Bharat, is a technology-driven platform launched on October 31, 2023, for youth development in India. It partnered with the Sports Authority of India (SAI) to launch nationwide digital engagement initiatives ahead of the Commonwealth Games 2030 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. These initiatives included a Torch Design Contest, CWG Reel Challenge, and CWG 2030 Quiz. The platform aims to encourage youth participation in sports, creativity, and nation-building activities through digital outreach and engagement programmes across the country.

questions.question: Who became the second youngest chess grandmaster in history in May 2026 after securing the final GM norm at the Sardinia World Chess Festival?
questions.explanation: Faustino Oro, a young chess prodigy from Argentina, achieved global recognition by becoming the second youngest grandmaster in chess history at the age of 12. He secured his final grandmaster norm during the Sardinia World Chess Festival held in Italy. Oro also became one of only a few players worldwide to earn the prestigious GM title before turning 13 years old. Earlier, he had already made history by becoming the youngest International Master and the first under-12 player to cross the 2500 ELO rating mark. His achievement reflects the growing rise of exceptionally talented young chess players in international competitions.

questions.question: Which country had its Olympic ban lifted by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for participation under its national flag at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics?
questions.explanation: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) lifted the ban on Belarus on May 7, 2026, allowing Belarusian athletes to participate under their national flag at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Belarusian teams and officials will also be included in the opening ceremony and official medal standings. In contrast, Russia continues to remain suspended because the Russian Olympic Committee unlawfully absorbed sports organisations from occupied Ukrainian territories. Russian athletes are only permitted to compete as “Individual Neutral Athletes” without national symbols. The decision reflects changing international sports policies and varying stances among global sporting federations regarding participation restrictions.

questions.question: Which city is scheduled to host the 22nd Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship 2026?
questions.explanation: The 22nd Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship 2026 is scheduled to be held in New Delhi from July 27 to August 2, 2026, at the Thyagraj Stadium. The event is being jointly organised by the Government of Delhi and the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI). Players from more than 35 Commonwealth nations, including England, Australia, Canada, South Africa, and Singapore, are expected to participate. The championship aims to strengthen India’s sports infrastructure and aligns with the Vision 2036 Olympics mission. India has previously hosted major Commonwealth sporting events, including the 2010 Commonwealth Games in New Delhi.

questions.question: Which Indian state observed the International AIDS Candlelight Memorial on May 17, 2026?
questions.explanation: Nagaland observed the International AIDS Candlelight Memorial on May 17, 2026, at the College of Nursing in Kohima. The memorial was organised under the theme “Light the Legacy: Remember. Advance. Act.” and aimed to honour individuals who lost their lives to HIV/AIDS-related illnesses while also supporting people currently living with HIV. The event emphasised the importance of reducing social stigma, improving healthcare accessibility, and encouraging collective action by governments and civil society organisations. Special focus was placed on the role of youth in spreading awareness, promoting safe practices, and encouraging social inclusion in the fight against HIV/AIDS.

questions.question: Which state organised the special "Youth and Sports Week" from May 18 to 23, 2026?
questions.explanation: Telangana organised a special “Youth and Sports Week” from May 18 to 23, 2026, to encourage youth empowerment, physical fitness, sports participation, and employment opportunities across the state. The programme was conducted under the larger 99-day public service initiative called “Praja Palana Pragathi Pranalika.” Activities during the week included marathons, career guidance sessions, youth parliament programmes, sports events, environmental cleaning drives, and employment facilitation initiatives. Events were held at district and grassroots levels, including major programmes at the L.B. Stadium in Hyderabad. The initiative aimed to actively involve students, youth organisations, athletes, and local communities in building a healthier and more empowered society.

questions.question: In which state was the Grih Pravesh of 5 lakh completed PMAY-G houses initiated on May 15, 2026?
questions.explanation: The Grih Pravesh ceremony for 5 lakh completed houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) was launched in Maharashtra by Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on May 15, 2026. The event took place in Satara and also marked the handover of keys for the 3-croreth rural house completed under the scheme. PMAY-G, launched in 2016 under the Ministry of Rural Development, aims to provide “Housing for All” in rural India. Maharashtra also received substantial central financial assistance and approval for PMGSY-IV road projects to improve rural connectivity and infrastructure across several habitations.

questions.question: Which state was selected to receive 1,243 EV chargers under the PM E-Drive scheme in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Karnataka was selected to receive 1,243 electric vehicle (EV) chargers under the central PM E-Drive scheme on May 12, 2026. The project, approved with a financial outlay of ₹123.26 crore, aims to strengthen the state’s electric mobility infrastructure and reduce range anxiety among EV users. The PM E-Drive scheme, administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, promotes clean and sustainable transportation across India. Karnataka has been a pioneer in the EV sector, becoming the first Indian state to introduce a dedicated Electric Vehicle and Energy Storage Policy in 2017. The state also leads the country in EV startups and public charging infrastructure development.

questions.question: Which Indian state celebrated 51 years of statehood on May 16, 2026?
questions.explanation: Sikkim celebrated its 51st Statehood Day on May 16, 2026, marking more than five decades since it officially became a state of India in 1975. Before joining India, Sikkim functioned as an independent Himalayan kingdom ruled by the Chogyal monarchy under the Namgyal dynasty. Growing political demands for democratic governance and public participation led to a historic referendum in 1975, where the majority supported integration with India. Following this, the monarchy was abolished, and the 36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975, formally made Sikkim the 22nd state of India. The state is also known for its rich cultural diversity and strong Buddhist heritage.

questions.question: What is the theme of the 18th edition of the Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF)?
questions.explanation: The theme of the 18th edition of the Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF) is "India in Amrit Kaal". This theme reflects the focus of the festival on showcasing India's cultural, social, and artistic richness during a period of prosperity and creativity, emphasizing innovation and creativity in documentary filmmaking. The festival also inaugurated its first Documentary Film Bazaar, providing a platform for filmmakers to showcase their documentaries and compete for awards, including a cash prize of Rs 1 lakh, along with a trophy and certificate.

questions.question: Which country has pledged to provide military support to Ukraine worth 1 billion euros?
questions.explanation: Spain has committed to providing military aid to Ukraine amounting to 1 billion euros ($1.08 billion) under an agreement. This aid package includes a dozen U.S.-made Patriot anti-aircraft missiles, 19 second-hand German-made Leopard 2A4 tanks, along with other Spanish-made weapons. This initiative highlights Spain's role in supporting Ukraine amid geopolitical tensions and demonstrates bilateral cooperation between the two nations.

questions.question: Which institution inaugurated a dedicated Incubation Centre for Startups in Weather and Climate and hosted WISE-2026 in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) Pune inaugurated a dedicated Incubation Center for Startups in Weather and Climate on May 15, 2026, and also hosted the Weather and Climate Innovation Meet for Startups and Entrepreneurs (WISE-2026). The initiative was launched under the Ministry of Earth Sciences to encourage innovation and private sector participation in meteorological and climate services. The incubation centre operates as a major component of the National Enterprise for Atmospheric Technology (NEAT) initiative. The event witnessed participation from hundreds of attendees, including startup founders and experts from institutions such as IMD, NCMRWF, NCPOR, ICRISAT, IISER Pune, and several IITs to advance climate-tech innovation in India.

questions.question: Which company partnered with the Adani Group on May 16, 2026, to establish its first data centre in India?
questions.explanation: Uber partnered with the Adani Group to establish its first data centre in India as part of a strategic technology and infrastructure collaboration. The agreement was finalised after a meeting between Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi and Gautam Adani in Ahmedabad. The facility is expected to become operational by the end of 2026 and will support Uber’s technological expansion in India. The project aligns with Adani Group’s broader vision of investing $100 billion in renewable-energy-powered and AI-ready data centres by 2035. The infrastructure is being developed through Adani Connex, which is building a large-scale five-gigawatt data centre platform across India.

questions.question: Which institution commissioned India's first Integrated CCUS Field Laboratory Facility in May 2026?
questions.explanation: IIT Bombay commissioned India’s first Integrated Carbon Capture, Utilisation, and Storage (CCUS) Field Laboratory Facility under Bharat Innovates 2026 on May 11, 2026. The indigenously developed pilot facility has the capacity to process up to 3 tonnes of carbon dioxide per day using advanced aqueous-based catalytic CO₂ capture technology. The system can capture carbon dioxide from ambient air and industrial emissions using non-potable water sources such as seawater and industrial effluents. The project also includes geological sequestration in the Deccan Traps to permanently store CO₂. IIT Bombay, established in 1958, is an Institute of National Importance located in Powai, Mumbai.

questions.question: Which organisation, functioning under the Ministry of Science & Technology, facilitated the transfer of 13 indigenous technologies developed by the Central Building Research Institute to industries and start-ups on National Technology Day 2026?
questions.explanation: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) is an autonomous body operating under the Ministry of Science & Technology. It facilitated the transfer of 13 indigenous technologies developed by the Central Building Research Institute (CBRI) during the National Technology Day event held on May 12, 2026. These technologies were related to fire safety, sustainable construction, infrastructure protection, energy efficiency, and advanced building materials. Headquartered in New Delhi and established in 1942, the organisation plays a major role in advancing scientific research, innovation, and industrial development in India through its network of laboratories and institutes.

questions.question: What is the name of the AI-powered virtual assistant launched by the judiciary in May 2026 to help litigants access judicial services?
questions.explanation: Su Sahay is an Artificial Intelligence-powered chatbot launched by the Indian judiciary to improve access to judicial services for citizens and litigants. Introduced alongside the One Case One Data initiative, the chatbot was developed by the National Informatics Centre in collaboration with the Supreme Court Registry. Its main purpose is to provide front-end assistance, guide users through judicial procedures, and offer access to live court updates and official legal information. The initiative aims to modernise the judicial system through digital integration, reduce administrative barriers, and make legal services more accessible and transparent for the general public across India.

questions.question: After whom will Pakyong Airport in Sikkim be renamed to honour his contribution to India’s freedom struggle?
questions.explanation: Trilochan Pokhrel is being honoured through the renaming of Pakyong Airport in Sikkim in recognition of his significant role in India’s freedom movement. Popularly known as “Gandhi Pokhrel,” he is regarded as Sikkim’s first independence activist and actively participated in major national movements such as the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement. Inspired by Mahatma Gandhi, he worked to spread nationalist ideas within Sikkim. The renaming symbolises the state’s effort to preserve its historical legacy and acknowledge local heroes who contributed to India’s independence.

questions.question: Which company has introduced a feature that allows users to change their primary Gmail address without losing emails, photos, or messages?
questions.explanation: Google has rolled out a new Gmail feature enabling users to change their primary @gmail.com address while retaining all account data. Emails, photos, chats, Drive files, and subscriptions remain intact, and the old email becomes an alias, ensuring continuity of communication. This update eliminates the need to create a new account or migrate data manually, offering greater flexibility and convenience for users who want a professional or updated email address. By maintaining login credentials, linked services, and subscription details, Google ensures a seamless transition without disrupting daily usage.

questions.question: Which organization released the Hindi translation of the Lithuanian novel “The Last Day,” titled “Antim Din”?
questions.explanation: Sahitya Akademi, under the Ministry of Culture, launched the Hindi edition of Lithuanian author Jaroslavas Melnikas’s novel “The Last Day”, titled “Antim Din”. This initiative marks the first-ever translation of a Lithuanian fiction work into Hindi, representing a milestone in India–Lithuania literary collaboration. The novel, translated by Dr. Poonam Tiwari, was released at Rabindra Bhawan, New Delhi, in partnership with the Embassy of Lithuania. The event underscored the Akademi’s mission to promote global literature in Indian languages and foster cultural understanding through translation, making international literary masterpieces more accessible to Indian readers.

questions.question: In which city was the 20th East Asia Summit held where the Kuala Lumpur Declaration was adopted?
questions.explanation: The 20th East Asia Summit took place in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, where member nations adopted the Kuala Lumpur Declaration reaffirming their shared commitment to peace, stability, and multilateral cooperation. The declaration emphasised ASEAN’s central role in regional architecture and endorsed transparent, rules-based approaches to conflict resolution. It also reinforced the EAS’s informal, leaders-led framework for strategic dialogue and cooperation on security, economic, and developmental issues. Amid shifting global power dynamics and regional tensions, the summit’s outcome in Kuala Lumpur underscored the importance of collaboration, trust-building, and a unified commitment to stability across the East Asian region.

questions.question: Which project was jointly inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi and Singapore PM Lawrence Wong on September 4, 2025?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong virtually inaugurated the PSA Mumbai Terminal Phase-II at Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPA) on September 4, 2025. This expansion has raised the terminal’s capacity to 4.8 million TEUs, officially making it the largest container terminal in India. Operated by Singapore-based PSA International, the facility is equipped with state-of-the-art cranes, automated systems, and a direct rail link to the Dedicated Freight Corridor. The project not only enhances India’s maritime infrastructure but also strengthens India-Singapore economic cooperation. It will significantly reduce logistics costs, improve cargo efficiency, and boost India’s competitiveness in global trade.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey was fought in
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey, 23 June 1757, was a decisive British East India Company victory over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies, establishing Company rule in South Asia which expanded over much of the Indies for the next 190 years. The battle took place at Palashi, Bengal, on the river banks of the Bhagirathi River, about 150 km north of Calcutta, near Murshidabad, then capital of undivided Bengal. The belligerents were Siraj-ud-daulah, the last independent Nawab of Bengal, and the British East India Company.More info:http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Plassey

Its design is that of the wheel which appears on the abacus of the Sarnath Lion Capital of Ashoka. Its diameter comes close to the width of the white band & it has twenty four spokes. The design of the National Flag of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on 22 July 1947.

In India, around 100 million people currently use tobacco, and approximately 45.7 million employees are involved in tobacco manufacturing and allied activities, including nearly 20 million farmers. This clearly indicates that tobacco use and production operate on a very large scale.

Due to this significant dependence, a sudden ban on tobacco may not be practical. Abrupt prohibition could have serious consequences for habitual users, including severe withdrawal effects and behavioural issues. Moreover, an immediate ban would negatively impact farmers and workers whose livelihoods depend on tobacco cultivation and manufacturing.

Therefore, instead of an instant ban, a gradual and phased reduction is a more effective approach. The first step should be to create strong awareness programs, especially targeting young people, to prevent new users from adopting tobacco habits. At the same time, the government should take responsibility for providing alternative employment opportunities and support systems for farmers and workers who rely on the tobacco industry.

By implementing these measures in parallel, India can realistically move toward the goal of a tobacco-free nation. This approach has already shown positive results. For example, in 2015, around 130 million people in India used tobacco, whereas the number has now reduced to approximately 100 million. This decline proves that, with sustained cooperation between the government and the public, India can eventually become a tobacco-free country.

Today, we are discussing a very important and relevant topic.
Is India ready for Electric Vehicles?
India is progressively moving toward readiness for electric vehicles (EVs), but it is not fully prepared yet, as the transition involves both strong advantages and notable challenges.

On the positive side, EVs offer a clean and sustainable alternative to conventional vehicles, helping reduce air pollution and carbon emissions an important factor for a country like India with rising environmental concerns.
The government is actively promoting EV adoption through initiatives such as FAME subsidies, tax benefits, and state-level incentives, which are encouraging both manufacturers and consumers.

Additionally, the growing investment from companies like Tata, Mahindra, and new startups, along with increasing awareness among people, has led to a significant rise in EV sales, especially in two-wheelers and three-wheelers. However, despite this progress, several obstacles remain. The charging infrastructure is still insufficient and unevenly distributed, mainly concentrated in urban areas, creating inconvenience for long-distance travel and rural users. Range anxiety, long charging times, and high initial costs of EVs continue to discourage many potential buyers.

Both creativity and efficiency are essential, but their importance depends on the situation.
Creativity is the ability to think differently and generate new ideas. It drives innovation, problem-solving, and growth.

For example, companies like Apple and Google succeed because of their creative thinking, which leads to unique products and solutions. Without creativity, organisations may become stagnant and fail to adapt to change.

On the other hand, efficiency focuses on doing tasks correctly with minimum time, cost, and resources. It ensures productivity, consistency, and profitability. For instance, in manufacturing, healthcare, or emergency services, efficiency is crucial to meet deadlines and avoid losses.

In reality, creativity without efficiency may remain just an idea, while efficiency without creativity may lead to repetition and lack of progress. A creative idea becomes valuable only when executed efficiently.
