With over three decades of experience in the coal sector, Sairam brings extensive technical and managerial expertise. His previous roles at Northern Coalfields Limited and Central Coalfields Limited involved major infrastructure, logistics, and capacity expansion initiatives, making him well-suited to guide Coal India amid rising production demands and energy security expectations.

questions.question: Which pair of grandmasters led Alpine SG Pipers to their maiden Global Chess League 2025 title?
questions.explanation: The Global Chess League 2025 Season 3 witnessed a landmark achievement as Alpine SG Pipers clinched their first-ever title. The team’s success was driven by the outstanding leadership and performances of R Praggnanandhaa and Anish Giri. Anish Giri delivered exceptional consistency and tactical brilliance, winning crucial games and earning the MVP of the Finals award. R Praggnanandhaa complemented this with a decisive and timely victory in the second match, showcasing maturity under pressure. Together, their combined efforts proved vital in defeating the defending champions and securing the championship.

questions.question: Who has been elected as the Chair of the Badminton World Federation (BWF) Athletes’ Commission for the 2026–2029 term?
questions.explanation: PV Sindhu’s election as Chair of the BWF Athletes’ Commission marks an important milestone in her career beyond competitive badminton. As a two-time Olympic medallist and former world champion, she brings immense experience and credibility to global sports governance. In her new role, she will represent the voices and concerns of badminton players worldwide and serve as a member of the BWF Council, directly influencing policy and decision-making. Her long association with the commission since 2017 and work as a BWF Integrity Ambassador underline her commitment to athlete welfare, fairness, and integrity in the sport.

questions.question: What does the REPM scheme primarily aim to achieve in order to strengthen India’s self-reliance in critical minerals and advanced manufacturing?

options.A: Encourage Import of Rare Earth Minerals
options.B: Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets

questions.explanation: The REPM scheme represents a strategic initiative to build India’s first fully integrated domestic manufacturing ecosystem for high-value rare earth permanent magnets. Its core focus is to promote manufacturing of sintered rare earth permanent magnets, which are vital for sectors such as electric vehicles, renewable energy, electronics, aerospace, and defence. By developing end-to-end capacity from rare earth oxides to finished magnets, the scheme aims to reduce dependence on imports, particularly from China. With an approved outlay of over ₹7,000 crore, the initiative supports long-term national goals like Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat by 2047 while strengthening supply-chain resilience.

questions.question: In which district of Kashmir was a 2,000-year-old Buddhist site with Kushan-era stupas and monastic structures recently unearthed?
questions.explanation: The archaeological discovery involved the excavation of an ancient Buddhist site located in Zehanpora village, which falls within the Baramulla district of Kashmir. Researchers identified Kushan-era stupas and monastic buildings, pointing to the region’s strong Buddhist heritage around 2,000 years ago. The location was pinpointed using a combination of historical clues, including blurred photographs preserved in a French museum and modern drone surveys that revealed artificial mounds. The findings are significant as they connect ancient Kashmir with the Gandhara trade route and the Kushan capital of Huvishkapura, highlighting Baramulla’s historical importance.

questions.question: Which Indian state is launching the country’s first public-private partnership (PPP) model medical colleges?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh is set to become the first state in India to introduce medical colleges under the public-private partnership model. The initiative involves establishing new medical colleges in the districts of Dhar and Betul, where private partners will be responsible for building the required infrastructure. At the same time, the state government will retain administrative control over the associated district hospitals. These hospitals will be upgraded in strict compliance with National Medical Commission norms, ensuring quality medical education and healthcare delivery. This model aims to strengthen medical infrastructure while maintaining public oversight.

questions.question: Which organization partnered with DRDO’s Defence Materials and Stores Research & Development Establishment to collaborate on research, testing, and facility sharing related to non-metallic materials?

options.B: ouncil of Scientific and Industrial Research

questions.explanation: A strategic memorandum of understanding was signed to strengthen research and technical collaboration in the field of non-metallic materials such as polymers, ceramics, and technical textiles. The agreement emphasizes joint research activities, shared testing facilities, and coordinated efforts to enhance material evaluation capabilities crucial for national defence. In addition to research and testing, the collaboration also includes organizing seminars and workshops aimed at building technical skills and knowledge among professionals. Through this partnership, National Test House plays a key role in supporting advanced material development and quality assurance aligned with defence requirements.

questions.question: Who won the Women’s Singles title at the 87th Senior National Badminton Championships held in Vijayawada?
questions.explanation: The Women’s Singles title at the 87th Senior National Badminton Championships was claimed by Surya Charishma Tamiri, marking a significant achievement in her badminton career. The prestigious national tournament was held in Vijayawada and featured top players from across the country competing in various categories. While Surya Charishma Tamiri emerged victorious in the women’s singles event, the championships also saw Rithvik Sanjeevi S winning the men’s singles title. Multiple doubles titles were decided as well, highlighting the depth of talent and competitive spirit present at the national level of Indian badminton.

questions.question: Which Indian chess player won a historic bronze medal at the World Rapid Chess Championship, securing India’s first male podium finish since Viswanathan Anand?
questions.explanation: The achievement highlights a significant milestone in Indian chess on the global stage, achieved by Arjun Erigaisi. Finishing third with an impressive score of 9.5 out of 13 points, Arjun Erigaisi delivered a consistent and high-quality performance throughout the championship. A crucial victory in the final round allowed him to edge past strong competitors such as Hans Niemann and Leinier Dominguez on tiebreaks. This result marked India’s first male podium finish at the World Rapid Chess Championship since Viswanathan Anand, underscoring Arjun Erigaisi’s rise as a leading figure in international chess.

questions.question: Which Indian chess player clinched the bronse medal at the World Rapid Championship after finishing joint-first but losing out on tiebreaks?
questions.explanation: Koneru Humpy delivered an outstanding performance at the World Rapid Championship by finishing joint-first with a score of 8.5 out of 11 points. Despite remaining undefeated throughout the tournament, she had to settle for the bronze medal due to inferior tiebreaks after a draw in the final round denied her a chance at gold. The championship title was eventually claimed by Aleksandra Goryachkina following a playoff win against China’s Zhu Jiner. Koneru Humpy’s consistent and resilient play once again highlighted her status as one of India’s most accomplished and reliable chess grandmasters on the global stage.

questions.question: In which Indian state did Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurate dairy, cooperative, and allied development projects, including the Vita Milk Chilling Centre and the HAFED Flour Mill?
questions.explanation: The initiatives highlighted involve major dairy and cooperative infrastructure developments inaugurated by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. These include the Vita Milk Chilling Centre at Salempur village in Bhiwani district, constructed by the Haryana Dairy Cooperative Development Federation at a cost of ₹3.30 crore, and the HAFED Flour Mill at Jatusana in Rewari district. Additionally, a portal dedicated to the International Year of Cooperatives was launched. All the locations mentioned—Bhiwani and Rewari districts—are administrative regions within the state of Haryana, clearly identifying Haryana as the state where these projects were inaugurated.

questions.question: Which country has announced a $2.2 billion plan to build a multi-layered anti-drone wall along its border?
questions.explanation: Poland has unveiled an ambitious $2.2 billion initiative to construct a multi-layered anti-drone defensive system along its 700-kilometre border with Belarus and Ukraine. The project aims to counter emerging aerial threats by integrating advanced electronic warfare measures, such as drone jamming, with kinetic defence systems including cannons, machine guns, and missiles. The construction will take place in phases, with initial operational capability expected within six months and full completion targeted within two years. This move reflects Poland’s growing focus on strengthening border security amid evolving regional security challenges in Eastern Europe.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the Supreme Court affirm that the right to hold or renew a passport is part of personal liberty?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court reaffirmed that the right to personal liberty, which includes the right to hold or renew a passport, flows from Article 21 of the Indian Constitution. The Court emphasised that personal liberty is not a concession granted by the State but a fundamental constitutional obligation. In the Mahesh Agarwal vs Union of India case, it clarified that the mere pendency of criminal proceedings cannot automatically deprive an individual of passport rights. Any restriction on such rights must follow due process of law and meet constitutional standards, reinforcing the expansive and protective scope of Article 21.

questions.question: Who became the first bowler in the history of T20 Internationals to take eight wickets in a single match?
questions.explanation: Sonam Yeshey created a historic milestone in international cricket by becoming the first bowler ever to claim eight wickets in a single T20 International match. Representing Bhutan, he achieved this remarkable feat during the third T20I against Myanmar on December 26, 2025. Bowling with exceptional control and pace, he recorded extraordinary figures of 8 wickets for just 7 runs in his full quota of four overs, including a maiden over. His spell dismantled Myanmar’s batting lineup, restricting them to only 45 runs and helping Bhutan secure a dominant victory and an unassailable lead in the series.

questions.question: Which company received RBI registration as a Type II Non-Banking Financial Institution, enabling its parent to expand into lending and credit activities?
questions.explanation: Aryaman Finance Ltd is the entity that obtained registration from the Reserve Bank of India on December 24, 2025, as a Type II Non-Banking Financial Institution, classified as a non-deposit taking Investment and Credit Company. This regulatory approval allows the company to legally operate in the lending and credit space. With this development, the parent company, Aryaman Financial Services Ltd, gains the ability to diversify its business operations beyond merchant banking. The RBI license is significant because it marks a strategic expansion into regulated financial activities, strengthening the group’s overall financial services portfolio.

questions.question: At which location was the successful maiden flight test of the Pinaka LRGR-120 rocket conducted?
questions.explanation: The successful maiden flight test of the Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket (LRGR-120) was conducted at Chandipur in Odisha. This location houses the Integrated Test Range, a key facility operated by the Defence Research and Development Organisation for testing advanced missile and rocket systems. The trial marked an important milestone in India’s defence capabilities, as the Pinaka LRGR-120 demonstrated its maximum strike range of 120 km. Conducting the test at Chandipur ensured precise tracking and evaluation of the rocket’s performance, accuracy, and guidance systems, reinforcing India’s growing expertise in indigenous long-range guided weapon technologies.

questions.question: Which Indian state launched the ‘e-Swasthya Samvad’ digital platform to enhance transparency and coordination in medical education?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan launched the ‘e-Swasthya Samvad’ digital platform on December 28, 2025, with the objective of improving transparency, communication, and coordination in the field of medical education. The initiative facilitates regular interaction between medical staff, administrators, and students through video conferencing sessions held twice a week on Tuesdays and Thursdays. A key feature of the platform is the mandatory submission of action-taken reports within 72 hours for all decisions taken during these interactions. This mechanism ensures accountability, timely follow-up, and more efficient governance in medical institutions across the state.

questions.question: Which country launched the live-fire military drills code-named “Justice Mission 2025” around Taiwan?
questions.explanation: China conducted large-scale live-fire military exercises around Taiwan under the code name “Justice Mission 2025” on December 29, 2025. The drills involved the deployment of 89 aircraft and 28 naval vessels, demonstrating significant military coordination and capability. These exercises were designed to simulate a blockade of Taiwan’s ports, highlighting China’s strategic intent in the region. Beijing characterised the operation as a stern warning in response to U.S. arms sales to Taiwan and support from Japan. The drills underscore heightened geopolitical tensions in the Taiwan Strait and China’s assertive posture in regional security affairs.

questions.question: Who became the first painter to receive the 2025 Most Achieved Chinese Award (MACA)?
questions.explanation: Zhang Damo made history by becoming the first painter to be honoured with the 2025 Most Achieved Chinese Award (MACA), an award previously given to eminent figures from science and architecture. He is widely recognised for his distinctive ink painting style that combines meticulous detailing with freehand expression, blending ancient Eastern philosophy with modern artistic aesthetics. Beyond his artistic achievements, Zhang Damo has played a significant role in promoting Chinese culture globally. Serving as the Chief Artist of the UN Peace Boat, he has spent more than three decades acting as a cultural ambassador, using art to foster cross-cultural understanding and international dialogue.

questions.question: In which Indian state was the first-ever camera-trap sighting of a Clouded Leopard in Kakoi Reserve Forest recorded?
questions.explanation: The first-ever camera-trap evidence of a Clouded Leopard in Kakoi Reserve Forest was recorded in the state of Assam on December 28, 2025. This sighting is significant as it confirms the presence of this elusive and vulnerable species in smaller forest patches beyond major national parks. The Clouded Leopard, scientifically known as Neofelis nebulosa, is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List and enjoys the highest level of legal protection under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The finding highlights the ecological importance of reserve forests in conserving endangered wildlife.

questions.question: Which provision of the Indian Constitution is violated when civilian awards like Bharat Ratna or Padma awards are used as prefixes or suffixes to a person’s name?
questions.explanation: The Bombay High Court clarified that using civilian awards such as the Bharat Ratna or Padma awards as prefixes or suffixes to a person’s name violates Article 18(1) of the Indian Constitution. Article 18(1) prohibits the State from conferring titles, ensuring equality among citizens. Although these awards are constitutionally valid as honours recognizing excellence, they are not titles and must not be treated as such. Misuse of these honours as name attachments undermines the constitutional principle of equality and can lead to forfeiture under Regulation 10, reinforcing the need for strict compliance with constitutional values.

questions.question: Which Indian cricketer became the second from the country and the fourth woman globally to score 10,000 international runs in women’s cricket?
questions.explanation: Smriti Mandhana achieved a historic milestone by becoming the second Indian woman and the fourth female cricketer worldwide to complete 10,000 runs in international cricket. She reached this landmark during the fourth T20I against Sri Lanka at Thiruvananthapuram. Her achievement reflects remarkable consistency across Test, ODI, and T20I formats. In the same match, she played a brilliant knock of 80 runs, helping India post their highest-ever women’s T20I total. This feat placed her alongside legends like Mithali Raj, Suzie Bates, and Charlotte Edwards, highlighting her status as one of the finest batters in modern women’s cricket.

questions.question: What was the growth rate of India’s Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in November 2025, marking a 25-month high?
questions.explanation: The Index of Industrial Production recorded a growth of 6.7% in November 2025, which was the highest level seen in the past 25 months. This 6.7% expansion was mainly driven by a strong recovery in manufacturing and a sharp rise in capital goods output. Higher manufacturing activity reflected improved demand, increased production, and better capacity utilization. At the same time, strong capital goods growth indicated renewed investment momentum in the economy. Overall, the 6.7% IIP growth highlighted improving industrial health and strengthening economic resilience in India.

questions.question: In which city will the Indian AI Research Organization (IAIRO) be established from January 2026?
questions.explanation: The Indian AI Research Organization is set to be established at GIFT City in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, marking a significant step in strengthening India’s artificial intelligence ecosystem. Gandhinagar was chosen due to GIFT City’s status as a premier global financial and technology hub with world-class digital and physical infrastructure. The location offers proximity to fintech, pharmaceutical companies, startups, and innovation-driven institutions. Establishing IAIRO in Gandhinagar supports collaboration between government, industry, and academia under a public–private partnership model, while aligning with national initiatives like the India AI Mission and Gujarat’s AI Action Plan.

questions.question: Which senior IPS officer has been given the additional charge of Director General of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) by the Ministry of Home Affairs?
questions.explanation: Rakesh Aggarwal has been assigned the additional charge of Director General of the National Investigation Agency to ensure continuity at the helm of India’s premier counter-terrorism body. A 1994 batch IPS officer of the Himachal Pradesh cadre, he is currently serving as Special Director General of the NIA. The decision followed the premature repatriation of the previous chief, Sadanand Date. Known for his extensive experience in counter-terrorism, terror financing, and radicalisation-related cases, Rakesh Aggarwal’s appointment reflects the government’s emphasis on operational experience and institutional stability in handling sensitive national security investigations.

questions.question: What is the designation of the Pinaka variant that was successfully tested by DRDO with a maximum range of 120 km?
questions.explanation: The Defence Research and Development Organisation successfully conducted the maiden flight test of the Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket, designated as LRGR-120, in December 2025. The LRGR-120 demonstrated a maximum range of 120 km with high precision and in-flight manoeuvrability, meeting all mission objectives. Developed by multiple DRDO laboratories, the rocket is compatible with existing Pinaka launchers, enhancing operational flexibility. The successful test validated the accuracy, reliability, and stability of the LRGR-120, significantly strengthening India’s indigenous rocket artillery capabilities and boosting the combat readiness of the armed forces.

questions.question: Which country announced that former US President Donald Trump will receive its highest civilian honour in the newly created Peace category in 2026?
questions.explanation: Israel announced that Donald Trump will be awarded the Israel Prize for Peace in 2026, marking a historic departure from tradition. This is the first time in 80 years that Israel’s highest civilian honour will be given to a non-Israeli and also the first-ever awarding of the Peace category under the Israel Prize. The decision reflects Israel’s recognition of Trump’s role in Middle East peace initiatives and strong support for Israel’s security. The announcement followed high-level talks in Florida, underscoring continued diplomatic engagement between Israel and Trump-era leadership.

questions.question: Which institution is partnering with the Delhi government to develop the AI-based Intelligent Grievance Monitoring System (IGMS)?
questions.explanation: The Delhi government has partnered with IIT Kanpur to develop the Intelligent Grievance Monitoring System, an AI-powered platform aimed at improving public grievance redressal. IIT Kanpur is responsible for system integration, ensuring secure API connectivity, conducting cybersecurity audits, and performing vulnerability assessments and penetration testing. The collaboration leverages IIT Kanpur’s technical expertise in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cybersecurity. By integrating multiple grievance portals into a single dashboard, the initiative seeks to reduce delays, eliminate duplication, enhance transparency, and enable data-driven governance, ultimately strengthening citizen trust in public service delivery.

questions.question: In which city was the world’s first administration of the ITVISMA gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy carried out?
questions.explanation: The world’s first administration of ITVISMA gene therapy took place in Abu Dhabi at Sheikh Khalifa Medical City. This historic achievement marked a major advancement in precision medicine and genomics-based healthcare. ITVISMA is a one-time gene therapy designed to treat spinal muscular atrophy by addressing its genetic root cause. The successful administration positioned Abu Dhabi as a global leader in advanced healthcare and rare disease treatment. It also demonstrated the UAE’s strong regulatory framework, clinical readiness, and commitment to providing world-class medical innovations to patients.

questions.question: Which bird sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh has been declared an Eco-Sensitive Zone to enhance biodiversity conservation and promote responsible ecotourism?
questions.explanation: The Union government designated the Parvati Arga Bird Sanctuary as an Eco-Sensitive Zone to provide enhanced protection to its fragile wetland ecosystem. Spread across about 1,084 hectares in Uttar Pradesh, the sanctuary is an important habitat for both resident and migratory birds, including species arriving from Central Asia and Tibet. Eco-Sensitive Zone status helps regulate activities around the sanctuary, reducing threats such as pollution, unplanned construction, and habitat degradation. The move supports long-term biodiversity conservation while encouraging sustainable, nature-based tourism that balances ecological protection with local livelihood opportunities.

questions.question: Which country was overtaken by India to become the world’s fourth-largest economy in 2025?
questions.explanation: India achieved a major economic milestone in 2025 by becoming the world’s fourth-largest economy in nominal GDP terms. With a GDP valued at $4.18 trillion, India moved ahead of Japan, which had long been among the top global economies. This achievement reflects strong domestic consumption, sustained structural reforms, rising investment activity, and robust GDP growth rates. Accelerating quarterly growth and positive projections from international institutions further underline India’s economic momentum. Surpassing Japan also signals a broader shift in global economic power toward emerging economies and strengthens India’s role in global economic decision-making.+

questions.question: How many countries received $5.8 million from the Kunming Biodiversity Fund to promote nature-friendly agriculture?
questions.explanation: A total of seven countries — Cook Islands, Madagascar, Mexico, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Turkey, and Uganda — collectively received $5.8 million from the Kunming Biodiversity Fund. The funding supports projects that integrate biodiversity into agricultural practices, empower local communities, and control invasive species. Backed by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the initiative aligns with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. By encouraging eco-friendly farming and strengthening biodiversity protection, the program promotes sustainable agriculture that benefits both ecosystems and local livelihoods across multiple regions.

questions.question: Which global technology company has partnered with Reliance Industries to strengthen India’s AI infrastructure and expand access to AI tools?
questions.explanation: Google has partnered with Reliance Industries to enhance India’s AI infrastructure and make artificial intelligence more accessible across the nation. The collaboration focuses on developing local AI computing power, promoting innovation, and supporting the “AI for All” mission. Through this alliance, Jio users aged 18 to 25 will receive 18 months of free access to Google Gemini Pro, empowering young Indians to explore AI technologies. The partnership also includes efforts to build AI models for Indian languages and establish domestic data centers powered by green energy, thereby boosting India’s digital inclusion, sustainability, and technological self-reliance.

questions.question: Which country co-chaired the annual health partnership meeting with India to review the 2025 Progress Report and approve Phase IV work plans for 2025–26?
questions.explanation: The annual partnership meeting between India and Norway focused on reviewing the 2025 Progress Report and approving Phase IV work plans for 2025–26 under the Norway India Partnership Initiative (NIPI). This collaboration aims to enhance public health outcomes through innovation and data-driven decision-making. One of its major achievements is the Indian Public Health Standards – Open Data Kit Tool, which enables states to identify healthcare gaps and receive focused support efficiently. The partnership showcases strong bilateral cooperation in improving maternal, newborn, and child health systems across India through technology and evidence-based planning.

questions.question: After whom has the FIDE Chess World Cup 2025 trophy been renamed?
questions.explanation: The FIDE Chess World Cup 2025 trophy has been renamed the Viswanathan Anand Cup to honour India’s legendary chess grandmaster and five-time World Champion. This decision celebrates Anand’s immense contributions to global chess and his role in inspiring generations of Indian players. Known as the “Tiger of Madras,” Anand’s achievements transformed chess into a mainstream sport in India. The renaming was announced during a ceremony in Goa, attended by key dignitaries, including the FIDE President and Indian officials. The tribute marks a proud recognition of Anand’s lasting legacy in the international chess community.

questions.question: Which senior IDAS officer took charge as the Financial Advisor (Defence Services) on November 1, 2025?
questions.explanation: Shri Raj Kumar Arora, a 1990-batch officer of the Indian Defence Accounts Service (IDAS), has assumed charge as the Financial Advisor (Defence Services) on November 1, 2025. With over three decades of experience in defence finance, budgeting, audit, and policy, he brings vast expertise to one of India’s most critical financial positions. Before this role, he served as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) and held senior posts in the UPSC, Ministry of Defence, and Ministry of Finance. His leadership is expected to enhance fiscal efficiency, transparency, and strategic financial planning in India’s defence establishment.

questions.question: Which organization released the Hindi translation of the Lithuanian novel “The Last Day,” titled “Antim Din”?
questions.explanation: Sahitya Akademi, under the Ministry of Culture, launched the Hindi edition of Lithuanian author Jaroslavas Melnikas’s novel “The Last Day”, titled “Antim Din”. This initiative marks the first-ever translation of a Lithuanian fiction work into Hindi, representing a milestone in India–Lithuania literary collaboration. The novel, translated by Dr. Poonam Tiwari, was released at Rabindra Bhawan, New Delhi, in partnership with the Embassy of Lithuania. The event underscored the Akademi’s mission to promote global literature in Indian languages and foster cultural understanding through translation, making international literary masterpieces more accessible to Indian readers.

questions.question: On which date will World Vegan Day 2025 be celebrated?
questions.explanation: World Vegan Day 2025 will be celebrated on November 1, marking the beginning of World Vegan Month. The day is dedicated to promoting vegan living, sustainability, and compassion toward all living beings. It encourages people to adopt a plant-based lifestyle that avoids animal exploitation and supports environmental protection. Events such as awareness campaigns, vegan fairs, and cooking workshops are held globally to highlight the benefits of veganism for human health, animal welfare, and the planet. Established in 1994 by Louise Wallis of the Vegan Society UK, the day continues to inspire sustainable and ethical choices worldwide.

questions.question: Which company has partnered with OpenAI to integrate its digital wallet into ChatGPT, becoming the platform’s first integrated payments wallet?
questions.explanation: PayPal has partnered with OpenAI to become ChatGPT’s first integrated digital payments wallet, allowing users to make secure purchases directly within the AI platform. This collaboration enables seamless e-commerce by letting users click “Buy with PayPal” in ChatGPT for instant payments. The move strengthens PayPal’s role in the emerging field of AI-powered commerce, showcasing its commitment to innovation and user trust through secure checkout, buyer protection, and verified transactions. By aligning with OpenAI’s growing ecosystem, PayPal positions itself at the forefront of the digital payment revolution, blending convenience, safety, and artificial intelligence to shape the future of online shopping.

questions.question: Which country agreed to cut tariffs on Chinese imports from 57% to 47% as part of the one-year truce on rare earth exports?
questions.explanation: The United States agreed to reduce tariffs on Chinese imports from 57% to 47% following diplomatic negotiations with China in Busan, South Korea. This deal temporarily eased tensions between the two major economies, marking a one-year truce on rare earth exports. The U.S. concessions were part of a broader agreement that included China’s resumption of soybean purchases and increased action against fentanyl trafficking, reflecting efforts by both sides to stabilise trade relations and promote economic cooperation despite ongoing strategic competition.

questions.question: Which country launched the Fully Digital Marine Fisheries Census 2025 using multilingual Android apps developed by ICAR-CMFRI?
questions.explanation: India launched the Fully Digital Marine Fisheries Census 2025, marking a major technological leap in fisheries data collection. This initiative replaces traditional paper-based surveys with advanced multilingual Android applications — VyAS-BHARAT, VyAS-SUTRA, and VyAS-NAV — developed by ICAR-CMFRI. The census aims to comprehensively cover 1.2 million fisher households across 5,000 marine villages in 13 coastal states and union territories. By integrating real-time geo-referenced data, drone-based craft enumeration, and dashboard monitoring, India is modernizing fisheries management, improving data accuracy, and enabling informed policymaking for the sustainable development of the marine sector.

questions.question: Across which front is India conducting the tri-service military exercise ‘Ex Trishul’?
questions.explanation: ‘Ex Trishul’ is a large-scale tri-service exercise conducted by India along its Western Front, which borders Pakistan. The exercise brings together the Army, Navy, and Air Force to enhance interoperability, coordination, and joint combat readiness. Held across Gujarat and Rajasthan from October 30 to November 10, 2025, it focuses on integrated operations involving land, sea, and air components. With over 20,000 troops and advanced assets like Rafale jets, Arjun tanks, and naval destroyers, the exercise demonstrates India’s preparedness, technological strength, and commitment to maintaining security and strategic stability along its western border region.

questions.question: Where was the International Salinity Conference 3.0, WE-CARE 2025, inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The International Salinity Conference 3.0, WE-CARE 2025, was inaugurated at the ICAR–Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute (ICAR-CCARI) in Old Goa. The event gathers 150 delegates from India and several SAARC and AARDO member nations, including Japan, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Dubai, Oman, Kenya, Ghana, Zambia, Gambia, Eswatini, and Lebanon. Hosting the conference in Goa highlights its role as an important hub for international collaboration in addressing global salinity issues, promoting research exchange, and fostering sustainable agricultural practices across diverse regions.

questions.question: Who from Punjab recently earned the International Master (IM) title in chess after performing at the 3rd Annemasse International Masters Tournament in France?
questions.explanation: Namitbir Singh Walia from Jalandhar, Punjab, achieved the prestigious International Master (IM) title after securing fourth place at the 3rd Annemasse International Masters Tournament in France. His consistent performance, including winning the Senior State FIDE Rating Open Chess Championship earlier this year, highlights his dedication and growing prominence in Indian chess. With this achievement, Namitbir becomes Punjab’s second International Master, following Dushyant Sharma, who earned the title in 2022. His success marks a significant milestone for the state’s chess community and inspires emerging players to aim for international recognition.

questions.question: Which state’s police launched the ‘Cyber Jago’ programme to promote internet safety among school students?
questions.explanation: The ‘Cyber Jago’ programme was launched by the Punjab Police’s Cyber Crime Division with the objective of educating government school students about internet safety and responsible online behavior. The initiative also emphasizes the role of teachers and parents in building awareness through open discussions on online risks and preventive measures. As a statewide effort, Cyber Jago aims to safeguard the younger generation from cyber threats, empowering them with knowledge to navigate the digital world securely while fostering a culture of responsible internet usage across Punjab.

questions.question: Which country received India's first-ever GI-tagged Indi and Puliyankudi Limes under the APEDA-facilitated air shipment?
questions.explanation: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the first-ever air shipment of GI-tagged Indi and Puliyankudi Limes to the United Kingdom. This historic consignment consisted of 350 kg of Indi Lime from Vijayapura, Karnataka, and 150 kg of Puliyankudi Lime from Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu, totaling 500 kg. The successful export signifies a major milestone in expanding the global reach of India’s unique GI-tagged horticultural products, strengthening trade ties and promoting regional produce in international markets.

questions.question: In which country did India and the United States sign a landmark 10-year Defence Framework Agreement?
questions.explanation: India and the United States signed a landmark 10-year Defence Framework Agreement in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. This agreement marks a significant step in strengthening the US–India Major Defence Partnership by outlining long-term cooperation in areas such as defence technology, joint military exercises, and information sharing. The framework aims to enhance strategic collaboration between the two nations while contributing to regional and global security. The choice of Malaysia as the signing venue underscores its importance as a neutral ground for fostering international defence partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region.

questions.question: Who became the oldest ever ICC No. 1 ODI batter at the age of 38 years and 182 days?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma, at 38 years and 182 days, created history by becoming the oldest player to top the ICC Men’s ODI batting rankings. This remarkable achievement marked his first time reaching the No. 1 position in the ODI charts. By doing so, Rohit surpassed the legendary Sachin Tendulkar, who held the previous record at 38 years and 73 days in 2011. He achieved this milestone by overtaking Shubman Gill, reaffirming his consistency, experience, and dominance in world cricket even in the later years of his career.

questions.question: Which team defeated Australia to enter the Women’s ODI World Cup 2025 final?
questions.explanation: In a historic semi-final of the 2025 Women’s ODI World Cup held at DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai, India defeated Australia by 5 wickets to secure a place in the final against South Africa. Chasing a mammoth target of 339 runs, India recorded the highest successful run chase in Women’s ODI history. Jemimah Rodrigues’ unbeaten 127 and Harmanpreet Kaur’s crucial 89 anchored the innings, while contributions from Richa Ghosh and Amanjot Kaur sealed the win. This victory marked India’s first appearance in a World Cup final since 2017 and ended Australia’s long unbeaten streak in the tournament.

questions.question: On which date is World Cities Day observed every year to promote sustainable urban development?
questions.explanation: World Cities Day is observed annually on October 31 to raise global awareness about the challenges and opportunities of urbanization while promoting sustainable and inclusive city development. Initiated by the United Nations General Assembly through Resolution 68/239, the day marks the conclusion of “Urban October,” an initiative led by UN-Habitat. The 2025 theme, “People-Centred Smart Cities,” emphasises leveraging technology and innovation to improve urban living standards, enhance sustainability, and prioritise human well-being. The 2025 global event, hosted in Bogotá, Colombia, aims to encourage cooperation and innovation for building resilient, inclusive, and prosperous cities worldwide.

questions.question: On which date is National Unity Day celebrated in India to honour Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s birth anniversary?
questions.explanation: National Unity Day, also known as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, is celebrated every year on October 31 to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the “Iron Man of India.” The day honours his crucial role in integrating over 560 princely states into a unified India after independence. In 2025, the celebration marks the 150th anniversary of Patel’s birth, with nationwide events such as the Run for Unity and cultural programs emphasizing patriotism, unity, and national integrity. This date also symbolises Patel’s enduring legacy in building a strong and united Indian nation.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the 53rd Chief Justice of India (CJI), succeeding Justice BR Gavai?
questions.explanation: Justice Surya Kant has been appointed as the 53rd Chief Justice of India, with his tenure beginning on November 24, 2025, following the retirement of Justice BR Gavai. The appointment was approved by President Droupadi Murmu based on the collegium’s recommendation. Justice Surya Kant, currently a Supreme Court judge, is known for his contributions to constitutional law, social justice, and human rights. Before his elevation, he served as Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court and as a judge at the Punjab and Haryana High Court. His leadership is expected to guide key judicial reforms and enhance justice delivery efficiency in India.

questions.question: Which Indian tennis legend announced his retirement after a 20-year professional career, ending with a final appearance at the Paris Masters 2025?
questions.explanation: Rohan Bopanna, one of India’s greatest tennis players, retired in 2025 after a distinguished two-decade-long career. Known for his powerful serves and exceptional doubles play, Bopanna achieved historic milestones, including winning two Grand Slam titles — the 2017 French Open mixed doubles and the 2024 Australian Open men’s doubles. He became the oldest player to reach World No. 1 in doubles at age 43. His famous partnership with Pakistan’s Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi, dubbed the “Indo-Pak Express,” symbolised sportsmanship and unity. Bopanna’s legacy extends beyond trophies, as he inspired future Indian tennis players through perseverance and excellence on the global stage.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Chief Product and Business Officer of Google Cloud?
questions.explanation: Karthik Narain, a seasoned technology leader and former Accenture Chief Technology Officer, has been appointed as the Chief Product and Business Officer at Google Cloud. With over 25 years of experience in cloud, AI, and enterprise transformation, Narain brings deep industry expertise to one of the world’s most competitive cloud ecosystems. In his new role, he will oversee product, engineering, and go-to-market strategies, helping Google Cloud expand its global presence and AI-driven enterprise offerings. His appointment strengthens Thomas Kurian’s leadership team and reinforces Google’s strategic push to accelerate innovation and compete effectively with AWS and Microsoft Azure in the enterprise cloud market.

questions.question: Which country launched the Shenzhou-21 mission carrying three astronauts and four lab mice to the Tiangong Space Station?
questions.explanation: China launched the Shenzhou-21 mission to its Tiangong Space Station, marking another milestone in its rapidly advancing space programme. The mission carried three astronauts — including 32-year-old Wu Fei, the nation’s youngest astronaut — and four lab mice for biological experiments in microgravity. Conducted from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre using a Long March-2F rocket, the mission aims to expand research on space-based biology, maintenance operations, and spacewalks. This achievement aligns with China’s long-term goal of landing humans on the Moon by 2030 and reinforces its position as a key global player in space exploration and scientific innovation.

questions.question: Who was elected as the 10th President of Ireland after winning about 63% of the vote in the 2025 presidential election?
questions.explanation: Catherine Connolly, an independent left-wing politician from Galway, was elected as Ireland’s 10th President with around 63% of the first-preference votes, defeating her main rival Heather Humphreys. Her victory marks a significant moment in Irish politics, being both a rebuke to the centre-right establishment and a sign of public support for progressive and inclusive values. Connolly, who has served as a Teachta Dála since 2016 and was Deputy Speaker of Parliament, campaigned on themes of social justice, neutrality in foreign policy, and equality, promising to be “a president for all” Irish citizens.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Archbishop of Canterbury, becoming the first woman to lead the Church of England?
questions.explanation: Dame Sarah Mullally has made history as the first woman appointed Archbishop of Canterbury, the highest office in the Church of England. Formerly the NHS Chief Nursing Officer for England, she transitioned to the priesthood in 2006 and became the Bishop of London in 2018. Her appointment marks a major milestone for gender equality in the Anglican Church, reflecting its ongoing journey toward inclusivity and reform. Approved by King Charles III after nomination by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, she will officially take office in January 2026. Her priorities include safeguarding reforms, rebuilding trust, and promoting compassion and inclusivity in the Church’s mission.

questions.question: Who was recognised by the World Food Prize Foundation as a 2025 Top Agri-Food Pioneer for his contributions to nutrition and sustainable food systems?
questions.explanation: Chef Sanjeev Kapoor, a celebrated Indian chef and Padma Shri awardee, was honoured by the World Food Prize Foundation as one of its 2025 Top Agri-Food Pioneers. He earned this global recognition for integrating culinary innovation with nutrition advocacy, sustainable sourcing, and agricultural transformation. Kapoor’s initiatives, such as Nutri Pathshala, have connected schools, farmers, and nutrition programmes, helping deliver over 2.5 million nutrient-rich meals to children. His promotion of bio-fortified crops like iron-rich pearl millet and zinc-rich wheat has advanced both food security and community health. This recognition highlights how chefs can drive real change in agriculture and nutrition policy.

questions.question: Which company launched ‘VEER’, India’s first electric vehicle designed specifically for defence operations?
questions.explanation: Pravaig, a Bengaluru-based company, has launched VEER, India’s first indigenous electric vehicle developed for defence applications. Built under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, the Pravaig VEER EV offers stealth capabilities, high terrain mobility, and quick field-repair readiness, making it ideal for modern military missions. The vehicle recently received the iDEX (Innovation for Defence Excellence) award, recognizing its contribution to indigenous defence innovation. By combining sustainability, tactical efficiency, and technological advancement, the VEER strengthens India’s self-reliance in defence manufacturing and positions the nation as a potential leader in electric military vehicle technology on the global stage.

questions.question: What is the name of the new programme launched by UIDAI to enhance Aadhaar security and promote digital innovation?
questions.explanation: SITAA, which stands for Scheme for Innovation and Technology Association with Aadhaar, is a new initiative launched by the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI). The programme aims to strengthen Aadhaar’s technological foundation by encouraging innovation and research in areas like artificial intelligence, biometric authentication, and data security. In collaboration with MeitY Startup Hub and NASSCOM, SITAA will nurture startups and researchers to develop homegrown solutions for a secure and inclusive digital identity ecosystem. It also aligns with national missions such as Digital Public Infrastructure and Atmanirbhar Bharat, fostering self-reliance and trust in India’s digital framework.

questions.question: What was the year-on-year growth rate of India's GST revenue in October 2025, which marked the slowest pace in over four years?
questions.explanation: India’s Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue grew by 4.6% year-on-year in October 2025, reaching ₹1.96 lakh crore — the highest in five months but marking the slowest growth in over four years. Despite the moderation, revenues remained above ₹1.8 lakh crore for the tenth straight month, reflecting consistent economic activity and strong tax compliance. The slowdown was partly due to the government’s restructuring of GST slabs, which simplified the tax system by reducing higher-rate categories. This reform is expected to stimulate consumption and investment over time, helping sustain fiscal stability and support India’s long-term economic growth trajectory.

questions.question: Which team won the ICC Women’s ODI World Cup 2025 by defeating South Africa by 52 runs in the final at Navi Mumbai?
questions.explanation: India won their maiden ICC Women’s ODI World Cup title in 2025 by defeating South Africa by 52 runs in the final held at the DY Patil Sports Academy, Navi Mumbai. India posted a strong total of 298/7, powered by Shafali Verma’s 87 and Deepti Sharma’s all-round brilliance, including a fifty and five wickets. South Africa’s Laura Wolvaardt scored a valiant 101, but India’s bowlers sealed the victory. This triumph marked India’s first-ever Women’s ODI World Cup title, making it a historic achievement for Indian cricket and a defining moment for women’s sports in the country.

questions.question: In which Indian state was the Integrated Sohra Tourism Circuit launched under the PM-DevINE scheme by Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia?
questions.explanation: The Integrated Sohra Tourism Circuit was launched in Meghalaya under the PM-DevINE scheme, with Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia laying its foundation. Valued at ₹233 crore, this project aims to develop Sohra (Cherrapunji) into a model destination for sustainable tourism. It forms part of the larger ₹650 crore initiative focusing on tourism, connectivity, and regional development in the Northeast. Additionally, key infrastructure projects such as the Shillong–Silchar Expressway, Umroi Airport expansion, and New Shillong City initiative are being implemented to boost Meghalaya’s economic growth and tourism potential in the region.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the 40th Chief of Materiel of the Indian Navy on 01 Nov 2025, succeeding Vice Admiral Kiran Deshmukh?
questions.explanation: Vice Admiral B Sivakumar, AVSM, VSM, assumed the role of the 40th Chief of Materiel on the specified date, taking over from Vice Admiral Kiran Deshmukh. His extensive background, including being an NDA alumnus, a postgraduate from IIT Chennai, and having over 38 years of service, is detailed. His prior experience as the Director General of Naval Projects in Visakhapatnam and his expertise in naval technology and warship production further confirm his identity as the officer who took on this key leadership position within the Indian Navy.

questions.question: On which date is World Jellyfish Day celebrated annually to raise awareness about the ecological importance and beauty of jellyfish?
questions.explanation: World Jellyfish Day is celebrated every year on November 3 to honour one of Earth’s oldest and most fascinating marine organisms. Jellyfish have existed for over 500 million years and play a vital role in maintaining marine ecosystem balance. Despite their reputation for stings, they contribute to oceanic food chains, provide shelter for juvenile fish, and act as indicators of ocean health and climate change. The day encourages appreciation through educational activities, aquarium visits, and conservation awareness, emphasizing the need to protect marine biodiversity and promote sustainable ocean practices worldwide.

questions.question: Which advanced communication satellite is ISRO launching to enhance the Indian Navy’s maritime domain awareness and secure communication network?
questions.explanation: GSAT-7R, also known as CMS-03, is India’s heaviest and most advanced indigenous naval communication satellite, weighing approximately 4,400 kg. Launched by ISRO from Sriharikota, it is designed to significantly enhance the Indian Navy’s space-based communication capabilities and maritime domain awareness across the Indian Ocean Region. The satellite is equipped with multi-band transponders that provide secure, high-bandwidth voice, data, and video connectivity between naval command centres and assets at sea. GSAT-7R strengthens India’s strategic communication infrastructure, ensuring reliable and real-time naval operations in both peacetime and defence scenarios.

questions.question: Which country’s Citizenship and Immigration Services agency has ended cheque and money order payments, making electronic debit via Form G-1650 mandatory for immigration filings?
questions.explanation: The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has introduced a significant policy change by discontinuing cheque and money order payments for immigration-related filings. Applicants must now use electronic debit through Form G-1650 for all transactions. This shift aims to enhance security, minimise the risk of fraud, and ensure faster, more efficient processing. According to USCIS spokesperson Matthew J. Tragesser, the updated system replaces outdated manual methods, aligning with modern digital standards to improve accuracy, reliability, and overall transparency in immigration service operations within the United States.

questions.question: In which city is the Emerging Science & Technology Innovation Conclave (ESTIC-2025) being held, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
questions.explanation: The Emerging Science & Technology Innovation Conclave 2025 (ESTIC-2025) is being hosted in New Delhi from November 3 to 5, bringing together over 3,000 participants, including leading scientists, innovators, and policymakers. The event, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, focuses on the theme “Viksit Bharat 2047 – Pioneering Sustainable Innovation, Technological Advancement and Empowerment.” During the conclave, the Prime Minister also launched the ₹1 Lakh Crore Research, Development, and Innovation (RDI) Scheme to accelerate private-led R&D initiatives and support deep-tech startups, strengthening India’s path toward technological self-reliance and sustainable innovation.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) on November 1, 2025?
questions.explanation: Shri Vishvajit Sahay, a 1990 batch officer of the Indian Defence Accounts Service (IDAS), assumed charge as the Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA) on November 1, 2025. With over 30 years of experience in defence finance, he has held several senior positions, including Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser in the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Finance Manager in the Ministry of Defence (MoD). An alumnus of St. Stephen’s College, Sahay has also represented India at international forums, contributing significantly to the modernization and transparency of defence financial management.

questions.question: Which DNA repair protein discovered by University of Iowa researchers shows potential for new cancer therapies by targeting DNA repair deficiencies such as BRCA1/2 mutations?
questions.explanation: RAD52 is a DNA repair protein identified by University of Iowa researchers as crucial for cancer cell survival, particularly in cells with BRCA1/2 mutations that impair DNA repair mechanisms. By inhibiting RAD52, researchers can selectively kill cancer cells without heavily affecting normal cells. This approach offers a promising alternative to PARP inhibitors, potentially overcoming drug resistance and reducing side effects associated with traditional treatments like chemotherapy and radiation, thereby opening new therapeutic avenues for cancers with DNA repair deficiencies.

questions.question: Who was re-elected as the President of Tanzania with 97.66% of the votes amid reports of violent unrest and protests?
questions.explanation: Samia Suluhu Hassan was re-elected as the President of Tanzania with an overwhelming 97.66% of the votes and a voter turnout of 87%. Her victory came during a period of significant unrest marked by violent protests and allegations of election irregularities. Opposition groups reported hundreds of deaths, although the United Nations confirmed at least 10 casualties. Despite the controversy surrounding the process, Hassan’s re-election secured her another five-year term, reinforcing her position as one of Africa’s prominent female leaders and a key figure in Tanzania’s political landscape.

questions.question: In which city was the International Conference on “Libraries Empowering Communities – Global Perspectives” held to mark 80 years of Kerala’s library movement?
questions.explanation: The International Conference on “Libraries Empowering Communities – Global Perspectives” was organised at Kanakakkunnu Palace in Thiruvananthapuram on November 2–3, 2025, commemorating 80 years of Kerala’s library movement initiated by the P. N. Panicker Foundation. The event gathered librarians, policymakers, and global experts to discuss the evolving role of libraries in promoting literacy and access to knowledge. Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan highlighted libraries as “temples of learning,” emphasizing their importance in fostering digital literacy, critical thinking, and combating misinformation in the modern age of technology and information overload.

questions.question: Which country launched the nuclear submarine “Khabarovsk” designed to carry the Poseidon underwater drone?
questions.explanation: Russia launched the nuclear-powered submarine “Khabarovsk” on November 1 at the Sevmash shipyard in Severodvinsk. The submarine is designed to carry the Poseidon Unmanned Underwater Vehicle (UUV)—a nuclear-powered torpedo capable of traveling thousands of kilometers and reportedly carrying a warhead with a yield of about 2 megatons. Poseidon’s potential to generate large-scale radioactive tsunamis and its stealthy underwater deployment make it a key component of Russia’s strategic deterrence. The launch significantly extends Russia’s naval strike and deterrence capabilities while intensifying global security and stability concerns in maritime domains.

questions.question: Who reclaimed the ATP World No. 1 ranking after winning the 2025 Paris Masters final against Felix Auger-Aliassime?
questions.explanation: Jannik Sinner, the Italian tennis sensation, reclaimed the ATP World No. 1 ranking by defeating Felix Auger-Aliassime in straight sets—6-4, 7-6 (4)—in the 2025 Paris Masters final. This victory marked Sinner’s first Paris Masters title and extended his impressive indoor winning streak to 26 matches. With this win, he surpassed Carlos Alcaraz in the ATP rankings, consolidating his dominance during the 2025 season. Sinner’s consistency, particularly in indoor tournaments like Vienna and Paris, showcased his exceptional form, tactical maturity, and mental resilience, cementing his position among the elite players shaping the new era of men’s tennis.

questions.question: Which country is set to receive its first Taliban-appointed diplomat since the group’s takeover of Kabul in 2021, signaling cautious diplomatic engagement?
questions.explanation: India is preparing to receive the first Taliban-appointed diplomat since the Taliban’s return to power in Afghanistan in August 2021. This development marks a cautious reopening of diplomatic engagement between the two sides without formal recognition of the Taliban regime. The move follows Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi’s visit to New Delhi in October 2025 and aligns with India’s broader strategy of maintaining humanitarian assistance and regional stability. By permitting a limited diplomatic presence, India balances its security concerns, humanitarian commitments, and geopolitical interests while preserving communication channels with Kabul amid evolving regional dynamics.

questions.question: Which country has become the first in the world to achieve thorium-to-uranium fuel conversion in a Thorium Molten Salt Reactor (TMSR)?
questions.explanation: China has achieved a historic milestone by successfully performing thorium-to-uranium fuel conversion within its Thorium Molten Salt Reactor (TMSR), making it the first country in the world to do so. This breakthrough, announced on November 3, 2025, represents a major advancement in fourth-generation nuclear technology, offering safer, cleaner, and more efficient energy generation. The reactor converts thorium-232 into fissile uranium-233, enabling a sustainable thorium fuel cycle. With this success, China has demonstrated the viability of molten salt reactors and taken a leading position in the race for advanced nuclear innovation, complementing India’s ongoing thorium-based research initiatives.

questions.question: Which lake in Bihar has recently been declared a Ramsar site, gaining recognition as India’s newest wetland of international importance?
questions.explanation: Gogabeel Lake, located in the Katihar district of Bihar, has been designated as India’s newest Ramsar site, earning international recognition for its ecological and cultural significance. This ox-bow lake, formed by the meandering of rivers in the trans-Gangetic plains, is flanked by the Mahananda River in the northeast and the Ganga in the south. It supports diverse flora and fauna, serving as a vital wintering ground for migratory birds and home to species like the Smooth-Coated Otter and Helicopter Catfish. Additionally, its community involvement and cultural importance highlight the Ramsar Convention’s principle of “wise use” of wetlands.

questions.question: Which organization launched the “Reimagining Agriculture: A Roadmap for Frontier Technology Led Transformation” initiative to modernise Indian farming using AI and advanced technologies?

options.B: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog launched the “Reimagining Agriculture: A Roadmap for Frontier Technology Led Transformation” to accelerate India’s agricultural modernization through the integration of AI, digital twins, and precision farming. The initiative emphasises climate-resilient crops, sustainability, and increased farmer income by leveraging frontier technologies. It introduces a farmer segmentation model with three archetypes—Aspiring, Transitioning, and Advanced—to enable targeted interventions. By focusing on innovation and data-driven agricultural practices, the roadmap aims to enhance productivity, resource efficiency, and long-term resilience against climate challenges, marking a major policy push toward tech-enabled, inclusive agricultural growth in India.

questions.question: The newly launched ‘SBI-STAR’ Awards by the State Bank of India are primarily aimed at recognizing which aspect of its workforce?
questions.explanation: The State Bank of India (SBI) has introduced the ‘SBI-STAR’ Awards—Staff Talent Acknowledgement & Recognition—to honour employee talents beyond professional achievements. The initiative celebrates excellence in areas such as arts, sports, literature, social work, and environmental initiatives, fostering a culture of holistic employee engagement. With over 2.45 lakh employees, SBI aims to highlight the creative, athletic, and humanitarian contributions of its staff, reinforcing its human-centric leadership approach. This annual award program promotes inclusivity, motivation, and well-being within the organization, setting a new benchmark for employee recognition in India’s public sector banking ecosystem.

questions.question: Which global technology company has partnered with AICTE to establish an Artificial Intelligence lab in India to upskill students and faculty?
questions.explanation: IBM has partnered with the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) to establish a state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) lab at AICTE headquarters. The initiative focuses on enhancing AI and data science skills among students and faculty through hands-on training, hackathons, and certified programs. It also includes a Master-Trainer Program to enable large-scale skill dissemination across India’s technical institutions. The collaboration aligns with India’s National Education Policy 2020 and National AI Strategy, as well as IBM’s global mission to promote inclusive technology education and build a future-ready digital workforce for the evolving tech ecosystem.

questions.question: Which country has become the first in the world to implement a generational smoking ban prohibiting tobacco use for anyone born after January 1, 2007?
questions.explanation: The Maldives has made history by enacting the world’s first generational smoking ban, effective from November 1, 2025. This law prohibits anyone born on or after January 1, 2007, from purchasing or using tobacco in any form. It applies to both citizens and tourists, covering cigarettes, vaping devices, and e-cigarettes. Retailers who violate the age verification mandate face heavy fines. By enforcing this strict regulation, the Maldives aims to create a completely smoke-free generation, prioritizing youth health and setting a global precedent after New Zealand’s repeal and the UK’s pending legislation on similar tobacco restrictions.

questions.question: Who was honoured with IIT Kanpur’s Distinguished Alumnus Award, the institute’s highest alumni honour, during its 66th Foundation Day celebrations?
questions.explanation: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was conferred IIT Kanpur’s Distinguished Alumnus Award, the premier recognition given by the institute to its former students for exceptional professional achievements. A 1985 B.Tech graduate in Civil Engineering from IIT Kanpur, Gyanesh Kumar has had an illustrious career in public service and governance. Instituted in 1989, this award celebrates alumni who have made significant contributions in their respective fields. The honour was presented during IIT Kanpur’s 66th Foundation Day celebrations, marking both academic excellence and leadership in public administration.

questions.question: Which tech company has signed a $38 billion deal with OpenAI to expand AI capabilities using its cloud infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Amazon, through its cloud division Amazon Web Services (AWS), has entered a $38 billion partnership with OpenAI to enhance AI infrastructure and scalability. Announced on November 3, 2025, the agreement provides OpenAI access to AWS’s extensive cloud computing resources, including millions of CPUs and hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA GPUs. This collaboration marks one of the largest AI infrastructure deployments in history and signifies a major strategic shift for OpenAI, which previously relied exclusively on Microsoft Azure. The deal strengthens Amazon’s position as a key competitor in the global AI and cloud computing market.

questions.question: Which bank executed its first gold trade as a Special Category Client (SCC) on the India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX)?
questions.explanation: The State Bank of India (SBI) achieved a major milestone by executing its first gold trade on the India International Bullion Exchange (IIBX) as a Special Category Client (SCC). This move enhances transparency and efficiency in India’s bullion market while making gold trading more accessible and cost-effective for MSME jewellers and bullion dealers. By participating in IIBX, SBI contributes to the development of GIFT City as a global financial and bullion trading hub. The initiative also aligns with the government’s vision of modernising India’s bullion ecosystem through regulated and technology-driven market practices.

questions.question: Which Indian state has launched the Artificial Intelligence Innovation Hub in Hyderabad to drive AI research and global collaboration by 2035?
questions.explanation: Telangana has launched the Telangana Artificial Intelligence Innovation Hub (TAIH) in Hyderabad to establish itself as a global leader in emerging technologies by 2035. Spearheaded by Minister D. Sridhar Babu, the hub aims to unite academia, industry and startups to advance AI-based innovation and research. Collaborators include institutions such as IIT Hyderabad, BITS Pilani, ISB, and global tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Amazon. The initiative reflects Telangana’s strategic transition from an IT-services powerhouse to a frontier technology leader and aligns with India’s national focus on AI-driven innovation and digital growth.

questions.question: Which country was severely affected by Typhoon Kalmaegi, also known locally as Tino, causing 26 deaths and widespread destruction in November 2025?
questions.explanation: Typhoon Kalmaegi, locally called Tino, struck the Philippines in early November 2025 with powerful winds reaching 205 km/h, devastating the Visayas region. The typhoon triggered floods, landslides, and 3-meter storm surges, heavily damaging provinces such as Cebu, Leyte, Samar, and Negros Occidental. At least 26 people lost their lives, primarily in Cebu, and hundreds of thousands were displaced as homes, infrastructure, and power systems were destroyed. The event underscored the Philippines’ continued vulnerability to intense tropical cyclones fueled by climate change and highlighted the urgent need for resilient infrastructure and disaster preparedness across coastal communities.

questions.question: Who was elected as the Mayor of New York City, becoming the city’s first Muslim and first person of South Asian descent to hold the office?
questions.explanation: Zohran Mamdani was elected as the Mayor of New York City on 4 November 2025, marking a historic moment in American urban politics. He became the city’s first Muslim mayor, the first person of South Asian descent, and the youngest individual in over a century to hold the post. Born in Uganda to Indian-origin parents, Mamdani’s progressive platform emphasised social equity through measures like free bus services, universal childcare, rent freezes, and higher minimum wages. His election represents a generational shift, greater diversity in city leadership, and the growing influence of progressive politics in major U.S. cities.

questions.question: Who has assumed charge as the Director General of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) effective 1 November 2025?
questions.explanation: Shri Sanjay Garg, a 1994-batch IAS officer from the Kerala cadre, has taken charge as the Director General of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) from 1 November 2025. With over three decades of administrative experience, he has contributed significantly to policy formulation, planning, and implementation across various national sectors. Prior to this role, he served as Additional Secretary at the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and as Secretary at ICAR, where he led digital transformation initiatives, including the expansion of the Kisan Sarathi portal aimed at empowering farmers through real-time advisory services.

questions.question: Which Indian city was declared a UNESCO Creative City in the field of Gastronomy in 2025?
questions.explanation: Lucknow has been declared a UNESCO Creative City under the Gastronomy category in 2025, joining the UNESCO Creative Cities Network (UCCN). Established in 2004, the UCCN promotes creativity as a core pillar of sustainable urban development. This recognition highlights Lucknow’s centuries-old culinary heritage rooted in Awadhi cuisine, known for its kebabs, biryanis, and refined cooking traditions. With this inclusion, Lucknow joins other Indian cities like Jaipur (Crafts and Folk Art), Varanasi and Chennai (Music), Hyderabad (Gastronomy), Mumbai (Film), and Srinagar (Crafts and Folk Art), further showcasing India’s cultural and creative diversity on a global platform.

questions.question: To which country did India export its first consignment of fortified rice from Chhattisgarh in 2025?
questions.explanation: India exported 12 metric tonnes of fortified rice kernels (FRK) from Chhattisgarh to Costa Rica, marking a milestone in nutrition-oriented trade and global food diplomacy. Facilitated by APEDA, this initiative highlights India’s growing role in promoting food fortification technology and combating micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. Fortified rice, enriched with iron, folic acid, and vitamin B12, is already used domestically under the Poshan Abhiyan. This export strengthens Chhattisgarh’s reputation as the “Rice Bowl of India,” while aligning with India’s goal to merge agricultural innovation with global health and trade initiatives, enhancing both economic and diplomatic engagement.

questions.question: Which Indian cooperative organisation secured the top rank globally in the 2025 International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) World Cooperative Monitor rankings?
questions.explanation: Amul, managed by the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), secured the No. 1 global ranking in the 2025 ICA World Cooperative Monitor, followed by IFFCO at second place. This milestone highlights India’s leadership in cooperative governance and its success in promoting inclusive rural growth. Amul’s three-tier cooperative model connects millions of dairy farmers to national and international markets, ensuring fair income and empowerment for producers. Its achievements in innovation, value addition, and sustainability have transformed India’s dairy sector into a global model of cooperative excellence. The recognition also strengthens India’s vision of “Sahkar Se Samriddhi.”

questions.question: On which date is World Tsunami Awareness Day 2025 observed globally to promote tsunami preparedness and early-warning systems?
questions.explanation: World Tsunami Awareness Day is observed every year on November 5, as designated by the United Nations General Assembly in 2015. The date was inspired by the Japanese legend of Inamura-no-hi (“The Burning of the Rice Sheaves”), where a farmer saved villagers by warning them of an incoming tsunami. The 2025 theme, “Be Tsunami Ready: Invest in Tsunami Preparedness,” stresses the importance of early-warning systems, community training, and resilient infrastructure. With more than 700 million people living in tsunami-prone areas worldwide, the observance reinforces the urgent need for awareness, preparedness, and global cooperation to reduce disaster risks.

questions.question: With which country did India sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at the 17th Joint Working Group meeting to strengthen defence cooperation?
questions.explanation: India signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Israel during the 17th Joint Working Group (JWG) on Defence Cooperation held in Tel Aviv to deepen strategic collaboration. The agreement focuses on co-development, co-production, advanced technology exchange, and counter-terrorism cooperation. It reinforces the two nations’ long-standing defence partnership, which has evolved through decades of shared security priorities and technological exchange. The MoU aligns with India’s Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliance) vision in defence manufacturing and supports the mutual goal of building a more secure and innovation-driven defence ecosystem between India and Israel.

questions.question: When will the final voter list for the second phase of the Special Voter List Revision be published?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India has initiated the second phase of the Special Voter List Revision, encompassing nine states and three Union Territories, representing an electorate of around 51 crore voters. This nationwide electoral update aims to ensure accuracy and inclusivity in voter registration. The process will conclude with the publication of the final voter list on February 7, 2026. The first phase of the exercise was completed in Bihar, covering 7.42 crore voters. The ongoing phase includes states like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, West Bengal, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh, while Assam remains excluded due to Supreme Court-led citizenship verification.

questions.question: Where was the Second World Summit for Social Development held in November 2025?
questions.explanation: The Second World Summit for Social Development took place in Doha, Qatar, from November 4–6, 2025. The event culminated in the adoption of the Doha Political Declaration, which reaffirmed global commitments to eradicate poverty, ensure decent work, and promote inclusive growth. The summit served as a key international platform to review progress on social development goals outlined in the original Copenhagen Declaration of 1995. India, represented by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, actively participated in discussions highlighting challenges faced by the Global South, especially those linked to development disparities and the transformative role of emerging technologies.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the brand ambassador for Paradeep Phosphates Ltd. to promote sustainable farming in India?
questions.explanation: Cricket legend Rahul Dravid has been appointed as the brand ambassador for Paradeep Phosphates Ltd. (PPL) to promote sustainable farming and balanced fertiliser use across India. Announced on 5 November 2025, this collaboration leverages Dravid’s reputation for integrity and discipline to connect with farmers and drive awareness about soil health and efficient nutrient management. Through campaigns like “Kheti Ka Game Changer” and “NPK and Organic Fertilisers Ki Winning Team,” the initiative aims to simplify agronomy using cricket-inspired themes, supporting national programmes such as the NMSA and PM-PRANAM for sustainable agriculture.

questions.question: Which Indian company has partnered with US-based General Atomics Aeronautical Systems (GA-ASI) to manufacture Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) for the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) has entered into a strategic partnership with US-based General Atomics Aeronautical Systems (GA-ASI) to jointly produce Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) for the Indian Army. Under this collaboration, L&T will act as the prime bidder for the 87 MALE RPAS programme, while GA-ASI will serve as the technology partner. This agreement strengthens India’s Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative by boosting indigenous defence manufacturing capabilities and promoting greater Indo-US cooperation in the aerospace and defence sectors.

questions.question: What is the name of Google’s project to build AI data centres in space using solar-powered satellites?
questions.explanation: Google’s Project Suncatcher is an ambitious initiative aimed at building AI data centres in orbit, powered by solar energy. The project plans to deploy satellites equipped with TPUs, solar panels, and high-speed optical communication systems to form a distributed computing network around Earth.
