The discussions covered areas such as trade, energy, mining, agriculture, digital infrastructure, and capacity building. Both countries also emphasised cooperation in counter-terrorism and human resource development through programs like ITEC and ICCR scholarships. Sudan condemned the terrorist attack in Pahalgam, reflecting support for security cooperation with India. The meeting further reinforced diplomatic engagement between the two nations, and it was decided that the next round of consultations would be hosted in New Delhi.

questions.question: Which country participated with India in the inaugural Joint Commission meeting to expand bilateral defence cooperation in May 2026?
questions.explanation: India and Algeria held their inaugural Joint Commission meeting in New Delhi on May 05, 2026, to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation. The meeting was co-chaired by senior defence officials from both countries and focused on expanding collaboration in military training, joint exercises, defence industries, and medical cooperation. Both sides signed the Rules of Procedure to establish a structured framework for implementing defence initiatives. The engagement reflects growing strategic ties between India and Algeria following the signing of a Defence Memorandum of Understanding in 2024. Algeria, the largest country in Africa by land area, continues to play an important role in India’s outreach to African nations.

questions.question: Which country partnered with India to set a bilateral trade target of $25 billion by 2030?
questions.explanation: India and Vietnam held bilateral discussions in New Delhi and agreed to achieve a bilateral trade target of $25 billion by 2030 under their enhanced comprehensive strategic partnership. The talks focused on expanding trade, improving agricultural market access, and strengthening defence cooperation. Both countries granted access for products such as Indian grapes and Vietnamese durians while also working toward faster clearances for other agricultural goods. They additionally agreed to establish a 2+2 Dialogue mechanism involving foreign and defence ministries. The discussions also emphasised the early review and implementation of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) to further strengthen economic integration and regional cooperation.

questions.question: Which entity has approved the world's first major law regulating AI, known as the AI Act?
questions.explanation: The European Union (EU) has approved the AI Act, marking a historic step in regulating artificial intelligence. This groundbreaking legislation imposes strict rules on AI applications, particularly high-risk systems, with significant penalties for non-compliance, demonstrating the EU's commitment to robust AI regulation.

questions.question: Which city will host the second edition of WAVES Doc Bazaar in June 2026?
questions.explanation: The second edition of WAVES Doc Bazaar will be hosted in Mumbai from June 16 to June 18, 2026, at the NFDC Complex alongside the 19th Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF). The event is designed to support documentary, animation, and short filmmakers by providing them with mentorship, networking opportunities, and international market exposure. Key components of the event include the Viewing Room for showcasing completed films and the Work-In-Progress Lab for filmmakers seeking expert guidance during post-production stages. Organised in connection with MIFF, the initiative strengthens India’s creative and cinematic ecosystem while promoting independent and high-quality filmmaking.

questions.question: Which two regions signed reform-linked agreements with the Ministry of Jal Shakti for implementing Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0?
questions.explanation: Mizoram and Ladakh signed reform-linked agreements with the Ministry of Jal Shakti on May 06, 2026, for the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The mission aims to provide sustainable and community-led rural drinking water systems under the vision of “Har Ghar Jal” by 2028. Mizoram achieved near-complete progress in water supply schemes and established multiple testing laboratories, while Ladakh recorded over 98% Functional Household Tap Connection coverage in rural areas. The agreements also emphasise the role of Village Water and Sanitation Committees, community participation, and convergence with schemes like MGNREGA to ensure long-term sustainability of rural water infrastructure.

questions.question: Which city will host the inaugural International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Summit in June 2026?
questions.explanation: The inaugural International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Summit will be hosted in New Delhi on 1st and 2nd June 2026 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The summit aims to bring together global wildlife conservation delegates to strengthen cooperation for the protection of big cat species. Guided by the theme “Save Big Cats, Save Humanity, Save Ecosystem,” the event seeks to adopt the historic Delhi Declaration focused on transboundary big cat conservation. The summit is inspired by India’s successful conservation initiatives, such as Project Tiger, and highlights India’s growing leadership role in global wildlife and biodiversity protection efforts.

questions.question: In which state will the Coal-to-Ammonium-Nitrate facility developed by BCGCL be situated?
questions.explanation: L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Onshore secured a major contract from Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd (BCGCL) to establish a Coal-to-Ammonium-Nitrate facility in Odisha. The project aims to convert high-ash domestic coal into ammonium nitrate with a planned production capacity of 2,000 tonnes per day. This initiative supports India’s broader goal of achieving 100 million tonnes of coal gasification capacity by 2030 under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The project is expected to reduce import dependence and promote the production of value-added products such as ammonia, methanol, and synthetic natural gas while strengthening India’s industrial and energy sectors.

questions.question: What was India’s rank in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF)?
questions.explanation: India was ranked 157th out of 180 countries in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF). The country received a global score of 31.96 in the annual assessment. The index evaluates press freedom conditions across nations using factors such as political context, legal framework, economic conditions, sociocultural environment, and journalist safety. Published annually since 2002, the index highlights the operational environment for media organisations and journalists worldwide. Norway secured the top position in the 2026 rankings, while Eritrea ranked last. RSF, headquartered in Paris, France, is an international non-profit organisation dedicated to protecting freedom of information and journalists’ rights globally.

questions.question: Which airport in India has achieved the prestigious Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) accolade?
questions.explanation: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport has become the first airport in India to achieve the Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWL) accolade, as recognized by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII-ITC) Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development. This acknowledgement underscores the airport's commitment to environmentally responsible practices and sets a benchmark for other airports to emulate.

questions.question: In which river are more than 2000 Gangetic dolphins found in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Chambal River in Uttar Pradesh harbours over 2000 Gangetic dolphins, as reported by the Wildlife Institute of India. This highlights the importance of the Chambal River in the conservation efforts aimed at protecting these endangered dolphins.

questions.question: Which city's High Court cancelled all OBC certificates in West Bengal issued after 2010?
questions.explanation: The Calcutta High Court invalidated all OBC certificates in West Bengal issued after 2010, addressing a plea that contested the state's certificate issuance process. This ruling, delivered by Justices Tapabrata Chakraborty and Rajasekhar Mantha, clarified that those already employed under such certificates would not be affected by this decision.

questions.question: In the 2024 WEF Travel & Tourism Development Index, what position did India achieve?
questions.explanation: India rose to the 39th position in the 2024 WEF Travel & Tourism Development Index, a significant improvement from its 54th position in 2021. This climb reflects India's resilience and competitiveness in various aspects of its travel and tourism industry, including price competitiveness, robust resources, and sustainability.

questions.question: In which year is the India-AI Impact Summit scheduled to be held?
questions.explanation: The India-AI Impact Summit is scheduled to take place in 2026, marking the first time a global AI summit will be hosted by a nation from the Global South. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) unveiled the official logo and initiatives for the event. The summit will focus on democratizing access to AI while ensuring safe and trusted ecosystems guided by the principles of People, Planet, and Progress. Flagship programs such as UDAAN Pitch Fest, YuvaAI, AI by HER, and the Global Innovation Challenge will encourage innovation, entrepreneurship, and inclusive participation in shaping AI’s future.

questions.question: Which country’s Rating and Investment Information, Inc. (R&I) agency upgraded India’s sovereign credit rating to BBB+?
questions.explanation: India’s sovereign credit rating was upgraded to BBB+ by Rating and Investment Information, Inc. (R&I), a well-known credit rating agency based in Japan. The upgrade reflects growing confidence in India’s strong domestic demand, prudent fiscal management, and external stability. This marks the third upgrade India has received in 2025, following earlier positive revisions by Morningstar DBRS and S&P Global Ratings. R&I also acknowledged India’s ongoing structural reforms, such as the two-tier GST system and infrastructure expansion. The move strengthens India’s global investment appeal while reinforcing Japan’s role in recognizing India’s growing economic resilience and potential on the world stage.

questions.question: Who has been proposed as the next First Deputy Managing Director of the IMF by Kristalina Georgieva?
questions.explanation: Daniel Katz, a senior U.S. Treasury official and Chief of Staff to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, has been nominated by IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva as the next First Deputy Managing Director, the second-highest position at the IMF. If approved by the IMF Executive Board, his appointment will take effect on October 6, 2025. Katz brings over a decade of experience in domestic and international economic policy, including work on U.S.-China trade, financial stability, and coordination with multilateral institutions like the IMF and World Bank. His nomination follows Gita Gopinath’s departure and reflects strategic leadership continuity in global finance.

questions.question: In which country did Typhoon Mitag make landfall?
questions.explanation: Typhoon Mitag, the 17th typhoon of the year, made landfall in Guangdong Province, China, particularly affecting Shanwei City with strong winds of up to 25 m/s near its center. Authorities expect the typhoon to weaken gradually as it moves northwest at 10–15 km/h. In response to the threat, China’s State Flood Control initiated a Level-IV emergency to ensure preparedness and reduce potential damage. The event underlines the vulnerability of coastal provinces in China to seasonal typhoons and highlights the importance of early warning systems and effective disaster management to protect lives and infrastructure from severe weather events.

questions.question: Which company signed an MoU with Oil India Limited for the exploration of critical minerals?
questions.explanation: Oil India Limited and Hindustan Copper Limited entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to work together on the exploration of critical minerals. This collaboration particularly focuses on copper and its associated minerals, which are crucial for industrial growth and energy transition. The agreement also aligns with the objectives of the National Critical Mineral Mission, which is aimed at strengthening India’s mineral security. By engaging in this strategic partnership, Hindustan Copper and Oil India seek to ensure access to essential mineral resources, thereby supporting economic growth and technological advancement in the country.

questions.question: In which state was the ‘Anbu Karangal’ scheme for orphaned children launched by Chief Minister?
questions.explanation: The ‘Anbu Karangal’ (Hands of Love) scheme was launched in Tamil Nadu by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on September 16, 2025. This welfare initiative provides ₹2,000 monthly financial support to orphaned children until they complete school education or reach the age of 18. In its first phase, over 6,000 children across Tamil Nadu will directly benefit. The scheme ensures uninterrupted education, protection under the Juvenile Justice Act, and access to digital resources such as laptops for college-bound orphans. Additionally, a mobile app developed with the Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency enables transparency, real-time monitoring, and grievance redressal, ensuring effective implementation statewide.

questions.question: Where will the 10th Ayurveda Day be celebrated on 23rd September?
questions.explanation: The 10th Ayurveda Day will be celebrated on 23rd September at the All India Institute of Ayurveda in Goa. This year’s theme is "Ayurveda for People and Planet," which emphasises the significance of Ayurveda not only for individual health but also for the overall well-being of the planet. By choosing Goa as the host location, the government highlights its efforts to promote Ayurveda at a global scale. The event also underlines the growing recognition and acceptance of Ayurveda as a holistic system of health and healing worldwide.

questions.question: On which date will International Red Panda Day 2025 be celebrated?
questions.explanation: International Red Panda Day 2025 will be observed on September 20, which falls on the third Saturday of September. This global observance was launched in 2010 by the Red Panda Network to highlight the urgent need for conservation of the endangered red panda, often referred to as the “Firefox.” With fewer than 10,000 individuals left in the wild, the red panda faces threats such as habitat loss, poaching, and low reproduction rates. Celebrating the day on September 20 draws international attention, generates support for conservation projects, and strengthens community-led initiatives to protect this rare and captivating Himalayan species.

questions.question: Zubeen Garg, the legendary singer of “Ya Ali” fame who passed away in 2025, was an icon of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Zubeen Garg, one of India’s most versatile and celebrated musicians, was an icon of Assam and the greater Northeast. Born in 1972, he built an extraordinary career spanning over three decades, with more than 38,000 songs recorded across 40 languages. He gained national recognition through the Bollywood hit “Ya Ali” from Gangster (2006), but his contribution to Assamese music and culture was unparalleled. Beyond singing, he was also a composer, actor, filmmaker, and philanthropist. His sudden passing in Singapore at age 52 left a deep void in Indian music. Leaders and fans across the country paid heartfelt tributes, acknowledging his role in carrying Assam’s cultural legacy to the national and global stage.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in T20 Internationals?
questions.explanation: Arshdeep Singh achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first Indian bowler to claim 100 wickets in T20 Internationals. He reached the landmark during India’s Asia Cup 2025 group-stage match against Oman, dismissing Vinayak Shukla as his 100th wicket. Remarkably, Arshdeep accomplished this feat in just 64 matches and 1,329 deliveries, making him the fastest fast bowler globally to reach the milestone and the fourth-fastest overall. Known for his powerplay effectiveness and death-over dominance, he has consistently outperformed peers like Haris Rauf. His achievement cements his position as one of India’s finest modern-day T20 specialists and a global pace-bowling force.

questions.question: What was India’s Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation recorded in July 2025?
questions.explanation: In July 2025, India’s Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation stood at -0.58%, marking the second consecutive month of deflation in wholesale prices. This decline was largely influenced by falling prices of food articles, mineral oils, crude petroleum, natural gas, and basic metals. WPI inflation reflects the overall change in prices at the wholesale level, differentiating it from the Consumer Price Index (CPI), which measures changes at the consumer level. The negative WPI figure indicates easing cost pressures for businesses, potentially impacting input costs, supply chains, and the broader inflation trajectory of the economy in the coming months.

questions.question: Who won the Quantbox Chennai Grand Masters 2025 Chess Title?
questions.explanation: The Quantbox Chennai Grand Masters 2025 witnessed a historic victory by German Grandmaster Vincent Keymer, who became the first sole champion in the event’s history. He secured the title with one round to spare after drawing his game with Jorden van Foreest. This achievement not only gave him the prestigious tournament title but also propelled him into the world’s Top 10 live chess ratings for the very first time, marking a milestone in his career. While Round 8 saw all matches end in draws, Indian players Arjun Erigaisi and Karthikeyan Murali remained strong contenders for second and third positions.

questions.question: L. Ganesan, who recently passed away at the age of 80, was serving as the Governor of which state at the time of his death?
questions.explanation: L. Ganesan, a veteran BJP leader and former Rajya Sabha member, passed away at the age of 80 while serving as the 21st Governor of Nagaland. Born in Thanjavur in 1945, he had a long political career, including his tenure as a Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh in 2016. He also held key gubernatorial responsibilities, serving as the Governor of Manipur from August 2021 to February 2023 and taking additional charge of West Bengal between July and November 2022. Since February 2023, he had been serving in Nagaland, where his sudden demise marked the end of his public service journey.

questions.question: What type of GST structure has the Centre proposed in its latest reform?
questions.explanation: The Centre has proposed a Two-Slab GST structure as part of its next-generation tax reform. This system introduces two main slabs—5% and 18%—along with a 40% levy on sin goods like tobacco and pan masala. The 5% slab will include daily-use and common goods, while the 18% slab will cover aspirational and white goods, such as refrigerators and televisions, that currently fall under the 28% category. Essential food items remain exempt, ensuring relief for households. The overhaul is aimed at simplifying the indirect tax system, resolving disputes, correcting inverted duty structures, reducing compliance burdens, and boosting overall consumption and GDP growth.

questions.question: By what percentage did India’s merchandise exports grow in July 2025?
questions.explanation: India’s merchandise exports in July 2025 registered a 7.3% growth, reaching $37.24 billion. This rise was driven by strong performances in sectors such as electronics, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, and gems & jewellery. Notably, electronic goods exports rose sharply by 34%, highlighting India’s increasing role in global high-tech supply chains, aided by Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes. While exports rose, imports also increased by 8.6% to $64.59 billion, pushing the trade deficit to an eight-month high of $27.35 billion. Despite this imbalance, the export growth indicates resilience in India’s trade sector amid volatile global market conditions.

questions.question: In which country are the Indian Naval Ships INS Rana and INS Jyoti participating in the SLINEX-25 naval exercise in August 2025?
questions.explanation: The SLINEX-25 naval exercise is being held in Sri Lanka, with the harbour phase in Colombo and the sea phase in nearby waters from 14–18 August 2025. Indian naval vessels INS Rana and INS Jyoti are joined by Sri Lanka’s SLNS Gajabahu and SLNS Vijayabahu, along with assets from the Sri Lanka Air Force. Activities include gunnery drills, seamanship exercises, VBSS operations, and cultural exchanges. This 12th edition of SLINEX reflects the strong naval partnership under India’s MAHASAGAR initiative, aimed at enhancing maritime interoperability, strengthening trust, and building collective security in the Indian Ocean Region against common challenges.

questions.question: Where is the first-ever Khelo India Water Sports Festival being held?
questions.explanation: The first-ever Khelo India Water Sports Festival is being hosted at the picturesque Dal Lake in Srinagar. The festival features a vibrant logo showcasing a Shikara against the backdrop of snow-capped mountains and pine trees, symbolizing the region’s natural beauty. Its mascot, the Himalayan Kingfisher, reflects the theme of water and nature. More than 400 athletes from 36 states and Union Territories are participating in events such as rowing, canoeing, and kayaking. Organised by the Jammu & Kashmir Sports Council in collaboration with the Union Ministry of Youth Affairs, this festival highlights Srinagar’s potential as a hub for water sports.

questions.question: How long was Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speech in 2025 that set a record as the longest such address by an Indian Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a landmark Independence Day speech on August 15, 2025, from the Red Fort that lasted 103 minutes. This became the longest Independence Day address by any Indian Prime Minister to date. Such extended speeches reflect his detailed communication style, covering multiple aspects of governance, achievements, and future vision. The record-setting length also highlighted the significance he placed on connecting with citizens on the nation’s 79th Independence Day. By surpassing previous records, the 103-minute duration stands out in history as a benchmark for Independence Day speeches.

questions.question: Under the new FASTag Annual Pass launched by NHAI, how many toll crossings are allowed before the pass expires?
questions.explanation: The FASTag Annual Pass, introduced by NHAI on 15 August 2025, provides a year-long facility for non-commercial vehicle owners to travel seamlessly across national highways without repeated toll recharges. Priced at ₹3,000, the pass remains valid for one year or 200 toll crossings, whichever occurs first. This scheme simplifies highway travel by removing the inconvenience of frequent FASTag top-ups and ensuring zero toll deductions after activation. With nationwide coverage across 1,150 toll plazas and tech-enabled features through the Rajmargyatra App, it enhances convenience, reduces congestion, and supports a smoother, more efficient toll payment ecosystem.

questions.question: Which organization released special picture postcards and a golden cancellation to mark the 50th anniversary of the film Sholay in 2025?
questions.explanation: To celebrate the 50th anniversary of the legendary film Sholay on August 15, 2025, India Post released two exclusive picture postcards, a presentation pack, and a golden cancellation. This tribute was unveiled by the Maharashtra Postal Circle in the presence of the Sippy family and other dignitaries. The release highlighted the unique legacy of Sholay, which originally premiered on August 15, 1975, and remains a milestone in Indian cinema. By merging philately with cultural heritage, India Post not only honored a cinematic masterpiece but also reinforced its tradition of commemorating significant national icons, events, and achievements through postal memorabilia.

questions.question: L. Ganesan, who recently passed away at the age of 80, was serving as the Governor of which state at the time of his death?
questions.explanation: L. Ganesan, a veteran BJP leader and former Rajya Sabha member, passed away at the age of 80 while serving as the 21st Governor of Nagaland. Born in Thanjavur in 1945, he had a long political career, including his tenure as a Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh in 2016. He also held key gubernatorial responsibilities, serving as the Governor of Manipur from August 2021 to February 2023 and taking additional charge of West Bengal between July and November 2022. Since February 2023, he had been serving in Nagaland, where his sudden demise marked the end of his public service journey.

questions.question: In which country did the acting President U Myint Swe pass away at the age of 74?
questions.explanation: U Myint Swe, who was serving as the acting President of Myanmar since February 2021, passed away at the age of 74 in Nay Pyi Taw, the country’s capital. He had previously been sworn in as Vice President in March 2016 and assumed the acting presidency after the detention of President U Win Myint. Suffering from Parkinson’s Disease and other neurological conditions, he had been on medical leave since July 2024. His death marks a significant moment in Myanmar’s recent political history, as he held the nation’s top leadership role during a turbulent period.

questions.question: Who was known as the world’s oldest marathon runner and the ‘Turbaned Tornado’?
questions.explanation: Fauja Singh, famously known as the ‘Turbaned Tornado’, was the world’s oldest marathon runner who passed away at the age of 114 after a tragic accident on the Jalandhar-Pathankot highway in Punjab. Born in 1911, he took up running at 89 and completed multiple marathons across major global cities like London, New York, and Toronto. He also carried the Olympic torch for both the 2004 Athens and 2012 London Olympics. Fauja Singh became a global symbol of strength, endurance, and fitness in old age, featuring alongside sports icons like Muhammad Ali and David Beckham in international campaigns.

questions.question: Which former Gujarat Chief Minister recently died in a plane crash after take-off from Ahmedabad?
questions.explanation: Vijay Rupani, who served as the Chief Minister of Gujarat from 2016 to 2021, tragically lost his life in a plane crash involving a London-bound Dreamliner that crashed shortly after departing from Ahmedabad. His untimely death makes him the second former Gujarat CM to perish in an air accident, following Balwantrai Mehta in 1965. Rupani was a significant political figure in Gujarat’s recent history and held various key positions within the BJP. His demise marks a moment of profound loss for the political community and the state of Gujarat.

questions.question: Who, known as a pioneer of India’s nuclear energy programme and former Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission, recently passed away?
questions.explanation: Dr. M.R. Srinivasan was a key architect of India’s nuclear energy programme and served as the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission. He passed away in Udhagamandalam, Tamil Nadu, at the age of 95. Over his career, he played a pivotal role in the establishment of 18 nuclear power units in India. His contributions were nationally recognized with several civilian honours, including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan. Dr. Srinivasan’s legacy is instrumental in shaping India's peaceful nuclear capabilities and energy independence.

questions.question: Who led ISRO as Chairman from 1994 to 2003 and oversaw its transition to a fully operational phase?
questions.explanation: Dr. K. Kasturirangan served as the Chairman of ISRO from 1994 to 2003, during which he played a pivotal role in transforming India's space program from an experimental phase to a fully operational one. His leadership saw advancements in earth observation, communication satellites, and launch services. Additionally, his initiatives like commercializing space and introducing thematic space missions such as EDUSAT for tele-education and Chandrayaan-1 for lunar exploration had a significant impact on India’s technological and societal growth.

questions.question: Which sport did Bhupinder Singh Rawat play professionally?
questions.explanation: Bhupinder Singh Rawat, known for his speed and agility as a winger, played football professionally until his passing on June 29, 2024, after a brief illness. He represented India in the 1969 Merdeka Cup and played for Delhi Garrison, Gorkha Brigade, and Mafatlal domestically. His nickname "Scooter" highlights his ability to swiftly navigate through opposing defenses.

questions.question: Who is the renowned wildlife field biologist and conservationist?
questions.explanation: A.J.T. Johnsingh, recognized globally for his contributions to wildlife conservation, passed away at the age of 78. His work, spanning decades, included significant efforts in protecting elephants and organizing international conferences. Johnsingh's legacy encompasses not only his scientific contributions but also his mentorship of future conservationists, leaving an enduring impact on India's biodiversity conservation endeavours.

questions.question: Who became India’s first openly queer Member of Parliament after taking oath in the Rajya Sabha in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Menaka Guruswamy made history by becoming India’s first openly queer Member of Parliament after taking oath in the Rajya Sabha in April 2026. A distinguished senior advocate of the Supreme Court of India, she played a key role in the landmark 2018 case that led to the decriminalisation of homosexuality by reading down Section 377 of the IPC. Representing West Bengal as a member of the All India Trinamool Congress, her achievement marks a significant step toward inclusivity and representation of LGBTQ+ individuals in India’s political landscape.

questions.question: Who assumed the role of Managing Director (MD) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Yes Bank on April 6, 2026?
questions.explanation: Vinay Muralidhar Tonse took charge as the Managing Director and CEO of Yes Bank on April 6, 2026, succeeding Prashant Kumar, who completed his tenure. With over 35 years of experience in the banking and financial services sector, he has held several key leadership positions at State Bank of India, including Managing Director (Retail Business & Operations) and MD & CEO of SBI Mutual Funds. His appointment ensures experienced leadership and continuity in the functioning and strategic direction of the bank.

questions.question: Who assumed charge as the Secretary of the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Shri Tejveer Singh, a 1994-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the Punjab cadre, assumed charge as the Secretary of the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) in April 2026. He has held several key administrative positions, including Additional Chief Secretary in Punjab’s Technical Education and Industrial Training Department, and Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister. His extensive administrative experience across various roles, including as District Magistrate, equips him to handle responsibilities related to policy formulation and development in the chemical and petrochemical sectors.

questions.question: Who released the “Market for Textiles and Clothing: National Household Survey 2024” report in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Giriraj Singh, the Union Minister of Textiles, released the National Household Survey 2024 report, which provides key insights into India’s textiles and clothing market. The report highlights significant growth in the sector, with the market size expanding substantially over the past 15 years. It also emphasizes the role of household demand, rising per capita consumption, and changing consumer preferences. The findings indicate strong demand for man-made fibers and sustainable textiles, along with increasing adoption of technical textile products. This report serves as an important resource for policymakers and industry stakeholders to guide future strategies and development.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Secretary of the Department of Land Resources in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Narendra Bhooshan, a senior IAS officer of the 1992 Uttar Pradesh cadre, assumed charge as the Secretary of the Department of Land Resources on April 6, 2026. With over three decades of administrative experience, he has held several key positions at both state and central levels. His previous roles include Additional Chief Secretary for Energy and Technical Education in Uttar Pradesh, as well as leadership positions in infrastructure, science and technology, and urban governance. His extensive experience is expected to contribute significantly to land resource management and rural development initiatives in India.

questions.question: Who recently clinched gold at the Asian Gymnastics Championships?
questions.explanation: Dipa Karmakar made history by securing the gold medal in the women’s vault individual final at the Asian Women’s Artistic Gymnastics Championships 2024, becoming the first-ever Indian to achieve this feat in any Asian Championships. This remarkable accomplishment adds to her previous achievements, including being the first Indian woman gymnast to qualify for the Summer Olympics in 2016.

questions.question: Who received the Amal Clooney Women's Empowerment Award from King Charles III?
questions.explanation: Arti, an 18-year-old woman from Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich district, received the Amal Clooney Women's Empowerment Award from King Charles III. This recognition celebrates her inspiring work as an e-rickshaw driver and her efforts in empowering other young women in her community through initiatives like the Pink E-rickshaw scheme.

questions.question: Who became the first black Astronaut candidate to travel to space at the age of 90?
questions.explanation: Ed Dwight, America’s 1st Black astronaut candidate, made history by travelling to space at the age of 90 aboard a Blue Origin rocket, 60 years after he was initially considered for NASA’s astronaut corps. This milestone marked a significant moment in both space exploration and racial history.

questions.question: Who recently became the oldest Indian Woman to Scale Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Jyoti Atre, aged 55, from Bhopal, achieved the feat of becoming the oldest Indian woman to summit Mount Everest. She reached an altitude of 8,848.86 meters on her second attempt after weather conditions disrupted her 2023 climb at 8,160 meters. Jyoti Atre surpassed the previous record held by Sangeeta Bahl, who scaled Everest on May 19, 2018, at the age of 53.

questions.question: Who recently conquered Mount Everest without supplementary oxygen, becoming only the 2nd Pakistani to achieve this feat?
questions.explanation: Sirbaz Khan, a notable Pakistani mountaineer, scaled Mount Everest without supplementary oxygen, marking him as the second Pakistani to achieve this feat. Khan aims to become the first Pakistani to conquer all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters. Starting his mountaineering career in 2016, he has since emerged as a pioneering figure in high-altitude climbing in Pakistan.

questions.question: Which city in Gujarat will host the 2026 Asian Weightlifting Championships from May 11 to 17, 2026?
questions.explanation: Gandhinagar, the capital city of Gujarat, has been selected as the host venue for the 2026 Asian Weightlifting Championships. The event is scheduled to take place from May 11 to 17, 2026, and it marks a significant milestone as India will organise the championship after a gap of 44 years. Around 180 athletes from 28 countries are expected to participate in the tournament. The championship is also important because it serves as a qualifying event for major international competitions like the Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games, highlighting India’s growing role in hosting international sporting events.

questions.question: Which Indian city is hosting the Kimberley Process Intersessional Meeting 2026 from May 11 to May 14, 2026?
questions.explanation: Mumbai is hosting the Kimberley Process Intersessional Meeting 2026 from May 11 to May 14, 2026, under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. India assumed the Chair of the Kimberley Process on January 1, 2026, focusing on the theme of credibility, compliance, and consumer confidence in the natural diamond sector. The meeting includes representatives from 86 countries and the European Union. The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme was established to prevent conflict diamonds from entering legitimate global markets. India’s role as a major global hub for diamond cutting and polishing further strengthens its importance in the international diamond trade and regulatory framework.

questions.question: Which city’s government launched a new aftercare scheme in May 2026 to support youth leaving child care institutions after turning 18?
questions.explanation: The government of New Delhi launched an aftercare scheme aimed at supporting vulnerable youth transitioning out of child care institutions after reaching the age of 18. The initiative focuses on rehabilitation, financial support, emotional counselling, education, and vocational opportunities. A budget allocation of ₹3.5 crore was made for the 2026-27 financial year to implement the program effectively. The scheme operates under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, which emphasises the welfare and rehabilitation of children in need of care and protection. District and state-level committees will oversee the implementation and ensure individualised care plans for beneficiaries.

questions.question: Which city is hosting India’s first International Ophthalmology Research Conference, AIOS-AFOU 2026?
questions.explanation: India’s first International Ophthalmology Research Conference, AIOS-AFOU 2026, is being held at the Manekshaw Centre in New Delhi on May 09 and 10, 2026. The conference is jointly organised by the Department of Ophthalmology at Army Hospital (Research & Referral) and the All-India Ophthalmological Society. The event focuses on advancements in ophthalmology and encourages collaboration between civil and military medical institutions. Renowned international experts and leading ophthalmologists from premier institutes such as AIIMS New Delhi, PGI Chandigarh, and LV Prasad Eye Institute are participating. The conference also highlights innovations in AI-driven eye diagnostics and modern ophthalmic research.

questions.question: In which city was the 100th N-Gen Post Office inaugurated at North-Eastern Hill University (NEHU)?
questions.explanation: The 100th N-Gen Post Office in India was inaugurated at North-Eastern Hill University (NEHU) in Shillong, Meghalaya, by Union Minister for Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia on May 6, 2026. N-Gen Post Offices are modern postal hubs designed mainly for youth and students within educational institutions. These facilities provide services such as free Wi-Fi, QR-based payment systems, concessional parcel services, and dedicated student service counters. The Shillong branch is unique because it is operated entirely by women staff and incorporates eco-friendly local materials like bamboo and straw, reflecting sustainability and community participation in its design and development.

questions.question: Where was the world's highest observatory inaugurated by the University of Tokyo?
questions.explanation: The University of Tokyo inaugurated the Atacama Observatory (TAO) in Chile's Antofagasta Region, situated at an elevation of 5,640 meters above sea level. This observatory has been recognized by the Guinness World Records as the highest observatory globally. Led by Professor Yuzuru Yoshii, TAO aims to delve into cosmic mysteries such as dark energy and primordial stars, benefitting from its high-altitude location and advanced technological infrastructure.

questions.question: In which country did the 10th World Water Forum officially open?
questions.explanation: The 10th World Water Forum, held under the theme "Water for Shared Prosperity," officially opened in Indonesia's Bali. The forum aims to address crucial topics such as water conservation, clean water and sanitation, food and energy security, and mitigation of natural disasters. Indonesian President Joko Widodo presided over the event, which is expected to host 100,000 participants and feature 350 sessions, highlighting Indonesia's commitment to addressing global water-related challenges.

questions.question: Where is AstraZeneca building a pioneering $1.5 billion manufacturing plant to produce advanced cancer-fighting drugs?
questions.explanation: AstraZeneca is constructing a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Singapore with a focus on producing advanced cancer-fighting drugs known as antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). This significant investment in Singapore's pharmaceutical landscape underscores AstraZeneca's commitment to expanding its global supply chain and leveraging Singapore's reputation for excellence in complex manufacturing.

questions.question: On which date is World Environment Day observed annually?
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is observed every year on June 5 as the United Nations’ flagship initiative to raise global awareness and drive action on pressing environmental issues. It was established in 1972 and has since become a major platform engaging over 150 countries worldwide. The 2025 theme, “Beat Plastic Pollution,” highlights the urgent need to reduce plastic waste that harms ecosystems, wildlife, and human health. The Republic of Korea is hosting the 2025 celebrations, showcasing its leadership in environmental policies and innovative waste management.

questions.question: Which Indian state recently had the Khichan and Menar wetlands added to the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance?
questions.explanation: Khichan and Menar wetlands, located in Rajasthan, were recently added to the Ramsar List of Wetlands of International Importance, increasing India’s total number of Ramsar sites to 91. Khichan in Phalodi is known for attracting thousands of migratory Demoiselle Cranes and is a vital stopover along the Central Asian Flyway. Menar, near Udaipur, is famous as a “bird village” with over 150 bird species, including flamingos and pelicans. This designation highlights India’s commitment to conserving crucial ecosystems and promoting biodiversity through both government efforts and local community participation.

questions.question: What is Nomura’s forecasted GDP growth rate for India in FY26?
questions.explanation: Nomura has projected that India’s GDP growth will slow down to 6.2% in FY26, a slight decline from the 6.5% growth recorded in FY25 and the sharp 9.2% expansion in FY24. This forecast reflects concerns about weakening fundamental economic indicators such as sluggish automobile sales and slow bank credit growth, despite strong headline data like GST collections. The moderation signals a cautious outlook amid global uncertainties and an uneven domestic recovery, contrasting with the Reserve Bank of India’s steady 6.5% growth estimate for the same period.

questions.question: Who is the primary beneficiary of the newly launched C CARES 2.0 portal?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Coal launched the C CARES Version 2.0 portal to enhance the welfare of coal workers by streamlining provident fund (PF) and pension disbursements. Developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), the portal enables real-time tracking of claims, significantly reducing settlement times. This initiative aims to improve social security benefits for coal workers by providing faster and more transparent access to their financial entitlements, reflecting the government’s focus on welfare and efficiency in managing workers’ benefits.

questions.question: Which country became the 101st WTO member to formally accept the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
questions.explanation: Nicaragua became the 101st member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) to accept the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies on June 2, 2025. This agreement aims to combat harmful fishing practices such as illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing by banning subsidies that contribute to overfishing and environmental damage. Nicaragua’s acceptance brings the total number of acceptances closer to the required 111 for the agreement to enter into force, marking a crucial milestone in global marine conservation and sustainable fisheries management efforts.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the 21st President of South Korea, pledging to reopen dialogue with North Korea and maintain a strong alliance with the United States?
questions.explanation: Lee Jae-myung, leader of the Liberal Democratic Party, was sworn in as South Korea’s 21st President for a five-year term. His election marked a commitment to balancing diplomacy by reopening dialogue with North Korea while maintaining a strong security alliance with the United States. His main competitor was Kim Moon-soo from the conservative People Power Party. Lee’s presidency is expected to influence South Korea’s domestic and international policies, especially concerning peace efforts on the Korean Peninsula and relations with global powers.

questions.question: Which country has been elected to the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) for the term 2026-28?
questions.explanation: India has been elected to serve on the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) for a two-year term from 2026 to 2028. ECOSOC is a principal organ of the UN that focuses on advancing sustainable development across economic, social, and environmental dimensions. The council plays a critical role in shaping policies and coordinating efforts among UN agencies to address global challenges, making India's election significant for its increased engagement in international economic and social governance.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Director of the Prime Ministers Museum and Library for a three-year term?
questions.explanation: Ashwani Lohani, a veteran administrator and former CMD of Air India as well as ex-Chairman of the Railway Board, has been appointed as the Director of the Prime Ministers Museum and Library (PMML) for a three-year tenure. His extensive leadership experience in sectors like aviation, railways, and tourism positions him to bring transformative changes to the PMML, an institution dedicated to preserving the legacy of India's Prime Ministers. This appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, filling the vacancy after the previous director’s exit.

questions.question: Which e-commerce firm recently received an NBFC licence from the Reserve Bank of India to enter the direct lending space?
questions.explanation: Flipkart has become the first major Indian e-commerce platform to receive a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) licence from the Reserve Bank of India. This licence allows Flipkart to lend directly to its customers and sellers, enabling it to operate independently in the credit space without intermediaries such as banks or third-party NBFCs. This move marks a significant fintech milestone for Flipkart, expanding its fintech ecosystem through its app, super.money, and transforming the online retail lending landscape in India.

questions.question: Which Indian state has begun exporting green vegetables to Dubai through its cooperative marketing federation, VEGFED?
questions.explanation: Bihar has initiated the export of green vegetables produced by its cooperative marketing federation, VEGFED, which operates similarly to the milk cooperative COMFED. The first consignment, weighing 1,500 kilograms, was shipped to Dubai via Varanasi. This marks a significant step in promoting agricultural exports from Bihar and expanding its market reach internationally. The next planned shipment is set for Singapore, showcasing Bihar’s growing role in the export of fresh produce and enhancing the cooperative movement in the state’s agricultural sector.

questions.question: Where was the National Agro-RE Summit 2025, attended by Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, held?
questions.explanation: The National Agriculture-Renewable Energy Conference 2025, also known as the National Agro-RE Summit 2025, was organized by the National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) and held in New Delhi. Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, participated in the event where he released the federation’s report and annual reference book focused on agriculture and renewable energy. This summit highlights the growing integration of renewable energy initiatives within India’s agricultural sector, emphasizing sustainable development and innovation.

questions.question: Which country was the destination of India’s first Tri-Services All-Women Sailing Team’s historic international open-sea expedition?
questions.explanation: India’s first Tri-Services All-Women Sailing Team completed a pioneering international open-sea expedition by sailing 1,800 nautical miles to Seychelles aboard the indigenous vessel ‘Triveni’. This two-month mission, spanning from April 7 to June 4, 2025, was a landmark achievement showcasing the skill, endurance, and teamwork of women officers from the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force. The voyage demonstrated India’s maritime capabilities, strengthened diplomatic ties with Seychelles, and highlighted women's empowerment within the Indian Armed Forces, marking a significant milestone in military history.

questions.question: In which year will the Government of India conduct the Population Census incorporating caste enumeration for the first time in decades?
questions.explanation: The Population Census of India is scheduled to be conducted in two phases with the primary reference date as March 1, 2027, for most regions. This census will mark a significant milestone by including caste enumeration after a long gap, enabling more detailed socio-economic data collection. The census had been postponed since 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, making 2027 the year to resume this vital demographic exercise to aid governance, planning, and social welfare policy formulation.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the 21st President of South Korea, pledging to reopen dialogue with North Korea and maintain a strong alliance with the United States?
questions.explanation: Lee Jae-myung, leader of the Liberal Democratic Party, was sworn in as South Korea’s 21st President for a five-year term. His election marked a commitment to balancing diplomacy by reopening dialogue with North Korea while maintaining a strong security alliance with the United States. His main competitor was Kim Moon-soo from the conservative People Power Party. Lee’s presidency is expected to influence South Korea’s domestic and international policies, especially concerning peace efforts on the Korean Peninsula and relations with global powers.

questions.question: Which country has denied allegations that police used sonic weapons to disperse anti-government protesters?
questions.explanation: The Serbian government has denied claims that police used sonic weapons to control anti-government protests. Sonic weapons, including Long-Range Acoustic Devices (LRAD), are used for crowd control by emitting concentrated, amplified sound over long distances. These weapons can cause hearing damage and other health issues, with the LRAD producing sounds as high as 160 decibels. Serbia, located in Eastern Europe, has been at the centre of political controversies, particularly concerning its stance on Kosovo's independence, which it does not recognize.

questions.question: Which country’s army took full control of the Presidential Palace in its capital, Khartoum?
questions.explanation: The Sudanese army took full control of the Presidential Palace in Khartoum after months of intense conflict with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The situation escalated with search operations around the palace amidst ongoing gunfire. This ongoing conflict has led to a severe humanitarian crisis in Sudan, with widespread famine and disease affecting many people across the country. The military action marks a critical point in the country’s political turmoil.

questions.question: In which region has the government decided to allocate Rs 3 crore annually for each MLA under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) scheme?
questions.explanation: The Jammu and Kashmir government has made the decision to allocate Rs 3 crore annually for each Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) scheme. This fund allows MLAs to recommend and oversee the implementation of key development projects in their respective constituencies, ensuring that essential projects are funded and managed at the regional level. By empowering the MLAs with this fund, the government aims to enhance local development in the Jammu and Kashmir region.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as Canada's new Liberal Party leader and Prime Minister, replacing Justin Trudeau?
questions.explanation: Mark Carney has been appointed as the new leader of Canada’s Liberal Party and the country’s next Prime Minister, succeeding Justin Trudeau. Carney, a former central banker with extensive experience in both the Bank of Canada and the Bank of England, won 85.9% of the votes in the leadership race. His victory marks a significant shift for the Liberal Party following Trudeau’s resignation due to rising internal opposition. Carney now faces the challenge of leading the party through the upcoming general elections and responding to the political climate.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as Israel’s new Chief of Staff?
questions.explanation: Eyal Zamir has been appointed as Israel's new Chief of Staff at a critical moment in the country's military history. He succeeds Lieutenant General Herzi Halevi, who resigned following the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Zamir, a former tank commander with extensive experience in military leadership, is expected to lead Israel's military efforts against Hamas and Iran. His previous roles include serving as the head of Southern Command and as Deputy Chief of Staff. Zamir is known for his tough, mission-oriented leadership style and his focus on ensuring Israel's security.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh for the fourth term?
questions.explanation: N. Chandrababu Naidu has been sworn in for his fourth term as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh. He previously served as Chief Minister during two terms of the undivided Andhra Pradesh and was also the first Chief Minister of the newly bifurcated Andhra Pradesh from 2014 to 2019. His recent oath-taking ceremony marked his return to power following a significant electoral victory in 2024.

questions.question: Who recently took oath as the Chief Minister of Sikkim for the second consecutive term?
questions.explanation: Prem Singh Tamang, the leader of Sikkim Krantikari Morcha (SKM), was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Sikkim for the second consecutive term on June 10. Administered by Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya at Paljor Stadium in Gangtok, the oath ceremony included 11 other Ministers from the SKM party. Tamang's reelection follows SKM's landslide victory in the state's recent elections, securing 31 out of 32 seats in the assembly. His leadership is pivotal as the state progresses under SKM's governance for another term.

questions.question: Who is set to be sworn in as Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister on June 12?
questions.explanation: After a decade-long hiatus, N. Chandrababu Naidu, the leader of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), is poised to reclaim the Chief Minister's position in Andhra Pradesh. His swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for June 12 at Kesarapalli IT Park near Gannavaram Airport, with elaborate arrangements being made for the event.

questions.question: In which Lok Sabha constituency did NOTA create a record with 2.18 lakh voters opting for it?
questions.explanation: NOTA created a record in Madhya Pradesh's Indore Lok Sabha constituency, with 2.18 lakh voters opting for the 'none of the above' option in the Lok Sabha elections. This significant number underscores the voters' dissatisfaction with the available candidates and their desire to exercise their right to abstain from voting for any of them.

questions.question: In which country did Claudia Sheinbaum become the first woman president?
questions.explanation: Claudia Sheinbaum's election as the first woman president of Mexico marks a significant milestone in the nation's political history, symbolizing a stride towards gender inclusivity in leadership roles. Sheinbaum's victory from the ruling Morena party reflects shifting political landscapes and aspirations for change within Mexico. Her background as a climate activist and former mayor of Mexico City adds depth to her leadership profile, resonating with environmental concerns and urban governance issues. This historic moment underscores Mexico's evolving socio-political dynamics and aspirations for progressive leadership.

questions.question: Which Indian state has launched a statewide Foot and Mouth Disease vaccination drive under the National Animal Disease Control Programme?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has initiated a large-scale Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccination drive to protect livestock and prevent the spread of this highly contagious viral infection. The campaign is being conducted under the National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) and runs from March 1 to April 15. It targets animals such as cattle, buffalo, sheep, and goats, which are highly vulnerable to the disease. Veterinary teams are actively visiting villages and farms to administer vaccines and monitor animal health. The initiative also uses digital tools like the INAPH portal to track vaccination coverage and ensure effective disease control.

questions.question: Which company received regulatory approval in China for the anaemia drug Desidustat?
questions.explanation: Zydus Lifesciences secured regulatory approval from China’s National Medical Products Administration for its innovative drug Desidustat, used to treat renal anaemia in chronic kidney disease patients. The drug functions as a HIF-PHI inhibitor, stimulating red blood cell production and improving iron metabolism. It has already shown strong clinical efficacy in Phase III trials conducted in China. The approval is significant due to China’s large CKD patient population. Additionally, the drug has been successfully marketed in India under the brand Oxemia, benefiting over 100,000 patients since its launch in 2022, highlighting its therapeutic effectiveness and commercial potential.

questions.question: At which institution were Odisha’s first comprehensive Liver Transplant Unit and a Robotic Surgery System inaugurated?
questions.explanation: AIIMS Bhubaneshwar is the institution where Odisha’s first comprehensive Liver Transplant Unit and a Robotic Surgery System were inaugurated by Health Minister JP Nadda through a virtual event. This development marks a significant healthcare milestone for eastern India by enabling advanced organ transplantation and minimally invasive robotic surgeries. The new facilities are expected to greatly benefit patients from Odisha and neighbouring states by providing access to world-class treatment closer to home. The initiative also aligns with the broader vision of promoting organ donation awareness and strengthening healthcare innovation across the region.

questions.question: Which vaccine has been additionally prequalified by the World Health Organisation to strengthen the global response against circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2)?
questions.explanation: The World Health Organisation has prequalified an additional novel oral polio vaccine type 2 (nOPV2) to enhance global outbreak response against circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (cVDPV2). This vaccine is genetically more stable than older oral polio vaccines and carries a lower risk of mutating into virulent strains while maintaining its ability to quickly stop virus transmission. The prequalification confirms that it meets international standards for safety, quality, and effectiveness, enabling global procurement and distribution. It also diversifies vaccine supply and strengthens worldwide efforts aimed at the final eradication of polio.

questions.question: Which organisation is leading the development of an improved Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD) vaccine and has initiated Phase I human clinical trials?
questions.explanation: ICMR is the organisation spearheading the development of an improved Kyasanur Forest Disease vaccine in India. As the country’s apex body for biomedical research, it has taken responsibility for advancing an indigenous solution to protect vulnerable populations in the Western Ghats region. The vaccine has successfully completed animal studies and toxicity testing and has now entered Phase I human clinical trials after regulatory approval. Through collaboration with scientific and manufacturing partners, ICMR’s effort highlights India’s growing capability in vaccine research, regional disease control, and strengthening public health security.

questions.question: Which institution's scientists developed a promising new malaria vaccine candidate?
questions.explanation: Scientists at Jawaharlal Nehru University, led by Shailja Singh and Anand Ranganathan, identified the Prohibitin protein (PfPHB2) as a novel vaccine target for malaria. Their research, published in iScience, highlights the protein's interaction with the human red blood cell protein Hsp70A1A, crucial for parasite infection. This discovery opens avenues for developing effective malaria vaccines and combating drug resistance associated with the disease.

questions.question: Which pharmaceutical company has received approval from the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) to market generic medication for treating asthma?
questions.explanation: Zydus Lifesciences has obtained final approval from the USFDA to market Theophylline extended-release tablets (300 mg and 450 mg), a generic medication used to treat asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). This approval enables Zydus to introduce this medication to the US market, expanding its pharmaceutical offerings.

questions.question: Which company manufactures the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine?
questions.explanation: The R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine, endorsed by the WHO, was manufactured and scaled up by the Serum Institute of India (SII). This vaccine, developed by the University of Oxford, utilizes Novavax's adjuvant technology to enhance its effectiveness in combating malaria.

questions.question: Who became the youngest and fastest swimmer to cross the Palk Strait from Sri Lanka to India in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Seven-year-old Ishank Singh from Ranchi, Jharkhand, created a world record by swimming across the 29-km Palk Strait from Sri Lanka to India on April 30, 2026. He completed the challenging open sea route from Talaimannar in Sri Lanka to Dhanushkodi in Tamil Nadu in 9 hours and 50 minutes. The achievement was officially recognised by the Universal Records Forum (URF), which awarded him the title of the Youngest and Fastest Palk Strait Swimmer. During the swim, he received security support from the Sri Lankan Navy and the Indian Coast Guard. His training for the endurance challenge was conducted at Dhurwa Dam in Ranchi under the guidance of coaches Aman Kumar Jaiswal and Bajrang Kumar.

questions.question: Who won the 2026 WTA 1000 Madrid Open women’s singles title by defeating Mirra Andreeva in the final?
questions.explanation: Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine won the 2026 Madrid Open women’s singles title after defeating Russia’s Mirra Andreeva in straight sets, 7-5, 6-3. The victory marked Kostyuk’s third career WTA tournament title and her first-ever WTA 1000-level championship. At 23 years of age, she also became only the second player ranked outside the top 20 to win the Madrid Open women’s singles event. The triumph followed her recent title win at Rouen, making it her second consecutive tournament victory. Kostyuk celebrated the achievement with an acrobatic backflip on the clay court, which gained recognition from legendary gymnast Nadia Comaneci.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the brand ambassador for the F1 Programme in India by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited?
questions.explanation: Shreyas Iyer has been appointed as the brand ambassador for the F1 Programme in India by Mumbai Falcons Racing Limited. This initiative coincides with the launch of the F1 Sim Racing India Open 2026, aimed at promoting esports talent in the country. Iyer’s selection reflects his strong appeal among youth and his reputation for leadership and performance in cricket. His involvement is expected to help bridge traditional sports with the rapidly growing esports industry. The program also seeks to create structured opportunities for aspiring racers, connecting gaming with professional motorsport and expanding India’s presence in global esports.

questions.question: Which state's football club successfully defended its title by defeating Zinc Football Academy 3-0 in the final of the AIFF Elite Youth League 2025-26 on April 28, 2026?
questions.explanation: On April 28, 2026, Punjab FC defended their title by defeating Zinc Football Academy 3-0 in the final match of the AIFF Elite Youth League 2025-26. The championship final was played at the Ramsar Sahib Sports Stadium in Paddi Sura Singh, Garhshankar, Hoshiarpur, Punjab. After a goalless first half, Punjab FC scored three goals within a 10-minute window: Karish Soram (69th minute), captain Vishal Yadav (70th minute), and Thongram Rishikanta Singh (79th minute). Viswajeet was the goalkeeper for Punjab FC. The AIFF, established in 1937 and headquartered in New Delhi, is the national governing body for football in India.

questions.question: In which city did the International Chess Federation (FIDE) join the International World Games Association during its AGM in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Lausanne served as the venue for a significant development in the global sports community, where the International Chess Federation became a member of the International World Games Association. This move marked the inclusion of mind sports into the broader World Games framework, highlighting the growing recognition of intellectual competitions alongside physical sports. The event took place at the Olympic Museum, reinforcing the city’s status as a major hub for international sports organisations. This development also strengthens chess’s global profile and aligns it more closely with other internationally recognised sporting disciplines.

questions.question: Who won the Gold in the men's T63 high jump at the World Para Athletics Championships?
questions.explanation: Mariyappan Thangavelu secured the Gold in the men's T63 high jump event at the World Para Athletics Championships by setting a championship record of 1.88 meters. This victory adds to his previous accolades from the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2021 Paralympics, showcasing his exceptional talent and consistency in para-athletics.

questions.question: Which country has been awarded the hosting rights for the 2027 Women's World Cup football?
questions.explanation: Brazil has been awarded the hosting rights for the 2027 Women's World Cup, marking a historic moment for South American football. This decision came after the Brazilian bid triumphed over the joint bid from Belgium, Netherlands, and Germany, making Brazil the first South American country to host the prestigious tournament.

questions.question: Who won the gold medal in the women's F51 club throw event at the World Para Athletic Championships?
questions.explanation: Ekta Bhayan secured the gold medal in the women's F51 club throw event at the World Para Athletic Championships with a season's best of 20.12m. This achievement adds to her previous successes, including a gold medal at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta and a bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in China.

questions.question: Which state became the first in India to complete all priority areas under both Phase I and Phase II of the Compliance Reduction and Deregulation initiative in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Tripura became the first Indian state to complete all 51 priority areas under the national Compliance Reduction and Deregulation initiative launched in January 2026. The initiative, led by the Cabinet Secretariat, focuses on simplifying governance, reducing regulatory burdens, and improving ease of doing business. Tripura introduced several digital governance reforms, including a centralised e-Gazette system, an upgraded SWAGAAT single-window approval platform, and an auto-appeal mechanism under the Right to Services framework. The state also implemented sectoral reforms such as self-certification for land-use approvals and inspection exemptions for industries, while partnering with National Law University Tripura and IIM Calcutta for legal review and impact assessment.

questions.question: Which Indian state implemented a rotational work-from-home policy for specific government employees on May 14, 2026, to conserve fuel and reduce expenditure?
questions.explanation: Tripura introduced a rotational work-from-home policy for Group C and Group D government employees to reduce fuel consumption and state expenditure. Under this arrangement, only 50 percent of employees attend offices physically each day, while the remaining staff work remotely on a weekly rotational basis. Employees working from home are required to stay electronically connected and must report immediately during emergencies. Essential and emergency services were exempted from the directive to ensure uninterrupted public services. Tripura, with its capital at Agartala, became a full-fledged state on January 21, 1972, under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971.

questions.question: Which state signed an agreement with the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) and the Department of Telecommunications for implementing the Amended BharatNet Programme?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh signed an agreement with the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), the Department of Telecommunications, BSNL, APBIL, and APSFL for implementing the Amended BharatNet Programme. The Central Government approved financial support of ₹2,432 crore for the project. The initiative aims to strengthen digital infrastructure by covering 13,426 Gram Panchayats and providing on-demand connectivity to thousands of villages. It also plans to facilitate more than 5 lakh rural home fibre connections. BharatNet is a flagship programme intended to expand broadband connectivity to rural India, while DBN, formerly known as USOF, funds major telecom and digital inclusion projects across the country.

questions.question: How many states were felicitated by NeGD for DigiLocker integration initiatives in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The National e-Governance Division (NeGD) felicitated five states for their successful integration of DigiLocker with citizen services during the National Consultative Workshop on Strengthening Cybersecurity Frameworks for State Data held on May 11, 2026. The recognised states included Karnataka, Gujarat, Keralam, Nagaland, and Rajasthan for their achievements in digital governance and service integration. DigiLocker, launched under the Digital India programme in 2015, enables citizens to securely access and store digital documents online. NeGD, functioning under the Digital India Corporation, plays an important role in promoting e-governance and digital public infrastructure across India.

questions.question: Which state cabinet approved the draft Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The Assam cabinet approved the draft Uniform Civil Code (UCC) Bill in May 2026, with plans to introduce it in the state legislative assembly on May 26, 2026. The proposed law aims to regulate civil matters such as marriage, divorce, live-in relationships, and compulsory marriage registration through a common legal framework. Tribal communities in Assam are exempted from the bill to preserve their traditional customs and cultural practices. The bill aligns structurally with UCC models of states like Gujarat, Uttarakhand, and Goa. Article 44 of the Indian Constitution mentions the Uniform Civil Code as a Directive Principle of State Policy.

questions.question: Which state leads in Transmission line additions by State Utilities according to statistics released by the Central Electricity Authority?
questions.explanation: According to statistics released by the Central Electricity Authority, Uttar Pradesh (UP) has topped the list for adding transmission lines of 1,460 Circuit km by state transmission utilities in FY24. UPPTCL, founded in 1999 and headquartered in Lucknow, also led in FY23 with the addition of 1,447 Circuit km of transmission lines, showcasing its consistent efforts in enhancing the state's transmission infrastructure.

questions.question: Jyoti Ratre, who became the oldest Indian woman to conquer Mount Everest, hails from which state?
questions.explanation: Jyoti Ratre, the entrepreneur and fitness enthusiast who became the oldest Indian woman to conquer Mount Everest, is from Madhya Pradesh. Her remarkable achievement highlights the spirit of determination and resilience, inspiring others to pursue their dreams relentlessly.

questions.question: In which Indian state has the mandate for 33% reservation for women in government contract jobs been implemented?
questions.explanation: Karnataka has implemented a policy mandating 33% reservation for women in outsourced government contract jobs across all departments. This initiative aims to promote gender equality and empower women in the workforce. The mandate applies to jobs lasting more than 45 days with over 20 employees and reflects Karnataka's commitment to inclusivity and diversity in government employment.

questions.question: When is the World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought celebrated?
questions.explanation: The World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought is observed annually on June 17th. This day serves to raise awareness about the challenges of land degradation and the importance of sustainable land management practices worldwide.

questions.question: In which position will India rank among countries with its own Deep Sea Mission?
questions.explanation: India is poised to become the sixth country globally to launch its own Deep Sea Mission. This initiative aims to explore ocean depths, develop indigenous technologies like the Matsyayaan 6000 submersible, and advance ocean sciences for sustainable marine resource management. The mission underscores India's commitment to pioneering deep-sea exploration and enhancing its capabilities in oceanographic research and technology development.

questions.question: Which organization entered its name into the Limca Book of Records for hosting the most people at a public service event?
questions.explanation: Indian Railways achieved a milestone by being recognized in the Limca Book of Records for organizing the largest public service event, attended by a staggering 40,19,516 people across 2,140 venues. The event, which took place on February 26, 2024, marked the inauguration of several railway infrastructure projects, including road over/under railway bridges and the laying of foundation stones for new railway stations, underscoring Indian Railways' significant role in national development and public service initiatives.

questions.question: Where were fossils of the new dinosaur species, Musankwa sanyatiensis, discovered?
questions.explanation: Fossils of the new dinosaur species, Musankwa sanyatiensis, were discovered along the shores of Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe. This herbivorous dinosaur lived approximately 210 million years ago during the Late Triassic period and is notable as the first dinosaur named from the Mid-Zambezi Basin in over 50 years, highlighting Zimbabwe's significance in paleontological discoveries.

questions.question: What is the name of the satellite used by Chinese scientists to discover a new pattern in solar rotation?
questions.explanation: Chinese scientists utilized the CHASE (Chinese H-alpha Solar Explorer) satellite to identify a novel pattern in the rotational dynamics of the solar atmosphere. Launched in October 2021 with a planned operational span of three years, CHASE orbits Earth in a fixed position relative to the sun, enabling continuous observation of solar phenomena and contributing valuable insights into solar physics and atmospheric dynamics.

questions.question: Who secured a second term as President of South Africa?
questions.explanation: Cyril Ramaphosa was reelected for a second term as President of South Africa on June 14, following a coalition agreement with a former political opponent just hours before the parliamentary vote. He secured 283 votes against Julius Malema's 44, marking his continuation in office after first assuming the presidency in 2018. This reelection underscores his political leadership and coalition-building efforts in South Africa's evolving political landscape.

questions.question: In which Indian state did the launch 'Mission Nishchay'?
questions.explanation: Punjab Police initiated 'Mission Nishchay' in the Fazilka district of Punjab, collaborating with BSF and Village Defence Committees to combat drug trafficking along the India-Pakistan border. This initiative aims to gather intelligence and engage local communities in efforts to curb drug-related activities, focusing on areas with significant border proximity and historical drug trafficking incidences.

questions.question: Where is the Malabar River Festival 2024 set to take place?
questions.explanation: The Malabar River Festival 2024, featuring the International White Water Kayaking Championship, will be hosted in Kerala's Kozhikode. This event will showcase the thrilling sport of white-water kayaking across several rivers including Thusaharagiri, Chalipuzha, and Iruvazhinjipuzha, attracting participants from around the world.

questions.question: Who was named a Land Hero by the UNCCD for his contributions to natural farming and waste management?
questions.explanation: Siddhesh Sakore, recognized as a Land Hero by the UNCCD, is celebrated for his innovations in natural farming and waste management. His efforts, highlighted on World Desertification and Drought Day, emphasize sustainable agriculture practices and solutions for soil degradation, benefiting farmers and ecosystems alike.
