questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Chairperson of Nasscom in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Srikanth Velamakanni, Co-Founder and Group CEO of Fractal, has been appointed as the Chairperson of Nasscom. He succeeds Sindhu Gangadharan and brings extensive experience from his prior role as Vice Chairperson and Executive Council member for over six years. Under his leadership, Nasscom is expected to focus on advancing enterprise AI, agentic AI, and autonomous multi-agent systems. His appointment reflects the growing importance of artificial intelligence in India’s technology sector. Along with Vice Chairperson Kishor Patil and President Rajesh Nambiar, he will help shape the strategic direction of the IT industry.

questions.question: Which organisation is responsible for grassroots delivery and community-based intervention in the e-SafeHER cybersecurity awareness program?
questions.explanation: The Reliance Foundation partnered with C-DAC Hyderabad to launch the e-SafeHER program on April 13, 2026, under MeitY’s ISEA programme. The initiative aims to train one million rural women (Cyber Sakhis) by 2029, with phased rollout starting in Madhya Pradesh and Odisha through women’s Self-Help Groups using a peer-led model. C-DAC Hyderabad develops localised multilingual training content, while Reliance Foundation handles grassroots delivery. The program enhances last-mile cybersecurity awareness for secure digital transactions and rural livelihoods. C-DAC, established in 1988 and headquartered in Pune, is a premier R&D organisation under MeitY. Reliance Foundation, established in 2010 and based in Mumbai, drives community-based intervention under this initiative.

questions.question: Who inaugurated the Robotic Orthopaedic System and Maternity Operation Theatre at the Cantonment General Hospital in April 2026?
questions.explanation: Rajesh Kumar Singh, serving as the Defence Secretary, inaugurated advanced medical facilities at the Cantonment General Hospital in Delhi Cantt on April 23, 2026. These facilities included a Robotic Orthopaedic System designed to enhance surgical precision and reduce recovery time, along with a dedicated Maternity Operation Theatre for improved maternal care. The initiative reflects the Ministry of Defence’s commitment to strengthening healthcare infrastructure for defence personnel and civilians. Additional planned upgrades, such as dialysis centres, ICU enhancements, and advanced diagnostic tools, further highlight a comprehensive approach toward modernising medical services.

questions.question: In which state is the 7th edition of the India–Japan Joint Military Exercise ‘Dharma Guardian’ being conducted?
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand is the state where the 7th edition of the India–Japan Joint Military Exercise ‘Dharma Guardian’ is being held at the Foreign Training Node in Chaubattia. The exercise involves participation from the Indian Army and the Japan Ground Self-Defence Force, with 120 personnel from each side. The drill focuses on enhancing interoperability, strengthening military collaboration, and improving joint operational capabilities in semi-urban environments. Activities such as heliborne operations, cordon and search missions, intelligence grid development, and house intervention drills are conducted to ensure combat readiness and coordinated response to regional security challenges.

questions.question: In which state was the new snake species Calamaria garoensis discovered in 2026?
questions.explanation: The newly identified snake species, Calamaria garoensis, was discovered in the West Garo Hills region, a biodiversity-rich area known for its dense forests and ecological significance. This species was earlier misclassified but later recognised as distinct through detailed taxonomic research. The discovery highlights the rich herpetofaunal diversity of Northeast India, particularly within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot. Meghalaya, with its unique terrain and ecosystems, continues to be a crucial region for biological discoveries, contributing significantly to scientific understanding and conservation of lesser-known reptile species.

questions.question: On which date is World Cancer Day observed globally to raise awareness and promote cancer prevention?
questions.explanation: World Cancer Day is observed every year on February 4 with the objective of increasing global awareness about cancer and encouraging its prevention, detection, and treatment. The day brings together individuals, organisations, and governments to address the growing burden of cancer and work toward equitable access to care for all. The theme “United by Unique” emphasizes people-centered cancer care and recognises that every individual’s experience with cancer is different. Established in 2000 by the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC), the observance plays a key role in mobilising global action to reduce cancer-related deaths worldwide.

questions.question: On which date is World Health Day observed globally every year?
questions.explanation: April 7 is observed annually as World Health Day to mark the founding of the World Health Organization in 1948. The day highlights global health issues and promotes awareness about key public health challenges. In 2026, the theme “Together for health. Stand with science” emphasises the importance of scientific collaboration in improving global health outcomes. Various international events, including forums and summits, are organised to address health concerns and strengthen partnerships. The observance serves as a reminder of the need for accessible healthcare and coordinated global efforts to tackle emerging health threats.

questions.question: Which two countries were added to the FATF “grey list” for increased monitoring due to deficiencies in anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing frameworks in February 2026?
questions.explanation: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), an international body responsible for setting standards to combat money laundering and terrorist financing, placed Kuwait and Papua New Guinea on its “grey list” for increased monitoring after its February 2026 plenary meeting. Countries on this list have strategic deficiencies in their financial monitoring systems and must implement specific action plans within a given timeframe to address these gaps. While the grey list expanded, the FATF “black list” remained unchanged and includes Iran, North Korea, and Myanmar. The monitoring aims to safeguard the global financial system while ensuring humanitarian financial flows are not disrupted.

questions.question: Which port in southern India became the first in the country to deploy an advanced anti-drone system to strengthen coastal and infrastructure security?
questions.explanation: VOC Port, officially known as V.O. Chidambaranar Port at Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu, created history by becoming India’s first port to deploy an advanced anti-drone system. The system integrates radar and radio frequency technologies to provide 360-degree surveillance and real-time detection, tracking, and neutralisation of unauthorised drones. This initiative enhances the safety of port assets, personnel, and cargo while addressing emerging aerial threats. The deployment aligns with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Amrit Kaal Vision 2047, positioning the port as a benchmark for technology-driven maritime security in India.

questions.question: Until which year has the Andhra Pradesh government extended the Ragi Java nutrition programme for government school students?
questions.explanation: The Andhra Pradesh government extended the Ragi Java nutrition programme for government school students until April 2029 through an agreement signed with the Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust. The programme provides a daily nutritious drink made from ragi flour and jaggery, both supplied free of cost by the trust. It currently benefits more than 30 lakh students studying in nearly 44,000 government schools across the state. The initiative aims to improve children’s health, energy levels, attentiveness in classrooms, and school attendance. The Sri Sathya Sai Central Trust, founded in 1972, has been actively supporting welfare and educational initiatives in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: In which city was the 5th Bollywood Maha Arogya Shivir (Mega Health Camp) organised, setting a world record for the largest health camp of 2026?
questions.explanation: The Mega Health Camp, organised by DRVA Charitable Trust and Doctor 365, achieved international recognition for its scale and impact. The event was held in Mumbai, where it received acknowledgement from the IEA and ACE Book of World Records as the world’s largest health camp of 2026. The camp delivered extensive free healthcare services, including health checkups, distribution of medicines worth ₹2.5 crore, and issuance of nearly 5 lakh health cards. Hosting such a large-scale public health initiative in Mumbai highlights the city’s role as a major hub for social, medical, and charitable activities in India.

questions.question: Which region of India witnessed the inauguration of a new District Court Complex at Kargil?
questions.explanation: The District Court Complex at Kargil was inaugurated to enhance judicial infrastructure in the remote and high-altitude region of Ladakh. Due to harsh climatic conditions, the inauguration was conducted virtually by the Chief Justice of India. Ladakh’s unique geographical challenges often make access to justice difficult for residents. The newly constructed complex, equipped with modern facilities and climate-resilient design, aims to address these issues. By bringing legal services closer to the people, especially in border districts like Kargil, it improves accessibility, reduces travel hardships, and strengthens the delivery of justice in the region.

questions.question: Which former India captain will have a stand named after him at Mumbai’s Wankhede Stadium?
questions.explanation: Ravi Shastri will have a stand named after him at the iconic Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai following approval by the Mumbai Cricket Association during its Apex Council meeting. The Level 1 Stand below the Press Box will bear his name, recognising his long and multifaceted contribution to Indian cricket as a player, captain, head coach, and commentator. A former all-rounder, he was part of India’s 1983 World Cup era and later guided the national team to significant overseas Test victories as coach. The tribute highlights Mumbai’s rich cricketing legacy and honours his enduring association with the sport.

questions.question: Which Indian state secured ₹2,000 crore investment interest during a Business Conclave and roadshow held in Bengaluru on December 04, 2026?
questions.explanation: Tripura attracted significant investment interest worth ₹2,000 crore during a Business Conclave and roadshow organised in Bengaluru. The event was conducted by the state’s Industries and Commerce Department to connect with investors, start-ups, and institutional stakeholders from Southern India. This initiative also served as a precursor to the upcoming ‘Destination Tripura: Business Conclave 2026’ in Agartala. Tripura, a northeastern state that gained full statehood in 1972, is notable for being the second-largest producer of natural rubber in India and shares a long international border with Bangladesh.

questions.question: Which state government approved a ₹50 crore heritage grant to preserve and restore the legacy of the Darrang kings of the Koch dynasty?
questions.explanation: The government of Assam approved a ₹50 crore grant to preserve the heritage of the Darrang kings of the Koch dynasty, reflecting a strong commitment to safeguarding indigenous history and culture. The initiative focuses on restoring royal sites, monuments, and culturally significant landmarks associated with the Koch rulers. Announced during Mahabir Chilarai Divas, the project also aims to honour the legacy of Mahabir Chilarai, one of Assam’s greatest military leaders. Beyond conservation, the effort seeks to develop the region into a major cultural tourism hub, linking historical preservation with economic and community development.

questions.question: Which state approved the use of paper ballots instead of EVMs for upcoming Panchayat and civic body elections to strengthen public trust in the electoral process?
questions.explanation: Karnataka decided to reintroduce paper ballots for both rural and urban local body elections, including Zilla and Taluk Panchayats as well as Greater Bengaluru civic polls. The decision, taken by the state cabinet led by Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, aims to enhance transparency and rebuild public confidence in the electoral system. This change will apply to all forthcoming local body elections in the state and will replace the use of electronic voting machines. To facilitate the shift, amendments to the Karnataka Conduct of Election Rules are to be introduced within a short timeframe.

questions.question: In which Indian state will India’s first indigenous Green Urea plant be set up at the Pudimadaka Green Hydrogen Hub?
questions.explanation: India’s first indigenous Green Urea plant is planned at the Pudimadaka Green Hydrogen Hub in Andhra Pradesh through a collaboration between NTPC Green Energy Ltd and Assago. The project will use renewable hydrogen and green ammonia, marking a major step toward sustainable fertilizer production. By supplying green ammonia, carbon dioxide, and renewable energy, the initiative aims to significantly reduce India’s dependence on urea imports, which currently range between 8–10 million tonnes annually. Locating the project in Andhra Pradesh strengthens the state’s role in green energy infrastructure while supporting national goals of lowering carbon emissions and enhancing self-reliance.

questions.question: Which state government launched the Banglar Yuva Sathi Scheme 2026 to provide monthly financial assistance to unemployed youth?
questions.explanation: West Bengal launched the Banglar Yuva Sathi Scheme 2026 to provide ₹1,500 per month to eligible unemployed youth aged 21–40 years through Direct Benefit Transfer into Aadhaar-linked bank accounts. The scheme offers support for up to five years or until beneficiaries secure employment or self-employment. Announced during the interim budget for 2026–27 and administered by the Department of Sports and Youth Services, it aims to provide interim financial relief amid rising joblessness. With a significant budget allocation and large-scale registrations, the initiative targets lakhs of beneficiaries across the state.

questions.question: Which organisation, functioning under the Ministry of Science & Technology, facilitated the transfer of 13 indigenous technologies developed by the Central Building Research Institute to industries and start-ups on National Technology Day 2026?
questions.explanation: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) is an autonomous body operating under the Ministry of Science & Technology. It facilitated the transfer of 13 indigenous technologies developed by the Central Building Research Institute (CBRI) during the National Technology Day event held on May 12, 2026. These technologies were related to fire safety, sustainable construction, infrastructure protection, energy efficiency, and advanced building materials. Headquartered in New Delhi and established in 1942, the organisation plays a major role in advancing scientific research, innovation, and industrial development in India through its network of laboratories and institutes.

questions.question: Which city deployed the AI-based “G-SPIDER” robot for hazardous canal maintenance to eliminate manual scavenging?
questions.explanation: The municipal corporation of Thiruvananthapuram introduced the AI-powered “G-SPIDER” robotic system to carry out hazardous canal maintenance and eliminate manual scavenging. Developed by Genrobotic Innovations, the robot operates using Cable-Driven Parallel Robotics along with a biomimetic claw that can grasp and remove irregular debris from canals. The initiative is part of the Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0, aiming to achieve completely human-free cleaning of the Amayizhanchan canal. The robot is equipped with artificial intelligence that identifies different types of waste in real time and transfers the extracted materials directly to collection vehicles, ensuring safer and more efficient waste management while preventing human exposure to toxic substances.

questions.question: Who has assumed charge as the Chairman of the Council for Leather Exports, bringing over four decades of experience in the leather industry?
questions.explanation: Ramesh Kumar Juneja has taken charge as the Chairman of the Council for Leather Exports (CLE), the apex body promoting Indian leather, footwear, and related products in global markets under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. With over 40 years of experience, including founding the JC Group and pioneering global collaborations, Juneja brings deep industry knowledge and long-standing institutional involvement with CLE. His leadership is expected to strengthen India’s international leather trade, focus on value addition, innovation, and market diversification, and address challenges such as sustainability standards and global competition, thereby supporting the sector’s growth and export potential.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board from January 1, 2026?
questions.explanation: A K Balasubrahmanian has taken charge as the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, marking an important leadership transition in India’s nuclear regulatory framework. He brings with him around four decades of experience as a nuclear engineer and is widely recognized for his expertise in Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) safety, ageing management, and reactor technologies. Prior to this appointment, he chaired the PHWR Project Design Safety Committee and served on multiple AERB safety review panels. His appointment reflects continuity and depth of technical leadership in nuclear safety regulation.

questions.question: What Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) per quintal was approved for sugarcane farmers for the Sugar Season 2026-27?
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane at Rs. 365 per quintal for the Sugar Season 2026-27. This rate is applicable for a basic recovery rate of 10.25% and will come into effect from October 1, 2026. Farmers are eligible for additional premiums if the sugar recovery rate exceeds the benchmark, while deductions apply for lower recovery rates. The decision benefits nearly 5 crore sugarcane farmers and lakhs of workers employed in sugar mills and related industries. The FRP system ensures fair compensation to farmers while maintaining stability in the sugar sector.

questions.question: What was the annual rate of inflation based on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for March 2026 in India?
questions.explanation: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for March 2026 in India was recorded at 3.88% on a year-on-year basis. WPI reflects price changes at the wholesale or factory level and is an important indicator of inflationary trends in the economy. Among the components, Primary Articles showed higher inflation at 6.36%, while Manufactured Products stood at 3.39% and Fuel & Power at 1.05%. Despite stable food inflation at 1.85%, sharp price fluctuations were observed in commodities like crude petroleum and vegetables, indicating sector-specific volatility within the broader inflation framework.

questions.question: On which date is World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day observed annually?
questions.explanation: World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day is observed every year on May 08 to recognise humanitarian efforts carried out across the world by volunteers and aid workers. The day commemorates the birth anniversary of Henry Dunant, the founder of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. In 2026, the theme was “United in Humanity. No Matter Where, No Matter When,” highlighting the importance of humanitarian assistance during conflicts, disasters, and refugee crises. Volunteers and relief workers provided support in regions affected by war, displacement, and infrastructure damage, including areas in the Middle East, Ukraine, and refugee camps in Chad, demonstrating global solidarity and compassion.

questions.question: Which country was elected by acclamation to several subsidiary bodies of the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)?
questions.explanation: India was elected by acclamation to multiple subsidiary bodies of the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), reflecting its growing global influence and active participation in international governance. These bodies include the Commission on Science and Technology for Development and the Committee on Non-Governmental Organisations. Additionally, India secured a position in the Committee for Programme and Coordination for the term 2027–2029. This election highlights India’s commitment to global development, multilateral cooperation, and its role in shaping policies related to science, technology, and social and economic progress worldwide.

questions.question: Which country is the final international destination covered in the Bharat Gaurav Mystic Mountain Tour launched by IRCTC in 2026?
questions.explanation: Bhutan is the international destination included in the Bharat Gaurav Mystic Mountain Tour organised by IRCTC. The 14-day journey begins in India and covers several northeastern destinations before crossing into Bhutan via the Phuentsholing border. The tour highlights important cultural and natural attractions in Bhutan, including Thimphu, Punakha, and Paro. This initiative reflects efforts to promote regional tourism and strengthen cross-border connectivity. By offering an all-inclusive travel experience, the program enhances accessibility to Himalayan destinations while encouraging cultural exchange and boosting tourism infrastructure between neighboring countries.

questions.question: Which country received a USD 175 million Special Economic Package announced by India during President Patrick Herminie’s visit?
questions.explanation: Seychelles received a USD 175 million Special Economic Package from India during the visit of President Patrick Herminie to New Delhi. The package covers social housing, e-mobility, health infrastructure, vocational training, defence, and maritime security. In addition, seven Memoranda of Understanding were signed to enhance cooperation in digital transformation, meteorology, governance, and health sectors. The initiative reflects India’s strategic focus on strengthening partnerships in the Indian Ocean region under Vision MAHASAGAR, reinforcing maritime security cooperation and deepening long-standing diplomatic ties between the two nations.

questions.question: Which year was the Dentists Act, repealed during the establishment of the National Dental Commission, originally enacted?
questions.explanation: The Dentists Act served as the foundational legal framework regulating dental education and practice in India for several decades. Enacted in 1948, it governed the functioning of the Dental Council of India until recent reforms replaced it with the National Dental Commission. The repeal of this Act represents a major step toward modernizing the regulatory structure. By moving away from an older system, the government aims to improve transparency, ensure better standards in dental education, and align India's healthcare framework with global best practices.

questions.question: Which region is set to be connected with the mainland under India’s first dedicated commercial seaplane service, approved in 2026?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep is the region targeted for connectivity under India’s first commercial seaplane service, launched by SkyHop Aviation after receiving approval from the DGCA. The project aims to connect five islands with the mainland, significantly improving accessibility to this remote archipelago. Using a modified Twin Otter aircraft, this initiative marks a milestone in domestic aviation innovation. It is further supported by government schemes like UDAN and Viability Gap Funding, ensuring affordability and sustainability. This development is expected to boost tourism, enhance local connectivity, and strengthen regional infrastructure in island territories.

questions.question: Under which Government of India initiative was the NHCX Hackathon organised by the National Health Authority?

options.C: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana Portal

questions.explanation: The NHCX Hackathon was organised by the National Health Authority as part of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), a flagship initiative of the Government of India aimed at creating a comprehensive digital health ecosystem. The hackathon encouraged innovators to develop open-source solutions to streamline and standardise health insurance claims through the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX). It focused on improving interoperability, converting legacy systems to FHIR standards, and structuring clinical data for efficient claims processing. ABDM also includes important digital components such as ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) and the Health Facility Registry, which together aim to enhance digital healthcare infrastructure, improve transparency, and ensure seamless access to health services across India.

questions.question: Who became India’s 94th Grandmaster and the first-ever from the North East region?
questions.explanation: Mayank Chakraborty, a 16-year-old International Master, achieved the milestone of becoming India’s 94th Grandmaster by securing his final norm at the 8th Grandmaster Tournament in Sweden. He delivered an outstanding performance, finishing first with 7 out of 9 points and maintaining an unbeaten streak in crucial rounds. By crossing the required FIDE rating of 2500, he officially earned the Grandmaster title. This achievement is particularly significant as he is the first player from Assam and the North East region to attain this prestigious title, marking a historic moment for Indian chess and inspiring young talents from the region.

questions.question: Where was the 28th Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of Commonwealth countries held?
questions.explanation: The 28th CSPOC Conference, bringing together Speakers and Presiding Officers from over 60 Commonwealth countries, was held in New Delhi. Chaired by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the conference focused on strengthening parliamentary democracy and institutional development. Key sessions addressed the use of artificial intelligence in parliamentary processes, the impact of social media on governance, public engagement strategies, and the well-being of MPs. Hosting the event in India’s capital underscored the country’s role in fostering international parliamentary collaboration and showcased its commitment to democratic practices and legislative innovation.

questions.question: From which country does Sina Ruppenthal, the Guinness World Record holder for lifting and throwing 10 female individuals, belong?
questions.explanation: Sina Ruppenthal is a strongwoman athlete from Germany who set a Guinness World Record by lifting and throwing 10 female individuals in just 37.44 seconds. The record was achieved during a televised event in Munich, highlighting her exceptional physical strength and endurance. She has also excelled in other strongwoman competitions, including obstacle medley events. Her achievement not only showcases her individual capability but also promotes the recognition of women in strength-based sports. This accomplishment has brought international attention and reflects Germany’s growing prominence in such competitive events.

questions.question: Which state launched the ‘Ningol Van Initiative’ on the occasion of the International Day of Forests in 2026?
questions.explanation: Manipur launched the ‘Ningol Van Initiative’ on March 21, 2026, aligning with the International Day of Forests. The initiative focuses on enhancing community participation in forest conservation, with special emphasis on the role of women in protecting biodiversity and promoting sustainable practices. It aims to expand across all 16 districts of the state and supports livelihoods through micro food-processing units under Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, most of which are operated by women. The program also complements efforts to tackle illegal activities like poppy cultivation and promotes reforestation through bamboo and essential oil crops.

questions.question: In which Indian state has the MSME Ministry approved the establishment of two new MSME Technology Centres to promote industrial growth and skill development?
questions.explanation: Himachal Pradesh has received approval from the MSME Ministry for the establishment of two new MSME Technology Centres as part of a national expansion initiative. These centres will be set up at Pandoga in Una district and Parwanoo in Solan district, each with an estimated cost of ₹10 crore. The initiative aims to strengthen industrial infrastructure, enhance skill development, and generate employment opportunities in the state. By providing modern technical support, training facilities, and entrepreneurship assistance, the centres are expected to boost manufacturing activity and attract new investments in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.question: Which organisation partnered with GalaxEye to globally promote and sell its SyncFused OptoSAR satellite imagery?
questions.explanation: Space startup GalaxEye entered into a strategic agreement with NewSpace India Limited, commonly known as NSIL, which functions as the commercial arm of the Indian Space Research Organisation. This partnership makes GalaxEye the first private Indian satellite operator to establish a data reseller collaboration of this kind. Under the agreement, NSIL will globally market and distribute GalaxEye’s SyncFused OptoSAR satellite imagery. The collaboration aims to provide high-precision data solutions for sectors such as agriculture, disaster management, environmental monitoring, and other critical applications, enhancing India’s presence in the global space-based data market.

questions.question: Which institution signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with HCLTech to drive deep tech innovation for Global Capability Centres (GCCs)?
questions.explanation: HCLTech collaborated with IIT Kanpur through a Memorandum of Understanding to promote research-led innovation in deep technology domains for Global Capability Centres (GCCs). The partnership aims to convert cutting-edge academic research into practical pilots and scalable solutions. Key focus areas include artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced engineering, and next-generation technologies. This collaboration positions HCLTech as a strategic enabler for GCCs, helping them accelerate research and development, gain access to specialised expertise, and reduce time-to-market without the need to establish dedicated in-house research facilities.

questions.question: Which country launched the ICP mobile application to help identify venomous snakes and improve public safety?
questions.explanation: Costa Rica launched the ICP mobile application through the Universidad de Costa Rica’s Clodomiro Picado Institute to assist in identifying venomous snakes accurately. The app covers 25 venomous species and also provides information on commonly confused non-venomous species, reducing misidentification risks. It includes visual aids, first aid instructions for snake bites, and geographical logging features to help healthcare providers determine the species involved in incidents. This initiative enhances public awareness, promotes safety, and prevents unnecessary harm to harmless snakes by offering reliable, science-based information accessible on both Android and iOS platforms.

questions.question: Which institution partnered with Indian Highways Management Company Limited to strengthen cyber security and digital forensics in national highway operations?
questions.explanation: Indian Highways Management Company Limited entered into a strategic partnership with the National Forensic Sciences University to enhance cybersecurity and data protection across digital highway operations. The collaboration focuses on areas such as cyber forensics, digital evidence integrity, research, training, and consultancy. With highways increasingly dependent on technologies like Multi-Lane Free Flow tolling and advanced traffic management systems, safeguarding sensitive data has become critical. NFSU’s expertise in cyber investigation and forensic sciences will help strengthen resilience against cyber threats, ensure secure digital operations, and build institutional capacity for managing cyber incidents in national highway infrastructure.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the new Director General of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) until August 31, 2028?
questions.explanation: Senior IPS officer Rakesh Aggarwal, a 1994-batch officer of the Himachal Pradesh cadre, has been appointed as the Director General of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) with tenure approved until his retirement on August 31, 2028. Prior to this, he served as Special Director General in the NIA and was holding additional charge as DG. His appointment, approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, ensures continuity in leadership at India’s premier counter-terrorism body. Aggarwal’s extensive experience in counter-terrorism will strengthen operational efficiency, inter-agency coordination, and the prosecution of terror-related cases nationwide.

questions.question: Which organisation signed an MoU with Aramco Asia India to explore establishing a branch office and expand long-term collaboration?
questions.explanation: Engineers India Limited entered into a strategic MoU with Aramco Asia India to evaluate the possibility of setting up a branch office and deepen cooperation across multiple sectors. This collaboration aims to leverage Aramco’s global strengths alongside India’s expanding energy landscape, covering areas such as petrochemicals, infrastructure, and renewable energy. Through coordinated procurement, joint project execution, and long-term business planning, the partnership is expected to create new opportunities for growth. It also enhances India’s capacity to engage with major international energy players while supporting technological advancements and sustainable sectoral development.

questions.question: In which city was the three-day North Tech Symposium inaugurated by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh in May 2026?
questions.explanation: The North Tech Symposium was inaugurated by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, from May 4 to May 6, 2026. The event was jointly organised by the Northern Command and Central Command of the Indian Army along with the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM). Conducted under the theme “Raksha Triveni Sangam - Where Technology, Industry & Soldiering Converge,” the symposium featured participation from 284 companies, including MSMEs, defence startups, and private technology firms. The primary objective of the event was to identify and integrate indigenous defence technologies, improve maintenance systems, and streamline procurement processes for the Indian armed forces.

questions.question: Which Financial Technology company announced the launch of the Artificial Intelligence-native lending infrastructure suite named Atlas?
questions.explanation: FinBox announced the launch of Atlas, an Artificial Intelligence-native lending infrastructure suite designed to transform the digital lending ecosystem. The platform significantly reduces loan processing time from nearly three weeks to just 24 hours by automating traditional lending operations. Atlas replaces manual workflows with AI-driven agents capable of handling borrower onboarding, document verification, and operational decision-making throughout the credit lifecycle. This innovation aims to improve efficiency, speed, and accuracy in digital lending services. The launch reflects the growing role of Artificial Intelligence in the fintech sector, where automation and data-driven systems are increasingly being used to streamline financial services and customer experiences.

questions.question: Which company launched India's first compliant stablecoin cross-border payments platform in May 2026?
questions.explanation: Xflow launched India’s first compliant stablecoin-based cross-border payments infrastructure on May 14, 2026. The platform allows Indian businesses to accept international payments in stablecoins such as USDC and USDT and convert them into Indian Rupees through authorised banking channels. The system ensures regulatory compliance by conducting stablecoin transactions and off-ramping processes outside India, while only fiat currency enters the country through AD Category I banks. The platform mainly supports MSMEs, SaaS companies, and service exporters facing challenges in global payments. Xflow was co-founded by Anand Balaji and Ashwin Bhatnagar and is backed by investors such as Lightspeed, General Catalyst, and Stripe.

questions.question: When is Indian Navy Day observed?
questions.explanation: Indian Navy Day is observed on December 4 to honour the heroic achievements of the Indian Navy, particularly the success of Operation Trident during the 1971 Indo-Pakistan War. On this day, Indian missile boats launched a decisive attack that neutralised significant Pakistani naval assets, marking a major strategic victory. The 2025 celebrations are being held in Thiruvananthapuram, featuring a large maritime demonstration at Shankhumukham, with the presence of President Droupadi Murmu and Navy Chief Admiral Tripathi. The observance also reflects the Navy’s ethos and commitment, symbolised by its motto “Shaṁ No Varunaḥ,” invoking the protection of the sea god Varuna.

questions.question: On which date is International Migrants Day observed globally?
questions.explanation: International Migrants Day is observed every year on December 18 to recognize and highlight the rights, contributions, and challenges of migrants across the world. The day was proclaimed by the United Nations General Assembly in 2000 to commemorate the adoption of the 1990 International Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families. It draws attention to the cultural, social, and economic contributions made by nearly 272 million international migrants globally, including millions of displaced persons, while also promoting awareness about migration-related issues and inclusive development.

questions.question: Which country has taken the final step to restart the world’s largest nuclear power plant after a regional vote?
questions.explanation: Japan has moved forward with the final approval required to restart the world’s largest nuclear power plant, marking a significant development in its energy policy. This decision comes nearly 15 years after the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, which had a profound impact on nuclear operations across the country. The plant in question, Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, is located in Niigata Prefecture and will be operated by Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO). The restart reflects Japan’s cautious but determined approach toward reviving nuclear energy while addressing safety concerns rooted in past experiences.

questions.question: What is India’s global ranking in the Henley Passport Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India is placed at the 75th position in the Henley Passport Index 2026, which evaluates passport strength based on the number of destinations accessible without a prior visa. Indian passport holders currently have visa-free, visa-on-arrival, or e-visa access to 55 destinations, reflecting a modest improvement compared to the previous year. Despite this progress, significant travel restrictions remain for regions such as Europe and North America. The ranking highlights disparities in global mobility, especially within South Asia, and underscores the influence of diplomatic relations, stability, and international agreements on travel freedom.

questions.question: Which city declared a waterborne disease outbreak an epidemic after multiple deaths in the Bhagirathpura area?
questions.explanation: The declaration of a waterborne disease outbreak as an epidemic reflects a serious public health emergency requiring immediate intervention. Indore took this step following reported fatalities in the Bhagirathpura area, prompting emergency containment and response measures. Special teams from both central and state agencies were deployed to identify the source of contamination, with experts from the National Centre for Disease Control and ICMR-NIRBI involved in the investigation. Authorities are examining whether pipeline leaks led to single or multiple contamination points, highlighting the importance of infrastructure safety and coordinated public health governance in urban areas.

questions.question: In which city was the India Internet Governance Forum (IIGF) 2025 held?
questions.explanation: The fifth edition of the India Internet Governance Forum (IIGF) 2025 was held in New Delhi from 27–28 November. The event focused on “Advancing Internet Governance for an Inclusive and Sustainable Viksit Bharat” and included four major panels and twelve workshops addressing key aspects of digital governance. Day 1 took place at the India Habitat Centre, while Day 2 was held at the India International Centre. The forum was inaugurated by Union Minister of State Jitin Prasada, highlighting the importance of internet policy, digital inclusion, and governance in shaping India’s technological and socio-economic landscape.

questions.question: In which city did the police trace over 1,300 missing persons under “Operation Milap”?
questions.explanation: Under “Operation Milap,” the Delhi police successfully traced 1,303 missing persons through sustained and coordinated efforts. The initiative involved extensive use of modern technology, close coordination across multiple districts, and systematic follow-ups on long-pending missing cases. These recoveries reflect improved policing strategies, stronger inter-agency cooperation, and a focused commitment to reuniting missing individuals with their families. The operation highlights the effectiveness of organised law enforcement initiatives in addressing sensitive social issues and strengthening public trust in the policing system in the national capital.

questions.question: In which city was India’s first comprehensive Urban Testbed and Aerosol Observatory inaugurated?
questions.explanation: India’s first comprehensive Urban Testbed and Aerosol Observatory was inaugurated in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, by the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES). The project was established by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) along with the Centre for Atmospheric Science Research and Innovation (CASRI). Equipped with advanced instruments, weather stations, and X-band radars, the observatory is designed to monitor atmospheric conditions, aerosols, rainfall patterns, and thermodynamic changes. The initiative aims to improve short-term weather forecasting, study the effects of aerosols on climate change, and strengthen India’s climate and weather research capabilities under the broader vision of Mission Mausam.

questions.question: Where was the 9th Narco Coordination Centre (NCORD) meeting chaired by the Home Minister held?
questions.explanation: The 9th meeting of the Narco Coordination Centre (NCORD) was chaired by the Union Home Minister as part of India’s ongoing efforts to strengthen drug control and inter-agency coordination. NCORD functions as the primary platform for cooperation between central and state agencies in combating drug trafficking and abuse. The meeting took place in New Delhi, highlighting the capital’s role as the administrative and decision-making hub of the country. Such high-level meetings are typically organized there to ensure effective policy discussion, coordination, and implementation under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.question: What percentage of all diseases in India is accounted for by cardiovascular diseases according to the NSO Survey 2025?
questions.explanation: Cardiovascular diseases have emerged as a major health concern in India, showing a significant increase over recent years. According to the NSO Survey 2025, these diseases now account for 25.6% of all reported illnesses, making them the leading category among various health conditions. This rise reflects changing lifestyles, increased stress levels, and other risk factors such as poor diet and lack of physical activity. Notably, the impact is not limited to older populations, as younger age groups are also increasingly affected. The data highlights the urgent need for improved public health strategies, awareness campaigns, and preventive healthcare measures to address this growing burden.

questions.question: Who became the 2025 FIDE World Cup Champion after a dramatic tiebreak victory in Goa?
questions.explanation: Javokhir Sindarov secured the 2025 FIDE World Cup title after an intense final against Wei Yi, where both classical games ended in draws, leading to rapid tiebreaks. Sindarov displayed exceptional composure and tactical sharpness, ultimately winning the tiebreaks 1½–½. His achievement is historic, as he became the youngest player to claim the World Cup title. The tournament, featuring 206 participants, included several dramatic encounters, major upsets, and strong performances from elite players. Sindarov’s victory, celebrated with his family and supporters, marks a defining milestone in his rapidly rising chess career.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the head coach of the Sri Lanka Men’s national cricket team starting from April 15, 2026?
questions.explanation: Gary Kirsten, a former South African international cricketer and experienced coach, has been appointed as the head coach of the Sri Lanka Men’s national cricket team beginning on April 15, 2026, for a two-year term ending on April 14, 2028. He is widely respected for his calm leadership style and strong emphasis on team discipline and mental conditioning. Kirsten previously achieved major coaching success with India, guiding the team to victory in the 2011 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup and helping them reach the No.1 Test ranking. He also coached South Africa to the No.1 ranking across all three formats in 2013, making him one of cricket’s most accomplished coaches.

questions.question: Which state government signed an MoU with the National Dairy Development Board in March 2026 to boost its dairy sector?
questions.explanation: The Himachal Pradesh government signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Dairy Development Board on March 16, 2026, to strengthen its dairy sector. The agreement focuses on enhancing milk processing capacity, improving infrastructure, and supporting farmers by providing better facilities. A key component of this initiative is the development of the Dagwar dairy project, which aims to become a major processing hub. Additionally, the promotion of dairy products under the ‘HIM’ brand is expected to boost the state’s market presence and generate employment opportunities in the dairy industry.

questions.question: Which Indian state’s living root bridges have been nominated for UNESCO World Heritage evaluation for the 2026–27 cycle?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya’s living root bridges have been nominated for UNESCO World Heritage status, recognising their outstanding cultural and ecological significance. These bridges are naturally grown from the aerial roots of rubber fig trees and have been carefully shaped over generations by the Khasi and Jaintia communities. They represent a remarkable example of sustainable bioengineering, showcasing a deep-rooted harmony between humans and nature. The nomination highlights centuries-old indigenous knowledge systems and emphasises the bridges’ resilience, functionality, and role as living symbols of sustainability and environmental stewardship on a global platform.

questions.question: Which Indian state launched a financial assistance scheme providing ₹1,500 per month to Udasin Bhakats?
questions.explanation: Assam launched a financial assistance scheme to support Udasin Bhakats, offering ₹1,500 per month to celibate Vaishnavite monks. The scheme applies to bhakats associated with Udasin Satras, which are key monastic centres of Assam’s Vaishnavite tradition. Announced in the state budget, the initiative aims to provide financial security to around 620 eligible monks across different districts of Assam. The government has also kept provisions to include any left-out eligible Udasin Bhakats, reflecting Assam’s commitment to preserving its cultural and religious heritage while extending welfare support.

questions.question: From which date will the new nomination rules under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 come into effect?
questions.explanation: The Central Government has announced that the updated nomination rules under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 will take effect from November 1, 2025. These reforms aim to make the nomination process for deposits, lockers, and safe custody articles more flexible and transparent. Customers can now nominate up to four individuals simultaneously or successively, ensuring clearer entitlement and quicker settlement in case of the depositor’s death. The changes are part of broader initiatives to strengthen governance, depositor protection, and efficiency in India’s banking system, aligning with modern financial practices and customer convenience.

questions.question: Which country is partnering with India to establish the National Centre of Excellence in Aeronautics and Defence at Kanpur under the PM-SETU scheme?
questions.explanation: France is collaborating with India to establish the National Centre of Excellence in Aeronautics and Defence at Kanpur under the PM-SETU scheme. The initiative was announced during the India–France Year of Innovation, reflecting deepening bilateral cooperation in advanced technologies, defence manufacturing, and skill development. The Centre will focus on aeronautics, maintenance and overhaul services, airport operations, and space-related training. This partnership builds upon the India–France Strategic Partnership and follows a 2025 Memorandum of Understanding in vocational education and training, aiming to create globally competitive aviation professionals aligned with international standards.

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the 18th Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman & Nicobar Command (CINCAN) in June 2025?

options.D: Lt Gen M V Suchindra Kumar

questions.explanation: Lt Gen Dinesh Singh Rana took over as the 18th Commander-in-Chief of the Andaman & Nicobar Command (CINCAN) on June 1, 2025. This position is significant as it leads India's only tri-services command, overseeing strategic operations in the Indian Ocean Region. With a career spanning several key military and academic appointments, Lt Gen Rana brings vast operational experience, having commanded an infantry brigade, division, and the Gajraj Corps. Prior to this, he served as the Director General of the Defence Intelligence Agency. His education and international exposure further strengthen India’s joint defence leadership in a geopolitically critical area.

questions.question: Which company received RBI in-principle approval to join Centralised Payment Systems (RTGS/NEFT)?
questions.explanation: Transcorp received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India to join the Centralised Payment Systems, including RTGS and NEFT. This approval allows the company to obtain its own IFSC code and maintain a bank account directly with the RBI, significantly strengthening its operational framework. The move enhances its digital payment ecosystem, improves compliance standards, and boosts operational efficiency. By gaining direct access to centralized payment infrastructure, the company is better positioned for technology-driven expansion and independent growth. It is a public limited company and is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

questions.question: Which country identified the 11th known lunar mineral, Cerium-Magnesium Changesite, in April 2026?
questions.explanation: China identified a new lunar mineral named Cerium-Magnesium Changesite on April 23, 2026, marking the 11th known mineral discovered from the Moon. This mineral was found within a lunar meteorite that had fallen within China’s borders, making it a significant scientific achievement. The mineral exhibits unique fluorescent properties and contains specific ratios of rare earth elements, magnesium, and iron. Its discovery holds potential for applications in advanced technologies such as next-generation LED materials and energy-efficient electronics. This breakthrough also highlights China’s growing capabilities in space exploration and extraterrestrial geological research.

questions.question: Which country has taken the final step to restart the world’s largest nuclear power plant after a regional vote?
questions.explanation: Japan has moved forward with the final approval required to restart the world’s largest nuclear power plant, marking a significant development in its energy policy. This decision comes nearly 15 years after the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, which had a profound impact on nuclear operations across the country. The plant in question, Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, is located in Niigata Prefecture and will be operated by Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO). The restart reflects Japan’s cautious but determined approach toward reviving nuclear energy while addressing safety concerns rooted in past experiences.

questions.question: Where was the Putin-Trump summit of August 2025 held?
questions.explanation: The much-anticipated summit between Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump was held at the Elmendorf-Richardson military base in Anchorage, Alaska. While the meeting lasted three hours, it ended without a peace deal on the Ukraine conflict. Both leaders, however, described the dialogue as constructive and expressed optimism for continued engagement. The choice of Alaska carried symbolic significance, being geographically positioned between the U.S. and Russia, underscoring its role as a neutral yet strategic venue. Although no concrete agreement emerged, the summit marked an important diplomatic interaction with potential implications for future negotiations.

questions.question: Which country has partnered with India for the restoration of the Prambanan Temple complex?
questions.explanation: India has collaborated with Indonesia to restore the historic 9th-century Prambanan Temple complex located in Yogyakarta. This initiative highlights strong cultural and diplomatic ties between the two nations. The restoration will be carried out using the anastylosis method to preserve authenticity, with support from the Archaeological Survey of India. The project also faces challenges such as identifying and assembling thousands of scattered stone blocks. This collaboration reflects India’s “Act East” policy and emphasises shared civilizational heritage, as Prambanan is a UNESCO World Heritage Site dedicated to the Hindu Trimurti.

questions.question: Which country signed a new MoU with India to strengthen cooperation in forests, wildlife, biodiversity conservation, and climate change?
questions.explanation: Nepal signed a new Memorandum of Understanding with India to enhance bilateral cooperation in forests, wildlife protection, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation. The agreement focuses on restoring transboundary wildlife corridors, protecting key species such as tigers, elephants, rhinoceroses, and snow leopards, and strengthening protected area management. It also emphasises combating wildlife crime, improving coordination between enforcement agencies, and promoting capacity building for frontline forest staff. Given the shared ecosystems and migratory wildlife habitats across borders, the partnership supports integrated conservation strategies and climate resilience efforts in the Himalayan and adjoining landscapes.

questions.question: What is the official duration of the mandated version of Vande Mataram at key functions as per the Ministry of Home Affairs protocol?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Home Affairs issued a protocol regarding the proper rendition of Vande Mataram during official events. It directed that when performed along with Jana Gana Mana, all six stanzas of Vande Mataram must be sung first. The official version has a prescribed duration of 3 minutes and 10 seconds and is mandated at key government functions. During its rendition, the audience is required to stand in attention as a mark of respect, except in specific contexts such as film screenings. Educational institutions are also encouraged to begin the day with community singing.

questions.question: Which city was ranked the cleanest in India in October 2025, according to CREA’s Air Quality Snapshot?
questions.explanation: As per the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) Air Quality Snapshot for October 2025, Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, recorded the cleanest air in India with an average PM2.5 concentration of just 10 μg/m³. In contrast, Dharuhera in Haryana topped the list of polluted cities with a PM2.5 level of 123 μg/m³, while other highly polluted cities included Ghaziabad, Delhi, and Noida. The report emphasized the need for consistent and year-round air quality management rather than short-term, seasonal interventions such as the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

questions.question: What type of initiative is the Gujarat Karmayogi Swasthya Suraksha Yojana?
questions.explanation: The Gujarat Karmayogi Swasthya Suraksha Yojana is a dedicated healthcare scheme launched by the Government of Gujarat to offer cashless medical treatment to eligible groups such as All India Services officers, state government employees, and pensioners. The scheme provides coverage of up to ₹10 lakh per family annually through a “G” category PMJAY card. It is implemented by the State Health Agency (SHA), which manages beneficiary data and ensures the proper distribution of benefits. By focusing on public servants and their families, the initiative strengthens healthcare accessibility and reduces financial stress related to medical expenses.

questions.question: Where was the MANTHAN 2025 national conference inaugurated by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh?
questions.explanation: The MANTHAN 2025 national conference was inaugurated in New Delhi by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Organised by the Directorate General of Defence Estates, the two day conference focused on the theme Strategic Roadmap to Aatmanirbhar Bharat @2047. The event highlighted the Defence Estates Department’s role in managing defence land and emphasised the importance of long term planning for strengthening India’s self reliance in the defence sector. Hosting the conference in the national capital provided a platform for policy makers, defence officials, and experts to collaborate on strategies that align with the country’s vision for 2047.

questions.question: In which city is Gulfood 2026 being held, where India has made its historic debut as a Partner Country?
questions.explanation: Gulfood 2026 is being hosted in Dubai, marking a significant milestone for India as it participates as a Partner Country for the first time in the event’s 31-year history. The exhibition is taking place across two major venues—the Dubai World Trade Centre and the Dubai Exhibition Centre at Expo City Dubai. India’s participation, led by APEDA, showcases the country’s growing agri-food export strength through a large and diverse pavilion featuring exhibitors from across India. This engagement highlights deepening India–UAE trade relations and reinforces Dubai’s role as a global hub for food, beverage, and agri-trade connectivity.

questions.question: In which city was the ‘Veer Sahara’ digital platform developed by students?
questions.explanation: The ‘Veer Sahara’ platform was developed by two Grade 11 students from Jayshree Periwal International School in Jaipur. The initiative demonstrates how young innovators can leverage technology to solve real-world problems, particularly for the defence community. The platform simplifies access to government welfare schemes by offering features such as AI-assisted interfaces, voice guidance, and bilingual support. Jaipur, known for its growing educational and technological initiatives, serves as the origin of this impactful project, highlighting the city’s contribution to innovation and social welfare through student-led efforts.

questions.question: Who became the first fast bowler to reach 200 wickets in the history of the Indian Premier League (IPL)?
questions.explanation: Bhuvneshwar Kumar achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first fast bowler to take 200 wickets in the Indian Premier League. He reached this landmark during a match between the Royal Challengers Bengaluru and the Chennai Super Kings by dismissing Ayush Mhatre. Traditionally, spinners have dominated the top wicket-taking charts in the IPL, making this achievement particularly notable for a pace bowler. Bhuvneshwar has been a consistent performer since his debut in 2011 and is also known for winning back-to-back Purple Caps in 2016 and 2017, highlighting his excellence in the tournament.

questions.question: In which state is the Khavda Solar Energy Project, where NTPC Green commissioned 49 MW in August 2025, located?
questions.explanation: The Khavda Solar Energy Project is situated in Bhuj, Gujarat, where NTPC Green Energy Ltd has begun commercial supply of 49 MW as part of its broader 300 MW solar initiative. Earlier phases of 142.2 MW and 32.8 MW were also made operational in June 2025, highlighting steady progress in the project’s rollout. Gujarat has been a leading state in India’s renewable energy sector due to its favorable geography and policy support. This development underlines NTPC Green’s commitment to expanding its clean energy portfolio, aligning with India’s long-term renewable energy and sustainability goals.

questions.question: Which country launched the ICP mobile application to help identify venomous snakes and improve public safety?
questions.explanation: Costa Rica launched the ICP mobile application through the Universidad de Costa Rica’s Clodomiro Picado Institute to assist in identifying venomous snakes accurately. The app covers 25 venomous species and also provides information on commonly confused non-venomous species, reducing misidentification risks. It includes visual aids, first aid instructions for snake bites, and geographical logging features to help healthcare providers determine the species involved in incidents. This initiative enhances public awareness, promotes safety, and prevents unnecessary harm to harmless snakes by offering reliable, science-based information accessible on both Android and iOS platforms.

questions.question: Which institution conducted India’s first dedicated clinical trial of an advanced brain stent under the GRASSROOT trial?
questions.explanation: AIIMS Delhi played a pioneering role by conducting India’s first dedicated clinical trial of an advanced brain stent under the GRASSROOT trial. The trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of the indigenously developed Supernova stent for treating severe strokes, particularly large vessel occlusion cases. Conducted across multiple medical centres, the study produced high-quality clinical evidence that led to CDSCO approval based solely on domestic data. This achievement strengthened India’s medical research ecosystem, reduced reliance on foreign trials, and supported national initiatives such as Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat in the medical devices sector.

questions.question: Which company launched a cloud-based virtual desktop service that transforms any TV into a personal computer?
questions.explanation: Reliance Jio has introduced JioPC, an innovative cloud-based virtual desktop service that enables any television to function as a personal computer. This service works through the Jio Set-Top Box and operates without the need for traditional hardware like CPUs. Running on Ubuntu, JioPC provides access to essential tools such as LibreOffice, browser-based Microsoft Office, and Adobe Express. Users can connect a keyboard and mouse to their TV and perform tasks like browsing, editing documents, and learning online. With flexible pricing options and no need for bulky hardware, JioPC is a cost-effective solution aimed at students, professionals, and households seeking affordable digital access.
